children.title: Generic Cutting-Plane Framework
children.top_down_role: Navigation through evolving relaxations, separation, cut admission, reoptimization, and completion status without procedural payload.

children.title: Relaxation Sequences
children.top_down_role: Successive strengthened relaxations used by cutting-plane methods.

assumptions_latex: F\neq\varnothing
F\subseteq R_0\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n
c\in\mathbb{R}^n
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\subseteq R_{k+1}\subseteq R_k\quad\text{and}\quad \inf_{x\in R_k}c^\top x\leq \inf_{x\in R_{k+1}}c^\top x\leq \inf_{x\in F}c^\top x.

notation.meaning: feasible set of the original minimization problem

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested outer relaxations for a minimization cutting-plane method.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be the nonempty feasible set of a minimization problem and let \(R_0\supseteq F\) be an initial relaxation. At iteration \(k\), admit a finite family \(H_k\) of inequalities valid for every point of \(F\), and define \[R_{k+1}=R_k\cap\bigcap_{h\in H_k}\{x:h(x)\leq 0\}.\] Then \(F\subseteq R_{k+1}\subseteq R_k\). Consequently, for every objective vector \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), the relaxation bounds are monotone: \[\inf_{x\in R_k}c^\top x\leq\inf_{x\in R_{k+1}}c^\top x\leq\inf_{x\in F}c^\top x.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding only valid cuts produces nested relaxations whose lower bounds for a minimization problem improve monotonically without excluding feasible solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Sequences

children.title: Separation-Oracle Interface
children.top_down_role: Interfaces connecting candidate solutions to violated-inequality discovery.

assumptions_latex: F\subseteq R\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n
\bar x\in R
\varepsilon\geq 0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal S(\bar x,\varepsilon)=\mathrm{NONE}\quad\text{or}\quad (a,\beta)\text{ with }a^\top x\leq\beta\ \forall x\in F\text{ and }a^\top\bar x>\beta+\varepsilon.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contract for exact or tolerance-based separation at a relaxation solution.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a feasible set \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), a current relaxation \(R\supseteq F\), a candidate \(\bar x\in R\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\), a separation oracle \(\mathcal S\) returns either \(\mathrm{NONE}\) or a pair \((a,\beta)\). A returned pair must satisfy \[a^\top x\leq\beta\quad\text{for every }x\in F,\qquad a^\top\bar x>\beta+\varepsilon.\] The response \(\mathrm{NONE}\) asserts that no inequality in the oracle's declared cut family violates \(\bar x\) by more than \(\varepsilon\). The caller may admit returned inequalities without removing any point of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The oracle either returns a valid inequality violated by the candidate beyond tolerance or reports exhaustion of its declared cut family.
knowledge_statements.title: Separation-Oracle Interface

children.title: Cut Admission Decisions
children.top_down_role: Criteria governing whether generated inequalities enter the evolving relaxation.

assumptions_latex: F\subseteq R_k
C_k\text{ is a finite pool of inequalities valid for }F
\bar x_k\in R_k
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A_k\subseteq C_k\quad\text{and}\quad R_{k+1}=R_k\cap\bigcap_{(a,\beta)\in A_k}\{x:a^\top x\leq\beta\}\supseteq F.

notation.meaning: candidate cut pool at iteration k
admitted subset of the cut pool
violation score at the current point

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity-preserving admission, with selection policy left algorithm-dependent.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), let \(C_k\) be a finite pool of inequalities \(a^\top x\leq\beta\) valid for every \(x\in F\), and define their violations by \(v_k(a,\beta)=a^\top\bar x_k-\beta\). An admissible decision selects a subset \(A_k\subseteq C_k\), possibly subject to prescribed violation, efficacy, parallelism, or pool-size thresholds. Every selected row must retain its validity for \(F\). The strengthened relaxation is \[R_{k+1}=R_k\cap\bigcap_{(a,\beta)\in A_k}\{x:a^\top x\leq\beta\},\] so necessarily \(F\subseteq R_{k+1}\subseteq R_k\). Rejecting a valid candidate affects strengthening, not correctness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Admission selects a manageable subset of valid candidate cuts; any selection preserves feasibility containment, while selection quality controls strengthening and computational cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut Admission Decisions

children.title: Relaxation Reoptimization
children.top_down_role: Resolution of the relaxation after accepted cuts alter its row set.

F\subseteq R_{k+1}\subseteq R_k
x_k\in\arg\min_{x\in R_k}c^\top x
\arg\min_{x\in R_{k+1}}c^\top x\neq\varnothing
c\in\mathbb{R}^n
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_{k+1}\in\arg\min_{x\in R_{k+1}}c^\top x\quad\text{and}\quad c^\top x_{k+1}\geq c^\top x_k.

notation.meaning: nonempty feasible set of the original problem
optimal relaxation solution at iteration k
relaxation objective value at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact reoptimization of a nonempty strengthened minimization relaxation.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, let \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and suppose \(x_k\in\arg\min\{c^\top x:x\in R_k\}\). If admitted valid cuts define \(F\subseteq R_{k+1}\subseteq R_k\) and the minimum over \(R_{k+1}\) is attained, reoptimization computes \[x_{k+1}\in\arg\min\{c^\top x:x\in R_{k+1}\},\qquad z_{k+1}=c^\top x_{k+1}.\] It returns \((x_{k+1},z_{k+1})\) to the separation stage. Because the feasible domain has contracted, \(z_{k+1}\geq z_k=c^\top x_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After valid cuts strengthen a nonempty relaxation, exact reoptimization returns a new relaxation optimum whose minimization bound cannot be lower than the preceding bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Reoptimization

children.title: Warm-Start Transfer
children.top_down_role: Reuse of solver state across cut admission events.

assumptions_latex: R_{k+1}=R_k\cap\{x:A^+x\leq b^+\}
S_k\text{ represents a valid solver state for }R_k
F\subseteq R_{k+1}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Solve}(R_{k+1},T(S_k,A^+,b^+))\text{ must return the same certified status and optimum as a cold solve of }R_{k+1}.

notation.meaning: solver state for the old relaxation
newly admitted rows and right-hand sides

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness requirement for transferring solver state after row addition.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_k\) be a valid internal state for solving relaxation \(R_k\), and let new rows define \(R_{k+1}=R_k\cap\{x:A^+x\leq b^+\}\). A warm-start transfer \(T\) maps \((S_k,A^+,b^+)\) to an initial state for reoptimizing \(R_{k+1}\). The transfer is correct only if subsequent optimization from \(T(S_k,A^+,b^+)\) returns the same certified feasibility status and, when finite, the same optimum as a cold solve of \(R_{k+1}\). Reusing a basis, incumbent, factorization, or iterate may change computational work but must not change the mathematical relaxation or its certified answer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transferred solver state may accelerate reoptimization, but it must yield the same certified result as solving the strengthened relaxation from scratch.
knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Start Transfer

children.title: Admission Failure Recovery
children.top_down_role: Handling of rejected, unstable, or incompatible candidate rows.

assumptions_latex: F\subseteq R_k
A_k\text{ contains only inequalities valid for }F
\operatorname{Solve}(R_k\cap A_k,S_k)\text{ fails without a valid certificate}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Solve}(R_k\cap A_k,S_{\mathrm{cold}})\text{ is attempted before any mathematical infeasibility conclusion is accepted}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conservative recovery from numerical or state-transfer failure during cut admission.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If reoptimization after admitting \(A_k\) fails without a valid optimality or infeasibility certificate, recovery first discards the transferred solver state and cold-solves the unchanged relaxation \(R_k\cap A_k\). If failure persists, the algorithm may partition \(A_k\), identify malformed or numerically unacceptable rows, and retry with a subset \(A'_k\subseteq A_k\). Every retained row must remain valid for \(F\), and every removed row is returned to the pool or logged as rejected. No failure status alone may be interpreted as mathematical infeasibility; such a conclusion requires a valid infeasibility certificate for a relaxation containing \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On an uncertified admission failure, retry from a fresh state and isolate problematic rows; never treat a solver failure alone as infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Admission Failure Recovery

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed cold restart, cut-pool partitioning, malformed-row isolation, and retry policy is solver-specific and is not reliably supported by the cited general cutting-plane section. The expression denoting intersection with a set of inequalities is also not formally defined in the assumptions. A solver-specific source is needed before selecting the exact recovery formulation.

children.top_down_role: Exact completion, separation exhaustion, stalled progress, and resource-limited stopping.

children.title: Exact Completion Regimes
children.top_down_role: Termination settings associated with an exact cutting-plane outcome.

assumptions_latex: F\neq\varnothing
F\subseteq R_k\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n
c\in\mathbb{R}^n
x_k\in\arg\min_{x\in R_k}c^\top x
x_k\in F
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_k\in\arg\min_{x\in F}c^\top x\quad\text{and}\quad \min_{x\in R_k}c^\top x=\min_{x\in F}c^\top x.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact completion through a relaxation optimum that is feasible for the original problem, or through matching certified primal and lower bounds.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, let \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(R_k\supseteq F\) be an outer relaxation. If reoptimization returns \(x_k\in\arg\min\{c^\top x:x\in R_k\}\) and an exact feasibility test establishes \(x_k\in F\), then \(x_k\) is globally optimal over \(F\), with \[\min_{x\in R_k}c^\top x=c^\top x_k=\min_{x\in F}c^\top x.\] More generally, exact completion is certified when a valid lower bound equals the objective value of a feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxation optimum that is feasible for the original minimization problem, or equality between a valid lower bound and a feasible incumbent value, certifies exact completion.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Completion Regimes

children.title: Separation Exhaustion
children.top_down_role: Stopping after available separation systems produce no further useful cuts.

assumptions_latex: F\subseteq R_k
x_k\in R_k
\mathcal H\text{ is the oracle's declared family of valid inequalities}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_{(a,\beta)\in\mathcal H}(a^\top x_k-\beta)\leq\varepsilon.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exhaustion is relative to a declared cut family and tolerance.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal H\) be the separation oracle's declared family of inequalities \(a^\top x\leq\beta\), each valid for \(F\), and let \(\varepsilon\geq0\). Separation is exhausted at \(x_k\) precisely when the oracle certifies \[a^\top x_k-\beta\leq\varepsilon\quad\text{for every }(a,\beta)\in\mathcal H.\] Equivalently, \(\sup_{(a,\beta)\in\mathcal H}(a^\top x_k-\beta)\leq\varepsilon\). This condition certifies membership only in the \(\varepsilon\)-relaxation induced by \(\mathcal H\); it certifies \(x_k\in F\) only when \(\mathcal H\) completely describes \(F\) and \(\varepsilon=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separation is exhausted when no inequality in the declared family is violated beyond tolerance; this need not certify original feasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Separation Exhaustion

children.title: Progress-Stall Termination
children.top_down_role: Termination triggered by insufficient improvement across cutting rounds.

assumptions_latex: z_k=\inf_{x\in R_k}c^\top x
\delta_z,\delta_v\geq0
m\in\mathbb{N}_{+}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max_{j=k-m+1,\ldots,k}|z_j-z_{j-1}|\leq\delta_z\quad\text{and}\quad \max_{j=k-m+1,\ldots,k}v_j\leq\delta_v.

notation.meaning: relaxation objective value at iteration k
largest detected cut violation at iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational, non-exact termination based on a finite progress window.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix tolerances \(\delta_z,\delta_v\geq0\) and a window length \(m\in\mathbb{N}_{+}\). For relaxation values \(z_j\) and largest detected violations \(v_j\), progress-stall termination at iteration \(k\geq m\) occurs when \[\max_{j=k-m+1,\ldots,k}|z_j-z_{j-1}|\leq\delta_z\quad\text{and}\quad\max_{j=k-m+1,\ldots,k}v_j\leq\delta_v.\] The algorithm returns the current relaxation bound, incumbent, and residual statistics with a stall status. Unless an independent exact-completion certificate is also present, this rule is computational termination only and does not certify global optimality or separation exhaustion outside the tested cut families.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Terminate after a prescribed window with negligible bound change and detected violation, reporting stall rather than claiming exact optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Progress-Stall Termination

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record gives a coherent operational stall condition and correctly avoids claiming exactness, but the exact two-threshold, finite-window formula is an algorithm-specific policy not established by the cited general cutting-plane section. A source supporting this termination rule, or a documented algorithm specification, is required.

children.title: Resource-Limited Termination
children.top_down_role: Stopping policies governed by time, iteration, memory, or row budgets.

assumptions_latex: B\in(0,\infty)
r_k\text{ is cumulative resource consumption}
r_k\geq B
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{termination returns the best certified bound and incumbent available, with status }\mathrm{RESOURCE\_LIMIT}.

notation.meaning: cumulative resource consumption through iteration k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Non-exact termination caused by an iteration, time, memory, or oracle budget.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a finite resource budget \(B>0\) and a nondecreasing consumption measure \(r_k\), such as elapsed time, iterations, admitted rows, oracle calls, or memory. Resource-limited termination occurs at the first iteration \(k\) satisfying \(r_k\geq B\). The algorithm returns the best certified relaxation bound \(L_k\), the best feasible incumbent value \(U_k\) when available, and status \(\mathrm{RESOURCE\_LIMIT}\). For minimization, \(L_k\leq\inf_{x\in F}c^\top x\leq U_k\). Budget exhaustion alone certifies neither exact optimality nor infeasibility; any stronger conclusion must be supported by a separate certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a fixed computational budget is exhausted, return certified bounds and any incumbent with a resource-limit status, without asserting exact completion.
knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Limited Termination

children.title: A Priori Constraint Addition
children.top_down_role: Static strengthening before iterative separation begins.

I_0\subseteq I
g_i(x)\leq0\text{ is valid for every }x\in F
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\subseteq R_0=\{x\in X:g_i(x)\leq0\ \forall i\in I_0\}\subseteq X.

notation.meaning: full index set of model constraints

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static valid strengthening performed before iterative separation.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the full feasible set be \(F=\{x\in X:g_i(x)\leq0\text{ for every }i\in I\}\). A priori constraint addition chooses an index subset \(I_0\subseteq I\), or another finite family of inequalities valid for \(F\), before the first relaxation is optimized. The initial relaxation is \[R_0=\{x\in X:g_i(x)\leq0\text{ for every }i\in I_0\}.\] Thus \(F\subseteq R_0\subseteq X\). These rows remain part of the static initial model; constraints in \(I\setminus I_0\) may subsequently be enforced by delayed generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Install a selected set of valid constraints before optimization, creating a stronger initial relaxation while leaving remaining constraints available for delayed enforcement.
knowledge_statements.title: A Priori Constraint Addition

children.top_down_role: Dynamic enforcement of initially omitted model constraints.

I_0\subseteq I
\varepsilon\geq0

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dynamic generation of omitted constraints from a finite or enumerable model family.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x\in X:g_i(x)\leq0\text{ for every }i\in I\}\), choose \(I_0\subseteq I\), fix \(\varepsilon\geq0\), and set \(R_0=\{x\in X:g_i(x)\leq0\text{ for every }i\in I_0\}\). At iteration \(k\), solve over \(R_k\) to obtain \(x_k\), identify a finite set \(V_k\subseteq I\setminus I_k\) such that \(g_i(x_k)>\varepsilon\) for every \(i\in V_k\), and update \[I_{k+1}=I_k\cup V_k,\qquad R_{k+1}=\{x\in X:g_i(x)\leq0\text{ for every }i\in I_{k+1}\}.\] Then \(F\subseteq R_{k+1}\subseteq R_k\). Stop when an exhaustive check finds no omitted constraint violated beyond \(\varepsilon\), or when another declared termination regime applies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve a restricted model, add omitted constraints violated beyond a fixed tolerance, and repeat until exhaustive separation or another declared stopping rule terminates the process.
knowledge_statements.title: Delayed Constraint Generation

children.title: Automatic Reformulation by Cuts
children.top_down_role: Progressive construction of stronger formulations through generated inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Automatic Reformulation by Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative outer approximation of an implicitly constrained mixed-integer feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), and let \(F=\{x\in X:x_i\in\mathbb{Z}\ (i\in I),\ g_t(x)\leq0\ (t\in T)\}\). Initialize a finite relaxation \(R_0\supseteq F\). At iteration \(k\), solve \(\min\{c^\top x:x\in R_k\}\) and obtain \(x^k\). If a separation oracle finds a valid inequality \(a^\top x\leq\beta\) for \(F\) with \(a^\top x^k>\beta\), set \(R_{k+1}=R_k\cap\{x:a^\top x\leq\beta\}\); otherwise return \(x^k\). Thus every reformulation remains a relaxation of \(F\) and excludes the separated optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve a finite relaxation, separate its optimizer, and append a valid violated inequality; stop when the oracle finds no violation.
assumptions_latex: \(R_0\supseteq F\) and each generated inequality is valid for \(F\).
Each restricted master problem is solved to the required exactness.
The separation oracle either returns a violated valid inequality or certifies none exists in its family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\subseteq R_{k+1}\subseteq R_k\quad\text{and}\quad x^k\notin R_{k+1}\text{ whenever a cut is generated}.\)

notation.meaning: Possibly large or implicit constraint index set.

children.title: Row-Oriented Generation

knowledge_statements.title: Row-Oriented Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Delayed generation in which each oracle response is materialized as a linear row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(F=\{x\in X:a_t^\top x\leq b_t\text{ for every }t\in T\}\), where \(T\) may be too large to enumerate. Choose finite \(T_0\subseteq T\). At iteration \(k\), solve the master problem over \(F_k=\{x\in X:a_t^\top x\leq b_t\ (t\in T_k)\}\). Given its optimizer \(x^k\), select a finite set \(V_k\subseteq\{t\in T:a_t^\top x^k>b_t\}\), append the corresponding coefficient rows, and set \(T_{k+1}=T_k\cup V_k\). Stop when no violated indexed row is returned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve using a subset of rows, append explicit violated rows from the indexed family, and stop when separation returns none.
assumptions_latex: \(T_0\subseteq T\) is finite.
The row oracle searches only inequalities belonging to the stated indexed family.
Each selected set \(V_k\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\subseteq F_{k+1}\subseteq F_k\), with \(x^k\notin F_{k+1}\) whenever \(V_k\neq\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Indices of rows currently present in the master problem.
Violated row indices selected at iteration k.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Oriented Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Delayed activation of members of an original indexed constraint system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{x\in X:g_t(x)\leq0\text{ for all }t\in T\}\), and initialize a finite active set \(T_0\subseteq T\). At iteration \(k\), optimize over \(F_k=\{x\in X:g_t(x)\leq0\ (t\in T_k)\}\) to obtain \(x^k\). A constraint oracle returns finite \(V_k\subseteq\{t\in T:g_t(x^k)>0\}\). If \(V_k\neq\varnothing\), set \(T_{k+1}=T_k\cup V_k\); otherwise return \(x^k\). Unlike derived cutting, every added condition is a member of the original family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Activate violated members of the original constraint family as needed, rather than constructing new implied inequalities.
assumptions_latex: \(T_0\subseteq T\) is finite.
The oracle returns only indices from the original family.
The master problem over each finite active set is well-defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_k=\varnothing\) with exact separation implies \(x^k\in F\).

children.title: Gomory Tableau-Row-Space Representation Pair
children.top_down_role: Basis-dependent and row-space views supporting Gomory fractional cuts.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Original-variable representation of a Gomory tableau cut
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation of the Gomory fractional cut derived from a basis row as a Chvátal–Gomory inequality in the original variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\beta=e_u^{\mathsf T}B^{-1}\), where \(B\) is the current basis matrix, and define the row vector \(q\) by \(q_i=\beta_i-\lfloor\beta_i\rfloor\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). Then the Gomory tableau cut \(\sum_{j\in NB}f_{uj}x_j\ge f_{u0}\), when expressed in the original variables, is \(\sum_{j=1}^n\lfloor q a_j\rfloor x_j\le\lfloor q b\rfloor\), where \(a_j\) is column \(j\) of \(A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Taking the componentwise fractional part of a row of the inverse basis yields an aggregation vector under which the corresponding Gomory tableau cut is represented in the original variables as a Chvátal–Gomory inequality.
assumptions_latex: \(Ax=b\) has current basis matrix \(B\).
\(\beta=e_u^{\mathsf T}B^{-1}\).
\(q_i=\beta_i-\lfloor\beta_i\rfloor\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_{j\in NB}f_{uj}x_j\ge f_{u0}\quad\text{is represented in the original variables as}\quad\sum_{j=1}^n\lfloor q a_j\rfloor x_j\le\lfloor q b\rfloor.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Gomory Fractional Cut from a Pure-Integer Tableau Row
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tableau-row and equivalent fractional-part representations for a pure-integer linear program with integral original data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose the integral-data formulation has nonnegative integer variables for every integer-feasible solution, and an LP basic solution yields the tableau row
\[
x_{\beta_i}+\sum_{j=1}^{n-m}\bar a_{\beta_i\eta_j}x_{\eta_j}=x_{\beta_i}^*,\qquad i\in\{0,\ldots,m\}.
\]
Then every integer-feasible solution satisfies
\[
x_{\beta_i}+\sum_{j=1}^{n-m}\lfloor\bar a_{\beta_i\eta_j}\rfloor x_{\eta_j}\leq\lfloor x_{\beta_i}^*\rfloor.
\]
This integer-coefficient inequality is violated by the current LP basic solution when \(x_{\beta_i}^*\notin\mathbb Z\). Using the tableau equality, it is equivalent to
\[
\sum_{j=1}^{n-m}\bigl(\lfloor\bar a_{\beta_i\eta_j}\rfloor-\bar a_{\beta_i\eta_j}\bigr)x_{\eta_j}\leq\lfloor x_{\beta_i}^*\rfloor-x_{\beta_i}^*.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the integral-data pure-integer formulation, a simplex-tableau row produces a valid integer-coefficient Gomory cut by flooring the row coefficients and right-hand side. The cut excludes the current LP basic solution if its basic value is fractional, and subtracting the tableau equality gives the equivalent fractional-part form.
assumptions_latex: a_{ij},b_i,c_j\in\mathbb Z
x_j\in\mathbb Z_{\geq 0}\text{ for integer-feasible solutions}
x_{\beta_i}+\sum_{j=1}^{n-m}\bar a_{\beta_i\eta_j}x_{\eta_j}=x_{\beta_i}^*
i\in\{0,1,\ldots,m\}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_{\beta_i}+\sum_{j=1}^{n-m}\lfloor\bar a_{\beta_i\eta_j}\rfloor x_{\eta_j}\leq\lfloor x_{\beta_i}^*\rfloor,\qquad x_{\beta_i}^*\notin\mathbb Z\Rightarrow G_{\beta_i}\text{ excludes the current LP basic solution}.

children.title: Simplex Tableau Representation
children.top_down_role: Basis-explicit data used for fractional-cut generation.

knowledge_statements.title: Simplex Tableau Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical tableau representation underlying a pure-integer Gomory fractional cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the standard-form pure-integer system \(Ax=b\), \(x\geq0\), \(x\in\mathbb{Z}^n\), let \(B\) be a nonsingular basis and partition \(A=(B,A_N)\) and \(x=(x_B,x_N)\). Define \(\bar b=B^{-1}b\) and \(\bar A=B^{-1}A_N\). The associated simplex tableau is \[x_B=\bar b-\bar A x_N.\] Its row \(i\) is \(x_{B_i}=\bar b_i-\sum_{j\in N}\bar a_{ij}x_j\). If \(\bar b_i\notin\mathbb{Z}\), integrality of all variables permits a Gomory fractional cut from this row.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A basis rewrites basic variables as affine functions of nonbasic variables; any row with fractional basic value can generate a Gomory cut.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) and \(b\) are rational.
All variables in the represented system are integer-constrained.
\(B\) is a nonsingular column basis of \(A\).

children.title: Fractional-Row Selection
children.top_down_role: Choice of tableau rows used as cut-generation sources.

knowledge_statements.title: Fractional-Row Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eligibility condition for selecting a tableau row in the pure-integer Gomory method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a primal-feasible tableau \(x_{B_i}=\bar b_i-\sum_{j\in N}\bar a_{ij}x_j\) for a pure-integer standard-form problem, row \(i\) is eligible precisely when its basic variable is required to be integral and \(f_i=\bar b_i-\lfloor\bar b_i\rfloor\) satisfies \(0<f_i<1\). The current basic solution has \(x_N=0\) and \(x_{B_i}=\bar b_i\), so it violates integrality in that row. The associated fractional cut is \[\sum_{j\in N}(\bar a_{ij}-\lfloor\bar a_{ij}\rfloor)x_j\geq f_i.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select a tableau row whose integer-constrained basic variable has a fractional current value; its fractional parts define a violated valid cut.
assumptions_latex: The tableau represents a pure-integer standard-form system.
The current basic solution is primal feasible.
Row \(i\) corresponds to an integer-constrained basic variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0<f_i<1\implies \sum_{j\in N}\{\bar a_{ij}\}x_j\geq f_i\), violated at \(x_N=0\).

notation.meaning: Fractional part of the row right-hand side.
Fractional part r minus its floor.

children.title: Row-Space Representation
children.top_down_role: Basis-induced row-space views supporting cut construction.

knowledge_statements.title: Row-Space Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier representation of a tableau row and its Gomory fractional cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Ax=b\), \(x\geq0\), \(x\in\mathbb{Z}^n\), and let \(B\) be a basis. For basis row \(i\), define the row multiplier \(u^\top=e_i^\top B^{-1}\). Then the tableau equality is the row-space identity \[u^\top Ax=u^\top b,\] with coefficient \(u^\top A_j\) on variable \(x_j\). Because the basic-column coefficients are integral unit-vector components, the fractional cut has the full-space representation \[\sum_{j=1}^n\{u^\top A_j\}x_j\geq\{u^\top b\},\] which reduces to the usual nonbasic-variable tableau cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tableau row equals a linear combination of the original equations; fractional parts of its multiplier-generated coefficients give the same Gomory cut.
assumptions_latex: \(A\) and \(b\) are rational and every variable is integer-constrained.
\(B\) is a nonsingular basis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u^\top=e_i^\top B^{-1}\implies \sum_j\{u^\top A_j\}x_j\geq\{u^\top b\}.\)

notation.meaning: Multiplier generating the selected tableau row.

children.title: Basis Dependence
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity of generated cuts to the active basis representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Basis Dependence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dependence of a tableau-derived Gomory cut on the selected basis and row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed relaxation \(P=\{x:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\), a basis \(B\) and row \(i\) determine the multiplier \(u^\top=e_i^\top B^{-1}\), hence determine the fractional inequality \(\sum_j\{u^\top A_j\}x_j\geq\{u^\top b\}\). Two bases representing the same basic optimum can yield different multipliers, coefficients, and cut strengths. Nevertheless, whenever all variables are integer-constrained, every such fractional inequality is valid for \(P\cap\mathbb{Z}^n\); basis dependence changes the selected relaxation strengthening, not the integer feasible set being protected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Different bases or tableau rows may produce different Gomory cuts, although every correctly derived cut remains valid for the same integer feasible set.
assumptions_latex: The system is a rational pure-integer standard-form system.
Each compared row has a fractional right-hand side.
Each multiplier is generated by a nonsingular basis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_1\neq B_2\) may imply distinct cuts, while \(P\cap\mathbb{Z}^n\) satisfies both.

children.title: Primal Simplex Form
children.top_down_role: Gomory cutting organized around primal-simplex relaxation states.

knowledge_statements.title: Primal Simplex Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gomory iteration reoptimized through a primal-feasible auxiliary simplex formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Solve the current pure-integer linear relaxation by primal simplex and select an eligible fractional tableau row. Append its Gomory inequality in equality form by introducing a nonnegative slack or surplus variable. Because the old optimizer violates the new inequality, construct a primal-feasible auxiliary basis, using a phase-I variable if necessary, and apply primal-simplex pivots until feasibility and optimality for the augmented relaxation are attained. If every integer-constrained basic value is integral, return the current solution; otherwise select another fractional row and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After adding a Gomory cut, establish a feasible auxiliary basis and use primal simplex to optimize the strengthened relaxation before generating another cut.
assumptions_latex: The relaxation is a rational pure-integer standard-form problem.
Each selected row satisfies the fractional-row condition.
The auxiliary phase detects infeasibility or produces a primal-feasible basis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{integral optimal basic solution}\Rightarrow\text{optimal solution of the pure-integer problem}.\)

children.title: Dual Simplex Form
children.top_down_role: Gomory cutting organized around dual-simplex reoptimization.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Simplex Form
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gomory iteration exploiting dual feasibility after insertion of a violated cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Begin with an optimal tableau of the current pure-integer relaxation and select a fractional row. Add the Gomory inequality with a slack variable and choose its sign so that the new slack is basic with a negative right-hand side at the old optimizer. The augmented tableau is then primal infeasible but retains the old reduced costs and hence dual feasibility. Apply dual-simplex pivots under a prescribed anti-cycling rule until primal feasibility is restored or infeasibility is certified. If the restored optimum is integral, return it; otherwise generate another fractional cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Insert each violated Gomory cut so dual feasibility is preserved, then use anti-cycling dual-simplex pivots to restore primal feasibility or certify infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: The current tableau is dual feasible and optimal before cut insertion.
The cut is valid and violated by the current basic solution.
Dual-simplex pivots use a prescribed anti-cycling rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{dual feasible augmented tableau}+\text{restored primal feasibility}\Rightarrow\text{optimal augmented tableau}.\)

notation.meaning: Slack variable introduced for the new cut.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite termination under lexicographic Gomory conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient finite-termination conditions for repeated Gomory cutting with dual-simplex reoptimization; no converse or guarantee outside these conditions is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose that throughout the Gomory cutting-plane procedure: \(\text{(i)}\) every column in every tableau is lexicographically positive; \(\text{(ii)}\) the rightmost tableau column decreases lexicographically at every dual-pivot iteration; and \(\text{(iii)}\) the highest possible tableau row is always selected as the source row for a cut. Then the cutting-plane method terminates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Gomory cutting-plane method terminates if every tableau column remains lexicographically positive, each dual pivot lexicographically decreases the rightmost column, and every cut is generated from the highest possible source row.
assumptions_latex: \text{Every column in every tableau is lexicographically positive.}
\text{The rightmost tableau column decreases lexicographically at each dual-pivot iteration.}
\text{The highest possible tableau row is always chosen as the cut source.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The Gomory cutting-plane method terminates after finitely many iterations.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-simplex form of the Gomory fractional cutting-plane procedure for a pure integer linear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Solve the LP relaxation and obtain an optimum \(x^*\). Set the feasibility flag to true. While \(x^*\notin\mathbb Z^n\) and the flag remains true, choose a source row, add its Gomory cut and a corresponding basic variable, and apply dual simplex. If dual simplex reports unboundedness, set the feasibility flag to false; otherwise let \(x^*\) be the new optimum. The reoptimization maintains dual feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the LP relaxation. While its current optimum is nonintegral and infeasibility has not been declared, choose a source row, add the corresponding Gomory cut and a basic variable, and reoptimize by dual simplex. If dual simplex reports unboundedness, declare the integer program infeasible; otherwise continue from the new optimum. Dual feasibility is maintained during reoptimization.
assumptions_latex: \text{The problem is a pure integer linear program.}
\text{Its LP relaxation can initially be solved to optimality.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The procedure continues with a dual-feasible optimum, stops at an integer optimum, or declares infeasibility after reported dual unboundedness.}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pure-integer Gomory cutting with primal-simplex initialization and dual-simplex reoptimization. Cut validity and the infeasibility test are included; finite termination requires the separately stated lexicographic conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\max\{cx:x\ge 0,\ Ax\le b,\ x\in\mathbb Z^n\}\) with integral \(A,b,c\), introduce nonnegative integral slack variables and obtain an optimal tableau of the LP relaxation. If its basic solution is integral, it is optimal for the ILP. Otherwise, a valid tableau equation \(\sum_j\delta_{ij}\xi_j=\varphi_i\), with integral \(\xi\ge0\) and \(\varphi_i\notin\mathbb Z\), yields the Gomory cut \(\sum_j\{\delta_{ij}\}\xi_j\ge\{\varphi_i\}\). This cut is valid for every integral feasible point and excludes the current fractional basic solution. Add the cut with a slack variable, reoptimize by dual simplex, and repeat. In the stated tableau convention, a dual-simplex row with negative right-hand side and all remaining row coefficients nonnegative certifies primal infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a pure integer linear program with integral data, initialize from an optimal LP tableau. An integral optimal basic solution solves the ILP. Otherwise, a tableau equation with fractional right-hand side produces a Gomory fractional cut that preserves all integer feasible points and removes the current fractional basic solution. Add the cut and reoptimize by dual simplex. A row with negative right-hand side and all remaining coefficients nonnegative certifies infeasibility in the stated tableau convention. Finite termination is not asserted without the additional lexicographic conditions.
assumptions_latex: A\in\mathbb Z^{m\times n},\quad b\in\mathbb Z^m,\quad c\in\mathbb Z^n
x\ge0,\quad Ax\le b,\quad x\in\mathbb Z^n
\text{The LP relaxation admits an optimal simplex tableau.}
\xi\in\mathbb Z_+^{n+m},\quad \sum_j\delta_{ij}\xi_j=\varphi_i,\quad \varphi_i\notin\mathbb Z
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_j\{\delta_{ij}\}\xi_j\ge\{\varphi_i\}\text{ is valid for all integral feasible points and excludes the current fractional basic solution; an integral optimal tableau solves the ILP, while the specified dual-simplex row certifies infeasibility.}

knowledge_statements.title: Form-Switching Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Choice of simplex reoptimization form according to feasibility retained after cut insertion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After a valid cut is appended to an optimal relaxation tableau, select the reoptimization form from the feasibility state of the augmented basis. If the basis remains dual feasible but is primal infeasible because the new basic slack violates its sign restriction, use dual simplex. If the basis is primal feasible but dual infeasible, use primal simplex. If it is both primal and dual feasible, it is already optimal. If it is neither primal nor dual feasible, perform a phase-I or basis-repair procedure before selecting a simplex form. This choice changes the reoptimization path but not the appended valid inequality or the strengthened feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use dual simplex for a dual-feasible but primal-infeasible augmented basis, primal simplex for a primal-feasible but dual-infeasible basis, no reoptimization when both hold, and basis repair when neither holds.
assumptions_latex: The appended inequality is valid for the integer feasible set.
Primal feasibility, dual feasibility, and reduced-cost signs are evaluated under one consistent simplex convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{dual feasible and primal infeasible}\Rightarrow\text{dual simplex};\quad \text{primal feasible and dual infeasible}\Rightarrow\text{primal simplex};\quad \text{both feasible}\Rightarrow\text{optimal};\quad \text{neither feasible}\Rightarrow\text{basis repair}.\)

children.title: Gomory Lexicographic Method

knowledge_statements.title: Gomory Lexicographic Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pure-integer Gomory cutting with lexicographic row choice and pivot control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a rational pure-integer linear program in standard form, maintain an optimal tableau whose basic solutions are ordered lexicographically. If the optimum is integral, stop. Otherwise choose the first basic row in the fixed lexicographic order whose right-hand side is fractional, append its Gomory fractional cut, and reoptimize using lexicographic dual-simplex ratio tests. If the augmented relaxation is infeasible, declare the integer problem infeasible; otherwise repeat. The fixed row order and lexicographic pivot rule prevent cycling and organize successive tableaux by a strict lexicographic progress measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select the first fractional row under a fixed order and reoptimize with lexicographic dual-simplex pivots, producing a noncycling pure-integer cutting-plane method.
assumptions_latex: The pure-integer program has rational standard-form data.
The initial linear relaxation has an optimal basis or is certified infeasible or unbounded.
Row selection and pivot ties use fixed lexicographic rules.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{integral terminal optimum}\Rightarrow\text{optimal pure-integer solution}.\)

notation.meaning: First fractional basic row in the fixed order.
Lexicographic order used for progress and tie-breaking.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pure-integer cutting-plane iteration using lexicographically optimal bases and the smallest-indexed fractional objective or original variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: t\gets0;\quad\text{at iteration }t:\quad\begin{cases}\text{If the current relaxation is infeasible, declare the original integer program infeasible.}\\\text{Otherwise compute a lexicographically optimal basis and its basic solution }\bar x.\\\text{If }(\bar x_1,\ldots,\bar x_n)\in\mathbb Z^n,\text{ return it as optimal.}\\\text{Otherwise set }h=\min\{i\in\{0,\ldots,n\}:\bar x_i\notin\mathbb Z\},\text{ add the rounded cut from row }h,\ t\gets t+1,\text{ and repeat.}\end{cases}
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Begin with no added cuts. At each iteration, infeasibility of the current relaxation certifies infeasibility of the original pure integer program. Otherwise compute a lexicographically optimal basis. If the original variables are integral, return them as an optimal integer solution. If not, choose the smallest-indexed fractional variable among the objective and original variables, add the rounded cut from its tableau row, increment the iteration counter, and repeat.
assumptions_latex: \text{The current relaxation is the augmented pure-integer formulation at iteration }t
\text{A lexicographically optimal basis is computed whenever the relaxation is feasible}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{infeasible relaxation}\Rightarrow\text{integer infeasibility};\quad (\bar x_1,\ldots,\bar x_n)\in\mathbb Z^n\Rightarrow\bar x\text{ is optimal};\quad\text{otherwise add the row-}h\text{ cut for }h=\min\{i\in\{0,\ldots,n\}:\bar x_i\notin\mathbb Z\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lexicographically optimal bases for Gomory's pure-integer method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tableau condition characterizing a lexicographically largest feasible solution and supporting finite fractional-cut progress under lexicographic rules.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \text{A feasible basis }B\text{ with nonbasic set }N\text{ is lexicographically optimal if, for every }j\in N,\text{ the least }i\in\{0\}\cup B\text{ for which }\bar a_{ij}\ne0\text{ satisfies }i<j\text{ and }\bar a_{ij}>0.\text{ The associated basic solution is the lexicographically largest feasible solution. If the relaxation is feasible and bounded, such a basis exists and can be computed by simplex. Suitable lexicographic pivot and cut-row rules make Gomory's method finitely convergent.}
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible basis is lexicographically optimal when the first nonzero tableau entry in every nonbasic column, ordered over the objective and basic rows, is positive and has an index smaller than the column index. Its basic solution is the lexicographically largest feasible solution. Every bounded feasible relaxation admits such a basis, and suitable lexicographic pivot and cut-row rules give finite convergence of Gomory's pure-integer method.

B\text{ is a feasible basis with nonbasic set }N
\text{Existence is asserted when the current relaxation is feasible and bounded}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B\text{ lexicographically optimal}\Rightarrow\bar x(B)\text{ is lexicographically largest};\qquad \text{feasible and bounded}\Rightarrow\exists B\text{ lexicographically optimal}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination guarantee for the lexicographic Gomory fractional dual cutting-plane method for integer linear programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In the fractional dual algorithm for an integer linear program, choose the source row to be the first row with \(a_{t0}\notin\mathbb Z\), and use the lexicographic dual simplex algorithm. If the cost \(z\) of feasible solutions to the original problem is bounded above, then the algorithm terminates after finitely many steps with an integer solution or finds that the original problem has no feasible integer solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In the fractional dual algorithm for an integer linear program, choose the first row whose relevant entry is noninteger and use the lexicographic dual simplex algorithm. If feasible-solution costs are bounded above, the algorithm finitely terminates with an integer solution or finds that no feasible integer solution exists.
assumptions_latex: \text{The original problem is an integer linear program.}
\text{The source row is the first row satisfying }a_{t0}\notin\mathbb Z.
\text{The lexicographic version of the dual simplex algorithm is used.}
\exists U\in\mathbb R\;\forall x\text{ feasible for the original problem},\;z(x)\le U.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{After finitely many steps, the algorithm returns an integer solution or finds that the original problem has no feasible integer solution.}

children.title: Finite-Convergence Theory
children.top_down_role: Termination results and their rationality, pivoting, and arithmetic regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Convergence Theory
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical finite termination under rational pure-integer and lexicographic algorithmic restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a rational pure-integer linear program in standard form whose linear relaxation has a finite optimum, and apply the lexicographic Gomory fractional cutting-plane method with exact rational arithmetic, first-fractional-row selection, and lexicographic dual-simplex pivoting. Then the procedure terminates after finitely many cut-generation and pivot operations, either with an optimal integer solution or with a certificate that no integer-feasible solution exists. This conclusion depends on the specified row-selection, pivoting, and arithmetic regime; arbitrary repeated tableau cuts or inexact pivoting are not covered.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under rational data, exact arithmetic, and prescribed lexicographic row and pivot rules, the classical pure-integer Gomory procedure terminates finitely.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a rational pure-integer standard-form linear program with finite relaxation optimum.
All tableau and cut computations use exact rational arithmetic.
First-fractional-row selection and lexicographic dual-simplex pivoting are enforced.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{The algorithm terminates finitely with an optimal integer solution or an integer-infeasibility certificate}.\)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited introductory cutting-plane section is insufficient to verify this exact finite-termination theorem, especially finite detection of integer infeasibility under the listed row-selection and pivot rules. A theorem-level source and its complete hypotheses are required.

children.title: Repeated-Tableau Cutting Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Classical practical limitations of repeated tableau cutting.

children.title: Degeneracy Effects
children.top_down_role: Progress limitations associated with degenerate tableau states.

assumptions_latex: The linear relaxation is represented by simplex tableaux and all computations are exact.
The selected basic integer row has a fractional right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Degeneracy can prevent strict improvement of the relaxation objective or primal point after a valid cut, although the current fractional basic solution is removed.

notation.meaning: linear-relaxation objective value at iteration k

review_flags: Exact convergence consequences depend on pivoting and cut-selection rules; a supporting source is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes validity of a Gomory cut from strict algorithmic progress after reoptimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a Gomory fractional cut is generated from a fractional basic integer row at a degenerate basic feasible solution \(\bar x\). The cut is valid and excludes the tableau solution, but reoptimization may perform zero-length pivots and reach a different basis representing the same primal point or the same objective value. Consequently, neither \(v_{k+1}<v_k\) for minimization nor a positive change in the primal solution is guaranteed at every cutting iteration. Degeneracy therefore invalidates progress tests based solely on strict objective improvement or basis change; finite convergence requires additional exact-arithmetic pivoting and cut-selection hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a degenerate tableau, a valid Gomory cut may cause only zero-length pivots or a basis change, so objective or primal-point improvement need not occur immediately.
knowledge_statements.title: Degeneracy Effects

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied. Moreover, an exact Gomory cut that is violated by the current tableau solution excludes that primal point, so reoptimization cannot return the identical primal point, although it can retain the same objective value or perform degenerate pivots. The progress and finite-convergence claims require correction and a precise convergence locator.

children.title: Coefficient-Growth Pathologies
children.top_down_role: Encoding and arithmetic burdens caused by repeated cutting.

assumptions_latex: The initial tableau data are rational and cuts are repeatedly generated from rational tableau rows.
Cuts are stored after clearing denominators to obtain integer coefficients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The encoding length of generated rows can grow with the number of pivots and cuts; no iteration-independent coefficient bound follows from validity alone.

notation.meaning: largest binary encoding length among coefficients after iteration k
least common multiple of denominators in a generated row

review_flags: A precise worst-case coefficient-growth theorem and locator are required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Addresses arithmetic size growth in repeated rational-tableau cut generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), pivoting divides tableau coefficients by a rational pivot, while forming a fractional cut introduces fractional parts of the resulting coefficients. If the cut is normalized integrally, multiplication by the denominator least common multiple \(D_k\) can enlarge every coefficient. Repeating these operations can make \(L_k\) increase even when the original formulation has small integral data. Thus cut validity and finite-dimensionality do not imply a uniform bound on generated coefficient magnitudes or encoding lengths independent of \(k\); implementations need normalization, coefficient filtering, or an explicit bit-complexity analysis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated rational pivots, fractional-part operations, and denominator clearing can produce cuts whose coefficient sizes and bit lengths grow substantially with the iteration count.
knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient-Growth Pathologies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind and local scope fit, but no source supports the claimed absence of an iteration-independent coefficient or encoding-length bound. A precise arithmetic-growth result or documented pathology is required.

children.title: Numerical-Stability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Reliability limits arising from finite-precision computation.

assumptions_latex: Tableau coefficients and cut coefficients are computed in finite-precision arithmetic.
Feasibility and integrality are judged using positive numerical tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without certified error bounds or validity-preserving rounding, computed cuts and stopping decisions need not be valid for the exact mixed-integer set.
review_flags: The tolerance-to-validity error bound depends on the solver arithmetic model and needs a dedicated source.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-precision boundary for tableau-derived Gomory cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fractional-part operations are discontinuous at integers: a coefficient within \(\tau_I\) of an integer may be classified differently after rounding, and cancellation can perturb both sides of a generated inequality. Hence the computed inequality \(\widehat\alpha^{\mathsf T}x\geq\widehat\beta\) is not automatically valid for the exact integer-feasible set merely because it is valid for the rounded tableau. Likewise, declaring all basic integer variables integral within \(\tau_I\) does not certify exact integrality. Validity requires exact rational reconstruction, directed validity-preserving rounding with a proved error margin, or independent certification against the original data.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near-integer tableau values are unstable under floating-point fractional-part operations; ordinary tolerances alone cannot certify exact cut validity or exact integrality.
knowledge_statements.title: Numerical-Stability Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement appropriately describes a numerical-stability boundary, but its validity and certification claims depend on the floating-point error model, rounding procedure, and solver tolerances. No supporting source or quantitative error result is supplied.

children.title: Repeated-Cutting Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Practical regimes where continued tableau cutting becomes ineffective.

assumptions_latex: Cuts are generated repeatedly from reoptimized simplex tableaux.
No exact-arithmetic, anti-cycling, or mandatory cut-selection rule is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The unrestricted repeated-tableau procedure has no general finite-termination guarantee and may stall, cycle among bases, or terminate incorrectly under tolerances.

notation.meaning: solution returned after reoptimizing over the current relaxation

review_flags: Finite convergence varies with the pure-integer or mixed-integer setting and the pivoting rule; an exact source is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary of naive repeated-tableau cutting, not of specially controlled exact Gomory algorithms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the procedure that solves \(P_k\), chooses any fractional tableau row, adds its Gomory cut, and reoptimizes to obtain \(P_{k+1}\) and \(x^{k+1}\). Validity gives \(P_{k+1}\subseteq P_k\), but nestedness alone does not ensure finitely many iterations. Degenerate pivots may yield no objective progress, weak cuts may accumulate without closing the relevant gap, and finite-precision tolerances may accept a nonintegral point or discard a necessary cut. Therefore finite termination cannot be asserted without the arithmetic, pivoting, normalization, and cut-selection conditions of a specific convergence theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arbitrary repeated tableau cuts only create nested relaxations; without controlled exact rules, the process may stall, cycle, or stop incorrectly.
knowledge_statements.title: Repeated-Cutting Failure Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, but stalling, cycling, and nontermination must be stated for a precisely specified pure- or mixed-integer procedure and supported by a convergence or counterexample source. Nestedness alone only establishes the stated insufficiency, not every listed failure mode.

children.title: Mixed-Integer Cutting-Plane Algorithms
children.top_down_role: General-purpose cutting-plane families for models containing both integer and continuous variables.

children.title: Gomory Mixed-Integer Cut Algorithms
children.top_down_role: Tableau-based mixed-integer cutting-plane systems.

assumptions_latex: A tableau row is \(x_B+\sum_{j\in J_I}a_jx_j+\sum_{j\in J_C}a_jx_j=b\), where \(x_B\) and \(x_j\) for \(j\in J_I\) are integer and all nonbasic variables are nonnegative.
The fractional part \(f_0=b-\lfloor b\rfloor\) satisfies \(0<f_0<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed Gomory mixed-integer inequality is valid, cuts off the current tableau solution, and may be added before reoptimization.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-row tableau version of Gomory mixed-integer cut generation.

source_refs.locator: 9.4 Using Lift-and-Project to Choose the Best Mixed Integer Gomory Cut p. 117

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At the current tableau solution set all nonbasic variables to zero. For every \(j\in J_I\), compute \(f_j=a_j-\lfloor a_j\rfloor\), and add the cut
\[
\sum_{\substack{j\in J_I\\ f_j\leq f_0}}\frac{f_j}{f_0}x_j+\sum_{\substack{j\in J_I\\ f_j>f_0}}\frac{1-f_j}{1-f_0}x_j+\sum_{\substack{j\in J_C\\ a_j\geq0}}\frac{a_j}{f_0}x_j+\sum_{\substack{j\in J_C\\ a_j<0}}\frac{-a_j}{1-f_0}x_j\geq1.
\]
Reoptimize the strengthened relaxation and repeat until no selected basic integer variable is fractional or a prescribed stopping limit is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: From a fractional tableau row with an integer basic variable, compute the standard GMI coefficients, add the violated cut, and reoptimize.
knowledge_statements.title: Gomory Mixed-Integer Cut Algorithms

source_witnesses.locator: 9.4 Using Lift-and-Project to Choose the Best Mixed Integer Gomory Cut p. 117

children.title: Mixed-Integer Rounding Algorithms
children.top_down_role: Aggregation-and-rounding systems for general mixed-integer separation.

assumptions_latex: The valid row is \(\sum_{j=1}^p a_jx_j+\sum_{k=1}^q g_ky_k\leq b\), with \(x\in\mathbb Z_+^p\), \(y\in\mathbb R_+^q\), and rational coefficients.
The fractional part \(f=b-\lfloor b\rfloor\) satisfies \(0<f<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The mixed-integer rounding inequality displayed in the statement is valid for every feasible mixed-integer point.

notation.meaning: fractional part of the right-hand side

review_flags: The supplied locator is indirect for the exact MIR formula.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical nonnegative single-row MIR procedure after valid aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Aggregate valid model rows to obtain the stated single-row inequality and scale it so that \(0<f<1\). For each integer coefficient set \(r_j=a_j-\lfloor a_j\rfloor\). Add
\[
\sum_{j=1}^p\left(\lfloor a_j\rfloor+\frac{(r_j-f)^+}{1-f}\right)x_j+\sum_{k=1}^q\frac{(g_k)^+}{1-f}y_k\leq\lfloor b\rfloor.
\]
If the current relaxation point violates this inequality, append it and reoptimize. Otherwise try another valid aggregation; stop when the prescribed aggregation family yields no violated MIR cut or an iteration limit is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aggregate rows into a canonical mixed-integer inequality, apply the MIR coefficient formula, add a violated cut, and repeat over the chosen aggregations.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Integer Rounding Algorithms

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: For a negative continuous coefficient, replacing it by zero is generally invalid: a negative-coefficient continuous variable can provide slack that permits integer assignments excluded by the displayed cut. The standard MIR formula requires an appropriate piecewise coefficient for continuous variables. The cited formulation section is also indirect for this exact formula, so an exact MIR theorem or definition locator is required.

children.title: Split-Cut Algorithms
children.top_down_role: Cut generation and iterative strengthening based on split disjunctions.

assumptions_latex: The relaxation is a rational polyhedron \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
The vector \(\pi\in\mathbb Z^n\) has support only on integer-constrained variables, and \(\pi_0\in\mathbb Z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every inequality valid for the convex hull of the two split branches is valid for all mixed-integer points in \(P\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iterative separation using one valid split disjunction at a time.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Disjunctive Programming and Extended Formulations p. 69

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a relaxation point \(\bar x\in P\), choose \(\pi\) and \(\pi_0\) such that \(\pi_0<\pi^{\mathsf T}\bar x<\pi_0+1\). Form
\[
P^{\pi,\pi_0}=\operatorname{conv}\bigl((P\cap\{x:\pi^{\mathsf T}x\leq\pi_0\})\cup(P\cap\{x:\pi^{\mathsf T}x\geq\pi_0+1\})\bigr).
\]
Use disjunctive separation to find an inequality valid for \(P^{\pi,\pi_0}\) and violated by \(\bar x\). Add it, reoptimize, and repeat over selected splits. Return the strengthened relaxation when no selected split separates the current point or a stopping limit is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a split violated fractionally by the relaxation point, separate it from the convex hull of both branches, add the cut, and reoptimize.
knowledge_statements.title: Split-Cut Algorithms

children.title: Lift-Project Algorithm Family
children.top_down_role: Mixed-binary cut generation through lifted disjunctive representations.

children.title: Lifted Disjunctive Formulations
children.top_down_role: Higher-dimensional disjunctive representations used to generate mixed-binary cuts.

assumptions_latex: Each disjunct is a nonempty bounded polyhedron \(P_i=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:A_ix\leq b_i\}\), for \(i=1,\ldots,m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The projection of the lifted system onto x is exactly \(\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{i=1}^mP_i)\).

notation.meaning: copy of the original vector associated with disjunct i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Balas lifted convex-hull formulation for a finite union of bounded polyhedra.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Disjunctive Programming and Extended Formulations p. 69

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Introduce \(x^i\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\lambda_i\geq0\) for every disjunct. Then
\[
\operatorname{conv}\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^mP_i\right)=\left\{x:\begin{array}{l}x=\sum_{i=1}^m x^i,\quad \sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i=1,\\ A_ix^i\leq b_i\lambda_i\quad(i=1,\ldots,m),\quad \lambda_i\geq0\end{array}\right\}.
\]
The variables \(x^i\) and \(\lambda_i\) are lifted variables; eliminating them recovers the convex hull in the original \(x\)-space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Copies of the original variables and convex-combination weights give an extended formulation whose projection equals the convex hull of a finite polyhedral union.
knowledge_statements.title: Lifted Disjunctive Formulations

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Disjunctive Programming and Extended Formulations p. 69

children.title: Projection-Based Cut Recovery
children.top_down_role: Recovery of original-space inequalities from lifted representations.

assumptions_latex: The lifted polyhedron is \(Q=\{(x,z):Ax+Bz\leq d\}\) and is nonempty.
All data and the proposed inequality are rational.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The multiplier vector is a directly checkable certificate that the recovered inequality is valid for the projection of Q.

notation.meaning: projection of the lifted polyhedron onto the original variables

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas-multiplier recovery of an original-space cut from a lifted formulation.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Disjunctive Programming and Extended Formulations p. 69

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An inequality \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) is certified valid for \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)\) whenever there exists \(\lambda\geq0\) satisfying
\[
\lambda^{\mathsf T}A=\alpha^{\mathsf T},\qquad \lambda^{\mathsf T}B=0,
\qquad \lambda^{\mathsf T}d\leq\beta.
\]
Indeed, the equality \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}B=0\) eliminates the lifted variables. A projection-based cut-recovery algorithm obtains such a multiplier from a separation or dual linear program, returns \((\alpha,\beta)\), and verifies these three relations before adding the cut in the original space.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative multiplier that cancels all lifted variables and dominates the proposed right-hand side certifies a recovered original-space cut.
knowledge_statements.title: Projection-Based Cut Recovery

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Disjunctive Programming and Extended Formulations p. 69

children.title: Mixed-Binary Lifting Regimes
children.top_down_role: Lift-and-project variants distinguished by binary structure and lifting choices.

assumptions_latex: The relaxation is \(P\subseteq[0,1]^p\times\mathbb R^q\), and coordinate \(x_k\) is required to be binary.
The current point \(\bar x\in P\) satisfies \(0<\bar x_k<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Separating the current point from the lifted hull yields a valid inequality for every feasible mixed-binary point and removes the current point when separation succeeds.

notation.meaning: convex hull induced by branching on the selected binary coordinate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-variable lift-and-project step for a mixed-binary relaxation.

source_refs.locator: 9.4 Using Lift-and-Project to Choose the Best Mixed Integer Gomory Cut p. 117
Chapter 5. Disjunctive Programming and Extended Formulations p. 69

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Select a fractional binary coordinate \(x_k\) and form
\[
H_k=\operatorname{conv}\bigl((P\cap\{x:x_k=0\})\cup(P\cap\{x:x_k=1\})\bigr).
\]
Construct the two-term lifted disjunctive formulation of \(H_k\), solve a separation linear program for \(\bar x\), and project the resulting inequality onto the original variables. If a violated inequality is found, add it and reoptimize; otherwise select another fractional binary coordinate. Stop when all binary coordinates are integral, no selected disjunction separates the point, or a prescribed resource limit is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch algebraically on a fractional binary variable, separate the point from the lifted two-branch hull, project the cut, and reoptimize.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Binary Lifting Regimes

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Valid lifting of a reduced lift-and-project cut
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Provides closed-form coefficients extending a lift-and-project cut generated from a reduced CGLP to the full variable space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let (\alpha^R)^T x^R\ge\beta be the lift-and-project cut generated by solving (\overline{\mathrm{CGLP}})^R, with u^R and v^R its multiplier components. For i\in R set \alpha_i=\alpha_i^R. For i\in N\setminus R, set \alpha_i^1=(u^R)^T\widetilde{\widetilde A}_i^R, \alpha_i^2=(v^R)^T\widetilde{\widetilde A}_i^R, and \alpha_i=\max\{\alpha_i^1,\alpha_i^2\}. Then \alpha^T x\ge\beta is a valid lifting of (\alpha^R)^T x^R\ge\beta to the solution space of \overline{\mathrm{CGLP}}, where \widetilde{\widetilde A}_i^R is the subvector of \widetilde{\widetilde A}_i with the row set of \widetilde{\widetilde A}^R.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keep the coefficients of variables retained in the reduced CGLP. For each omitted variable, use the maximum of the coefficients induced by the reduced u- and v-multipliers. The resulting full-space inequality is a valid lifting of the reduced lift-and-project cut.
assumptions_latex: (\alpha^R)^T x^R\ge\beta\text{ is generated by solving }(\overline{\mathrm{CGLP}})^R
u^R\text{ and }v^R\text{ are the associated reduced-CGLP multiplier components}
\widetilde{\widetilde A}_i^R\text{ has the same row set as }\widetilde{\widetilde A}^R
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha_i=\begin{cases}\alpha_i^R,&i\in R,\\\max\{(u^R)^T\widetilde{\widetilde A}_i^R,(v^R)^T\widetilde{\widetilde A}_i^R\},&i\in N\setminus R,\end{cases}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \alpha^T x\ge\beta\text{ is a valid lifting.}

children.title: Extended-Space Cost Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Computational limits associated with higher-dimensional representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Extended-Space Cost Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit variable, constraint, and coefficient-storage bounds for the standard disaggregated disjunctive formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The standard lifted convex-hull formulation introduces \(mn\) disaggregated scalar variables and \(m\) weights, in addition to \(n\) original variables if \(x\) is retained explicitly. It has \(\sum_{i=1}^m r_i\) scaled disjunct inequalities, \(n\) linking equalities, one weight-sum equality, and \(m\) weight nonnegativity bounds. Consequently, its variable-and-row count is
\[
O\left(mn+\sum_{i=1}^m r_i\right).
\]
This count excludes coefficient storage and coefficient bit lengths. With dense disjunct matrices, storing the scaled disjunct inequalities can require \(O\left(n\sum_{i=1}^m r_i\right)\) coefficient entries. Thus the formulation replicates the original variable vector once per disjunct and can become impractical as the number, dimension, or description size of the disjuncts grows.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The standard disjunctive lift uses one variable copy per disjunct. Its variable-and-row count is linear in the replicated variables and disjunct rows, while coefficient storage additionally depends on matrix sparsity and coefficient encoding.
assumptions_latex: A disjunction contains \(m\) polyhedra in \(\mathbb R^n\), where disjunct \(i\) has \(r_i\) inequalities.
The standard disaggregated convex-hull formulation is constructed explicitly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The formulation has \(O(mn+\sum_{i=1}^m r_i)\) variables and rows, while dense coefficient storage can require \(O(n\sum_{i=1}^m r_i)\) entries, apart from coefficient bit lengths.

notation.meaning: number of inequalities describing disjunct i

children.title: Knapsack Separation
children.top_down_role: Separation systems exploiting knapsack constraint structure.

assumptions_latex: The knapsack set is \(K=\{x\in\{0,1\}^n:a^{\mathsf T}x\leq b\}\), with \(a\in\mathbb Z_+^n\) and \(b\in\mathbb Z_+\).
A finite prescribed family \(\mathcal F\) of valid inequalities \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) for \(K\) is available through an exact optimization oracle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns a maximally violated inequality in the prescribed family or certifies that the point satisfies every inequality in that family.

notation.meaning: prescribed family of valid knapsack inequalities

review_flags: Complexity depends on the chosen inequality family and its oracle representation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle-form separation over a specified family of valid knapsack inequalities.

source_refs.locator: 6.2.2 Algorithms for 0-1 linear knapsack problem p. 161

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(\bar x\), solve the family-specific auxiliary optimization problem
\[
\Delta^*=\max\{\alpha^{\mathsf T}\bar x-\beta:(\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal F\}.
\]
If \(\Delta^*>0\), return an optimizer \((\alpha^*,\beta^*)\) as the violated cut \((\alpha^*)^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta^*\). If \(\Delta^*\leq0\), certify that no member of \(\mathcal F\) separates \(\bar x\). When the auxiliary problem has integer weights or capacity states, it may be solved exactly by enumeration or dynamic programming; the resulting running time is polynomial in the state-space size and may be pseudopolynomial in numeric capacity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximize violation over a specified valid knapsack-inequality family; return the maximizer when positive, otherwise certify family-wise nonseparation.

children.title: Cover Separation
children.top_down_role: Separation of cover-derived inequality families.

knowledge_statements.title: Cover Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact separation of basic cover inequalities for a binary knapsack row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(a\in\mathbb{R}_{>0}^n\), \(b\ge 0\), and \(\bar x\in[0,1]^n\), solve \[\min\left\{\sum_{i=1}^n(1-\bar x_i)z_i:\ z\in\{0,1\}^n,\ \sum_{i=1}^n a_i z_i>b\right\}.\] If the problem is infeasible or its optimum is at least \(1\), report that no basic cover inequality is violated. Otherwise, for \(C=\{i:z_i=1\}\), output \(\sum_{i\in C}x_i\le |C|-1\). The inequality is violated at \(\bar x\) exactly when \(\sum_{i\in C}(1-\bar x_i)<1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Find a knapsack cover minimizing its slack at the fractional point; output its cover inequality precisely when the minimum slack is below one.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i>0\) for every \(i\), and the valid knapsack row is \(a^\top x\le b\).
\(x\in\{0,1\}^n\) in the integer model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns a violated basic cover inequality or certifies that none exists for the given row.

children.title: Flow-Cover Separation
children.top_down_role: Separation specialized to mixed-binary flow-cover structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Flow-Cover Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation over the standard single-node capacitated flow-cover family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X=\{(x,y):\sum_{i\in N}x_i\le d,\ 0\le x_i\le u_i y_i,\ y_i\in\{0,1\}\}\) and \((\bar x,\bar y)\) in its relaxation, enumerate or optimize over subsets \(C\subseteq N\) satisfying \(\sum_{i\in C}u_i=d+\lambda_C\) with \(\lambda_C>0\). Minimize the slack of \[\sum_{i\in C}x_i+\sum_{i\in C}(u_i-\lambda_C)^+(1-y_i)\le d.\] Output a minimizing inequality when its slack at \((\bar x,\bar y)\) is negative; otherwise certify nonviolation within this flow-cover family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search capacity covers of a single-node flow set and return the standard flow-cover inequality having negative slack, if one exists.
assumptions_latex: \(d>0\) and \(u_i>0\) for all \(i\in N\).
\(0\le\bar x_i\le u_i\bar y_i\) and \(0\le\bar y_i\le1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A negative minimum slack identifies a violated flow-cover inequality for \(X\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed flow-cover formula is plausible, but no citation supports its precise form or the claimed family-level separation certificate.

children.title: Cover-Structure Recognition
children.top_down_role: Identification of embedded structures suitable for cover-based separation.

knowledge_statements.title: Cover-Structure Recognition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recognition of valid binary knapsack restrictions capable of generating cover inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a valid row \(\sum_{i\in B}\alpha_i x_i+g(w)\le\beta\), where \(x_i\in\{0,1\}\), choose a certified lower bound \(L\le g(w)\) valid over the relevant bounds and constraints. Then \(\sum_{i\in B}\alpha_i x_i\le\beta-L\) is an implied binary row. Complement each binary variable having a negative coefficient and absorb the resulting constant into the right-hand side, obtaining \(\sum_{i\in N}a_i y_i\le b\) with \(a_i>0\). Declare usable cover structure when \(b\ge0\) and \(\sum_{i\in N}a_i>b\). A subset \(C\subseteq N\) is a cover exactly when \(\sum_{i\in C}a_i>b\), and it is minimal exactly when additionally \(\sum_{i\in C\setminus\{j\}}a_i\le b\) for every \(j\in C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Derive a valid binary knapsack restriction using a certified lower bound for eliminated terms, complement binaries to obtain positive coefficients, and recognize covers and minimal covers by the stated capacity tests.
assumptions_latex: \(B\) is finite and every \(x_i\), \(i\in B\), is binary.
The bound \(L\le g(w)\) is valid uniformly over the relevant feasible domain.
Only exact substitutions, such as fixing, justify an equivalence claim; general bound substitution yields an implication.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recognized subsets are precisely the covers of the derived valid binary knapsack row, and the deletion tests characterize its minimal covers.

notation.meaning: Indices of binary variables before normalization.
Indices retained in the positive-coefficient normalized row.
A certified lower bound on the eliminated contribution.
