children.title: Packing Separation
children.top_down_role: Separation based on binary packing structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Packing Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of explicitly recognized at-most-one packing sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P\) be a finite family of recognized index sets for which \(\sum_{i\in P}x_i\le1\) is valid for every \(P\in\mathcal P\), and let \(\bar x\in[0,1]^n\). Compute \(v(P)=\sum_{i\in P}\bar x_i-1\) for every \(P\in\mathcal P\). If \(\max_{P\in\mathcal P}v(P)>0\), output a maximizing packing inequality. Otherwise report that no inequality represented by \(\mathcal P\) is violated. This scan does not certify absence of stronger clique inequalities not explicitly contained in \(\mathcal P\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scan recognized at-most-one sets and output the packing inequality with greatest positive violation; the certificate is limited to the supplied family.
assumptions_latex: Every member of \(\mathcal P\) is a valid at-most-one set for the integer feasible region.
\(\mathcal P\) is finite and explicitly represented.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm exactly separates the packing inequalities indexed by \(\mathcal P\).

notation.meaning: Violation of the packing inequality indexed by \(P\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite scan is mathematically coherent and correctly limits its certificate to the supplied packing family, but the validity and separation framework have no cited source.

children.title: Clique Separation
children.top_down_role: Separation using cliques in conflict representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Clique Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact conflict-graph separation of clique inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a conflict graph \(G=(V,E)\) for binary variables and a point \(\bar x\in[0,1]^V\), solve the maximum-weight clique problem \[\omega(\bar x)=\max\left\{\sum_{i\in K}\bar x_i:\ K\subseteq V,\ \{i,j\}\in E\text{ for all distinct }i,j\in K\right\}.\] If \(\omega(\bar x)>1\), output \(\sum_{i\in K}x_i\le1\) for a maximizing clique \(K\). If \(\omega(\bar x)\le1\), certify that no clique inequality of \(G\) is violated at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve a maximum-weight clique problem using fractional variable values as weights; a weight above one yields a violated clique inequality.
assumptions_latex: An edge \(\{i,j\}\in E\) means that \(x_i=x_j=1\) is infeasible.
All vertices index binary variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The maximum-weight clique value exceeds one exactly when a clique inequality is violated.

notation.meaning: A clique of mutually conflicting variables.

children.title: Cycle Separation

knowledge_statements.title: Cycle Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation of odd-cycle inequalities for a conflict-graph stable-set relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a conflict graph \(G=(V,E)\) and \(\bar x\in[0,1]^V\), minimize over all simple odd cycles \(C\) of length at least three the slack \[s(C)=\frac{|C|-1}{2}-\sum_{i\in C}\bar x_i.\] If the minimum is negative, output the odd-cycle inequality \(\sum_{i\in C}x_i\le (|C|-1)/2\) for a minimizing cycle. Otherwise certify that no odd-cycle inequality associated with a simple odd cycle of \(G\) is violated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search all simple odd conflict cycles and return one whose fractional vertex sum exceeds half its length rounded down.
assumptions_latex: Every edge of \(G\) represents a valid pairwise conflict.
Vertices correspond to binary variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Negative minimum slack is equivalent to violation of an odd-cycle inequality.

notation.meaning: A simple odd cycle in the conflict graph.
Slack of the odd-cycle inequality at \(\bar x\).

children.title: Conflict-Graph Recognition
children.top_down_role: Construction and interpretation of graph structures supporting these separators.

knowledge_statements.title: Conflict-Graph Recognition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic recognition of pairwise conflicts among binary variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For binary variables indexed by \(V\) and feasible set \(F\), construct \(G=(V,E)\) by placing \(\{i,j\}\in E\) exactly when \[F\cap\{x:x_i=1,\ x_j=1\}=\varnothing.\] An exact recognizer queries feasibility for each unordered pair and returns the resulting graph. A row-based recognizer may add \(\{i,j\}\) whenever a valid packing row with nonnegative coefficients implies \(x_i+x_j\le1\), but then returns only a certified subgraph of the exact conflict graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Connect two binary variables exactly when fixing both to one makes the model infeasible; cheaper row tests may recognize only a certified subgraph.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is the integer feasible region projected onto variables containing \(V\).
Each feasibility query is answered exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exact procedure recognizes every pairwise binary conflict, while sufficient row tests recognize only valid edges.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact pairwise-feasibility definition and certified-subgraph qualification are coherent, but no source supports the recognition procedure or conflict-graph convention.

children.title: Routing-Connectivity Separation Family

children.title: Routing Separation
children.top_down_role: Separation systems specialized to routing formulations.

knowledge_statements.title: Routing Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Capacity-cut separation for an undirected capacitated vehicle-routing relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V\cup\{0\},E)\) have depot \(0\), customer demands \(q_i\ge0\), vehicle capacity \(Q>0\), and fractional edge vector \(\bar x\). For each nonempty \(S\subseteq V\), define \(r(S)=\lceil\sum_{i\in S}q_i/Q\rceil\) and slack \[s(S)=\bar x(\delta(S))-2r(S).\] Minimize \(s(S)\) over customer subsets by an exact oracle or a documented heuristic. Output \(x(\delta(S))\ge2r(S)\) when negative; only an exact oracle may certify absence of violated rounded capacity cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search customer subsets for a rounded capacity cut whose fractional boundary is too small; only exact search certifies that none is violated.
assumptions_latex: Routes start and end at the depot and carry total demand at most \(Q\).
Edge variables count undirected route traversals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every subset with \(s(S)<0\) yields a violated rounded capacity inequality.

notation.meaning: Edges with exactly one endpoint in \(S\).
Minimum number of vehicles required to serve \(S\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rounded capacity inequality is standard and the exact-versus-heuristic qualification is appropriate, but its precise CVRP assumptions and formula lack a citation.

children.title: Connectivity Separation
children.top_down_role: Detection of violated connectivity requirements in network models.

knowledge_statements.title: Connectivity Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum-cut separation of undirected two-edge connectivity inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\), a designated root \(r\in V\), and nonnegative fractional edge capacities \(\bar x\), compute a minimum \(r\)-\(v\) cut for every \(v\in V\setminus\{r\}\). If some cut \(\delta(S)\) has \(\bar x(\delta(S))<2\), output the violated connectivity inequality \(x(\delta(S))\ge2\). If every computed minimum-cut value is at least \(2\), certify that all inequalities \(x(\delta(S))\ge2\) for nonempty proper \(S\subset V\) are satisfied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use rooted minimum cuts to find a vertex subset with boundary value below two or certify all two-edge-connectivity cuts.
assumptions_latex: Every feasible integer solution is a connected Eulerian spanning subgraph, hence crosses each proper cut at least twice.
\(\bar x_e\ge0\) for all \(e\in E\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Rooted minimum cuts exactly separate the stated two-edge-connectivity inequalities.

notation.meaning: Edges crossing the vertex cut \((S,V\setminus S)\).

children.title: Comb Separation
children.top_down_role: Separation of comb-structured inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Comb Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact family-level separation of symmetric traveling-salesperson comb inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fractional edge vector \(\bar x\) on the complete undirected graph, optimize over a handle \(H\) and an odd number \(t\ge3\) of pairwise disjoint teeth \(T_1,\ldots,T_t\), where \(T_j\cap H\ne\varnothing\) and \(T_j\setminus H\ne\varnothing\). Minimize \[\bar x(\delta(H))+\sum_{j=1}^t\bar x(\delta(T_j))-(3t+1).\] If the optimum is negative, output the corresponding comb inequality \(x(\delta(H))+\sum_{j=1}^t x(\delta(T_j))\ge3t+1\); otherwise certify nonviolation only if the optimization was exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search valid handles and an odd number of disjoint teeth; negative slack identifies a violated symmetric TSP comb inequality.
assumptions_latex: The integer solutions are Hamiltonian cycles in an undirected graph.
The separation oracle enforces all displayed handle-and-teeth conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible comb structure with negative objective gives a violated comb inequality.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed symmetric TSP comb inequality and structural conditions are plausible, but no authoritative source supports the exact formula, admissible comb family, or exact separation claim.

children.title: Network-Structure Recognition
children.top_down_role: Identification of graph features used by routing-specific separators.

knowledge_statements.title: Network-Structure Recognition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recognition of directed node-arc incidence structure in a constraint matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), seek nonzero row scalings and positive column scalings that transform every column into one of two forms: exactly one entry \(+1\) and one entry \(-1\), or a single entry \(+1\) or \(-1\). For a two-entry column, create a directed arc from its \(-1\) row to its \(+1\) row; attach single-entry columns to an added root row. Accept precisely when all scaling requirements are mutually consistent, and return the resulting directed graph and scaling certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scale rows and columns to node-arc incidence form, interpreting two-entry columns as arcs and single-entry columns as arcs incident to an added root.
assumptions_latex: Only nonzero row scalings and positive column scalings are permitted.
The recognized form is directed node-arc incidence, possibly with one row deleted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Acceptance supplies explicit scalings and a graph whose reduced node-arc incidence matrix equals the transformed matrix.

children.title: Logical Conflict Cut System
children.top_down_role: Cuts learned from infeasible search states, propagation histories, and logical implications.

children.title: Conflict-Cut Learning
children.top_down_role: Generation of cuts from infeasible search states.

knowledge_statements.title: Conflict-Cut Learning
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clause learning from a propagation conflict in a binary branch-and-cut search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent the truth value of each binary literal \(\ell\) by \([\ell]=x_i\) when \(\ell\) is \(x_i\), and by \([\ell]=1-x_i\) when \(\ell\) is \(\neg x_i\). Starting from a valid conflict clause, repeatedly resolve a current-decision-level propagated literal with its recorded valid reason clause on complementary occurrences of that literal until the chosen stopping rule, such as one remaining current-level literal, is met. If \(L\) is the set of literals in the resulting learned clause, output the conflict cut \[\sum_{\ell\in L}[\ell]\ge1.\] Backtrack to a level at which this inequality propagates, add it to the relaxation, and stop when no conflict remains or the root node is proved infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resolve the conflict clause with valid propagation reasons, encode the learned clause by requiring at least one learned literal to be true, add the inequality, and backtrack to an asserting level.
assumptions_latex: The initial conflict clause and every recorded reason clause are valid consequences of the binary model.
Each resolution step uses complementary occurrences of the same binary literal.
The learned clause is falsified by the conflicting partial assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The learned inequality excludes the conflicting assignment while remaining valid for every feasible binary solution.

notation.meaning: Set of literals in the learned clause.

children.title: Implication-Cut Extraction
children.top_down_role: Generation of inequalities from logical implications.

knowledge_statements.title: Implication-Cut Extraction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary encoding of a frontier implication whose simultaneous literals force infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Starting from an infeasibility vertex, repeatedly replace a propagated literal by the antecedent literals in one of its recorded reason constraints. Stop when the chosen frontier \(S\) contains only decision literals or literals retained by the learning scheme. If the recorded implications establish \(\bigwedge_{\ell\in S}\ell\Rightarrow\bot\), output
\[
\sum_{\ell\in S}z_\ell\le |S|-1.
\]
Equivalently, at least one frontier literal must be false. Attach the cut to every branching or local-bound assumption on which a reason used during extraction depends.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resolve the recorded reasons for infeasibility back to a frontier of literals, then forbid those frontier literals from being simultaneously true.
assumptions_latex: The current infeasible subproblem has a finite implication graph whose arcs are labeled by valid reason constraints.
Each frontier literal \(\ell\) has a binary truth indicator \(z_\ell\in\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality \(\sum_{\ell\in S}z_\ell\le |S|-1\) is a valid logical conflict cut under the assumptions used to derive the implication graph.

notation.meaning: Selected frontier literals whose simultaneous truth implies infeasibility.

children.title: Propagation-History Analysis
children.top_down_role: Use of recorded propagation causes as cut-learning evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Propagation-History Analysis
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reason-graph analysis for conflict learning in a branch-and-cut node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Construct \(G=(V,E)\) with one vertex for each decision, propagated literal, and conflict; add \((u,v)\in E\) when literal \(u\) occurs in the recorded reason that inferred \(v\). Initialize the active frontier with the conflict's immediate antecedents. Process active propagated literals in reverse inference order, replacing a selected literal by its reason antecedents and recording every node-local assumption used. Stop according to a specified frontier rule, such as one remaining literal from the latest decision level. Output the frontier \(F\), its accumulated validity context, and the induced conflict constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Traverse propagation reasons backward from a conflict, replacing inferred literals by antecedents until a selected learning frontier is reached.
assumptions_latex: Every propagated literal has a recorded reason constraint valid in the subproblem where propagation occurred.
The propagation history is finite and acyclic after ordering literals by inference time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Backward traversal identifies a frontier whose conjunction, together with its recorded validity context, implies the detected conflict.

notation.meaning: Set of frontier literals after backward analysis.

children.title: Logical-Cut Validity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Scope restrictions governing cuts learned from local logical information.

knowledge_statements.title: Logical-Cut Validity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes globally reusable logical cuts from cuts valid only below a search-tree node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose propagation under context \(H\) yields a learned inequality \(a^\top x\le\beta\) and establishes only \(P\cap H\subseteq\{x:a^\top x\le\beta\}\). Then the inequality may be enforced at the deriving node and at descendants whose domains imply \(H\). It may be inserted into the global cut pool only when the derivation also proves \(P\subseteq\{x:a^\top x\le\beta\}\). Removing a branching literal or local bound from the learned explanation without a replacement derivation can invalidate the cut outside \(H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conflict cut depending on local decisions or bounds is valid only where those assumptions hold unless separate global validity is proved.
assumptions_latex: A learned cut is derived from globally valid constraints and from a context \(H\) of branching decisions or locally tightened bounds.
The derivation proves \(P\cap H\subseteq\{x:a^\top x\le\beta\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cut is valid on \(P\cap H\); it is globally valid only if validity on all of \(P\) is established independently.

children.title: Cut Generation-Separation Pipeline

children.title: Cut-Generation Representations
children.top_down_role: Computational representations from which candidate inequalities are generated.

children.title: Simplex-Tableau Generation
children.top_down_role: Basis-dependent cut generation from simplex tableaux.

knowledge_statements.title: Simplex-Tableau Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basis-dependent intersection-cut generation from a simplex tableau cone and a split disjunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
From the current basis, write the corner relaxation as \(x=\bar x+\sum_{j\in N}r^j s_j\), where \(s_j\ge0\). Choose a split \(\pi^\top x\le\pi_0\) or \(\pi^\top x\ge\pi_0+1\) whose open slab contains \(\bar x\). For each ray define
\[
t_j:=\inf\{t>0:\bar x+t r^j\text{ lies on the split boundary}\}.
\]
Generate \(\sum_{j\in N}s_j/t_j\ge1\), translate it through the tableau into the original variables, and retain it when it violates the current LP solution and passes numerical acceptance tests.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use a simplex tableau cone and a violated split to compute ray-boundary intersections, yielding an intersection cut in nonbasic variables.
assumptions_latex: A simplex basis gives a vertex \(\bar x\) and tableau cone \(x=\bar x+\sum_{j\in N}r^j s_j\) with \(s_j\ge0\).
The vertex violates a split disjunction and every relevant ray meets its boundary at a finite positive parameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generated inequality \(\sum_{j\in N}s_j/t_j\ge1\) is valid for points in the tableau cone satisfying the split disjunction and cuts off \(\bar x\).

notation.meaning: Nonbasic ray variables and tableau rays.
First positive parameter at which ray j reaches the split boundary.

children.top_down_role: Generation from aggregated constraints, bounds, and reduced relaxations.

children.title: Row Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Formation of cut sources from combinations of model rows.

knowledge_statements.title: Row Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative aggregation of valid inequality rows before a cut-generating transformation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P:=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:a_i^\top x\le b_i,\ i=1,\ldots,m\}\) and any \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\), define \(\bar a:=\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i a_i\) and \(\bar b:=\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i b_i\). Then every \(x\in P\) satisfies \(\bar a^\top x\le\bar b\). Row aggregation uses this valid surrogate row as input to a subsequent integrality-based operation, such as rounding, disjunctive separation, or construction of a single-row relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative linear combination of valid inequality rows is valid and can serve as the source row for later cut generation.
assumptions_latex: The relaxation contains inequalities \(a_i^\top x\le b_i\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\).
Aggregation multipliers satisfy \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The aggregate \((\sum_i\lambda_i a_i)^\top x\le\sum_i\lambda_i b_i\) is valid for the relaxation and hence for its mixed-integer feasible subset.

notation.meaning: Aggregated coefficient vector and right-hand side.

children.title: Bound-Augmented Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Aggregation regimes incorporating variable-bound information.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Augmented Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregation treating variable bounds as explicit valid rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Represent upper bounds as \(x\le u\) and lower bounds as \(-x\le-\ell\). For any \(\lambda\ge0\), \(p\ge0\), and \(q\ge0\), nonnegative aggregation gives
\[
(\lambda^\top A+p^\top-q^\top)x\le \lambda^\top b+p^\top u-q^\top\ell.
\]
A bound-augmented generation procedure selects these multipliers, forms this surrogate inequality, and applies its chosen integrality-based cut rule. Bounds used in a globally stored cut must be globally valid; locally tightened bounds restrict the resulting cut to their validity subtree unless subsequently eliminated by a global derivation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add variable-bound rows to structural rows before aggregation, while preserving whether each bound is globally or only locally valid.
assumptions_latex: The relaxation includes \(Ax\le b\) and valid finite bounds \(\ell\le x\le u\).
The multipliers \(\lambda\), \(p\), and \(q\) are componentwise nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The bound-augmented aggregate \((\lambda^\top A+p^\top-q^\top)x\le\lambda^\top b+p^\top u-q^\top\ell\) is valid for the bounded relaxation.

notation.meaning: Multipliers for upper- and lower-bound rows.

children.title: Reduced-Relaxation Generation
children.top_down_role: Generation from restricted or simplified relaxation representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Relaxation Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut generation on a selected relaxation that still contains the original feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a reference point \(\bar x\notin X\), select a subset or aggregation of structural rows, integrality restrictions, and valid bounds defining \(R\) with \(X\subseteq R\). Invoke a separator for \(R\). If it returns \(a^\top x\le\beta\) satisfying \(a^\top x\le\beta\) for every \(x\in R\) and \(a^\top\bar x>\beta\), add that inequality to the original relaxation. If no such inequality is found, report failure for the selected reduced relaxation, not membership of \(\bar x\) in \(\operatorname{conv}(X)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separate over a smaller, tractable relaxation containing the feasible set; any resulting valid inequality remains valid for the original problem.
assumptions_latex: The original mixed-integer feasible set is \(X=P\cap(\mathbb Z^I\times\mathbb R^{n-|I|})\).
A tractable reduced relaxation \(R\) satisfies \(X\subseteq R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every inequality valid for \(R\) is valid for \(X\), although omitting constraints can weaken the obtainable separation.

children.title: Aggregation-Quality Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural criteria for choosing useful aggregated sources.

knowledge_statements.title: Aggregation-Quality Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact strength ordering induced by containment of aggregation-based generation relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For any set \(R\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let
\[
\mathcal V(R):=\{(a,\beta):a^\top x\le\beta\text{ for all }x\in R\}.
\]
If \(X\subseteq R_2\subseteq R_1\), then
\[
\mathcal V(R_1)\subseteq\mathcal V(R_2)\subseteq\mathcal V(X).
\]
Thus retaining more constraining information, or optimizing over a richer admissible aggregation class, defines a weakly stronger exact generation regime. This ordering concerns attainable validity and separation only; it does not assert superior running time, sparsity, conditioning, or branch-and-cut performance for the richer regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested generation relaxations induce the reverse ordering on valid cuts, though stronger exact separation may cost more or behave worse numerically.
assumptions_latex: Two generation relaxations satisfy \(X\subseteq R_2\subseteq R_1\).
Both cut families contain all linear inequalities valid for their respective relaxations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The valid-inequality family of \(R_1\) is contained in that of \(R_2\); the tighter regime cannot be weaker under exact separation.

children.title: Cut-Generating Linear Programs
children.top_down_role: Optimization-based representations for cuts obtained from disjunctions.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Generating Linear Programs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier representation of inequalities valid for a finite union of polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A cut-generating linear program uses variables \((\alpha,\beta,u^1,\ldots,u^k)\) satisfying, for every \(h\),
\[
\alpha=(A^h)^\top u^h,\qquad \beta\le(b^h)^\top u^h,\qquad u^h\ge0.
\]
These constraints imply \(\alpha^\top x\ge\beta\) for every \(x\in P_h\) and hence for every \(x\in D\). Add a normalization excluding positive rescaling, then minimize \(\alpha^\top\bar x-\beta\). A negative optimum supplies a cut separating \(\bar x\); a nonnegative optimum certifies only that this normalized CGLP found no violated represented cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A CGLP finds common nonnegative multiplier representations over every disjunct and optimizes the resulting normalized cut's violation.
assumptions_latex: The disjunctive set is \(D=\bigcup_{h=1}^kP_h\), with \(P_h=\{x:A^h x\ge b^h\}\).
The reference point \(\bar x\) is to be separated from \(\operatorname{conv}(D)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every feasible CGLP solution defines \(\alpha^\top x\ge\beta\) valid for \(D\); an objective minimizing \(\alpha^\top\bar x-\beta\) searches for a violated normalized cut.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 9. Solving CGLP_k on the LP Simplex Tableau p. 107
10.2 Most Violated Cut Selection Rule p. 126

children.title: Lattice-Free Intersection-Cut Geometry
children.top_down_role: Generation through lattice-free geometry and intersection constructions.

children.title: Lattice-Free Geometry
children.top_down_role: Geometric structures used as sources for valid cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Lattice-Free Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mixed-integer lattice-free convex sets in the original variable space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the mixed-integer set by \(M_I:=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:x_i\in\mathbb Z\text{ for every }i\in I\}\). A convex set \(L\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) with nonempty interior is lattice-free relative to \(M_I\) if
\[
\operatorname{int}(L)\cap M_I=\varnothing.
\]
It is maximal lattice-free if no convex lattice-free set relative to \(M_I\) properly contains it. For pure-integer geometry, \(I=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and \(M_I=\mathbb Z^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex set is lattice-free when its interior contains no point satisfying the specified integer-coordinate restrictions; maximality means inclusion-wise maximal.
assumptions_latex: The integer variables occupy coordinates indexed by \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A convex set is lattice-free precisely when its interior contains no point satisfying the designated integrality restrictions.

notation.meaning: Mixed-integer set associated with integer coordinates I.

children.title: Intersection-Cut Construction
children.top_down_role: Cut generation from intersections between relaxation geometry and excluded regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Intersection-Cut Construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical intersection cut for a simplicial or finitely generated corner cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each ray define \(t_j:=\sup\{t\ge0:\bar x+t r^j\in L\}\) and assume \(0<t_j<\infty\). Then every point \(x=\bar x+\sum_{j=1}^q r^j s_j\) in \(C\cap M_I\) satisfies
\[
\sum_{j=1}^q\frac{s_j}{t_j}\ge1.
\]
This is the intersection cut determined by the first boundary intersection of each cone ray with \(L\), and it excludes the apex \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersect every cone ray with a lattice-free set's boundary; reciprocal exit distances define a valid inequality excluding the cone apex.
assumptions_latex: A pointed cone is represented by \(C=\{\bar x+\sum_{j=1}^q r^j s_j:s\ge0\}\).
A closed convex lattice-free set \(L\) contains \(\bar x\) in its interior, and each cone ray exits \(L\) at a finite positive parameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality \(\sum_{j=1}^q s_j/t_j\ge1\) is valid for \(C\cap M_I\) and excludes the apex \(\bar x\).

notation.meaning: Apex and rays of the corner cone.
First exit parameter of ray j from L.
Mixed-integer set defining the integrality restrictions.

children.title: Geometric Source Selection
children.top_down_role: Choice of geometric objects used for cut generation.

knowledge_statements.title: Geometric Source Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-family selection of a lattice-free source using normalized violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(L\in\mathcal L\), compute its ray exit parameters, construct the associated inequality \(a_L^\top x\ge\beta_L\), and scale it by a fixed normalization \(\nu(a_L,\beta_L)=1\). Evaluate the signed slack \(\sigma_L:=a_L^\top\bar x-\beta_L\). Choose \(L^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{L\in\mathcal L}\sigma_L\) and output its cut when \(\sigma_{L^\star}<0\); otherwise report no violated cut in \(\mathcal L\). Ties may be resolved by sparsity or numerical conditioning without changing validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generate normalized intersection cuts from candidate lattice-free sets and select the one with greatest violation at the current fractional point.
assumptions_latex: A finite candidate family \(\mathcal L\) consists of lattice-free convex sets containing the fractional apex \(\bar x\) in their interiors.
Each candidate yields finite exit parameters on all cone rays and a computable intersection cut.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Selecting a candidate minimizing its normalized cut activity at the reference point returns the most violated cut within the enumerated family and normalization.

notation.meaning: Finite family of admissible lattice-free source sets.
Intersection cut generated from source L.

source_refs.locator: 10.2 Most Violated Cut Selection Rule p. 126

source_witnesses.locator: 10.2 Most Violated Cut Selection Rule p. 126

children.title: Intersection-Construction Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Representational and computational limits of geometric generation.

assumptions_latex: \(P=\{\bar x+Rs:s\in\mathbb R_+^k\}\), where \(R=(r^1,\ldots,r^k)\).
\(L\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is closed and convex, \(\bar x\in\operatorname{int}L\), and every designated integer-feasible point in \(P\) lies outside \(\operatorname{int}L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{j=1}^k s_j/t_j\ge 1\) is valid precisely under the stated exclusion condition, with coefficient \(0\) when \(t_j=+\infty\).

notation.meaning: Maximum distance along ray \(r^j\) that remains in \(L\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary conditions for a corner-polyhedron intersection cut, including rays that never leave the lattice-free set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each ray define \(t_j:=\sup\{t\ge 0:\bar x+tr^j\in L\}\), using \(1/(+\infty)=0\). Every designated integer-feasible point \(x=\bar x+Rs\) satisfies the intersection inequality \[\sum_{j=1}^k\frac{s_j}{t_j}\ge 1.\] A ray contained in \(L\) contributes zero and therefore cannot alone produce separation. The construction loses validity if \(L\) contains a designated integer-feasible point in its interior; without the ray representation, the displayed inequality applies only to points represented by \(s\ge0\). Thus lattice-freeness relative to the designated feasible set and coverage by the corner cone are essential boundaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The intersection cut is valid only when the chosen convex set excludes all relevant integer-feasible points from its interior and the corner rays represent those points.
knowledge_statements.title: Intersection-Construction Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The boundary role and intersection-cut formula are plausible, but no citation supports the lattice-free hypotheses, infinite-ray convention, or the claim that the exclusion condition is precise. A specific intersection-cut theorem or section is required.

children.title: Extended-Space Cut Generation Family
children.top_down_role: Cut generation in higher-dimensional representations followed by projection or recovery.

children.title: Lifted-Space Generation
children.top_down_role: Cut generation after introducing auxiliary dimensions or lifted variables.

assumptions_latex: \(Q\subseteq\mathbb R^{n+q}\) is a relaxation of a lifted feasible set \(S^L\), with \(S=\operatorname{proj}_x(S^L)\).
A candidate point \(\bar x\) has a lift \(\bar y\) satisfying \((\bar x,\bar y)\in Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is a valid lifted inequality violated by \((\bar x,\bar y)\), or a declaration that the selected oracle found none.

notation.meaning: Lifted feasible set in original and auxiliary variables.
Violation of a lifted inequality at the candidate lift.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic cut generation directly in an auxiliary-variable formulation.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Disjunctive Programming and Extended Formulations p. 69

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(Q\), \((\bar x,\bar y)\in Q\), a normalized family \(\mathcal F\) of inequalities \(\alpha^\top x+\gamma^\top y\le\beta\) valid for \(S^L\), a tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), and a separation oracle. Initialize the incumbent violation to \(0\). The oracle searches \(\mathcal F\) and updates the incumbent whenever \(v(\alpha,\gamma,\beta):=\alpha^\top\bar x+\gamma^\top\bar y-\beta\) increases. Stop according to the oracle's exactness or resource rule. If the incumbent exceeds \(\varepsilon\), output its lifted inequality and add it to \(Q\); otherwise report that this oracle produced no cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a lift of the current point, search a normalized family of lifted valid inequalities, and add one whose violation exceeds tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Lifted-Space Generation

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Disjunctive Programming and Extended Formulations p. 69

children.title: Extended-Formulation Generation
children.top_down_role: Generation within explicit extended formulations.

assumptions_latex: For \(i=1,\ldots,m\), \(P_i=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:A_i x\le b_i\}\) is a nonempty polytope.
The disjunctive feasible set is \(S=\bigcup_{i=1}^m P_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=\operatorname{conv}(S)\).

notation.meaning: Scaled copy of the original vector for disjunct \(i\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-hull extended formulation for a finite union of nonempty polytopes.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Disjunctive Programming and Extended Formulations p. 69
4.5.2 A Tighter Disjunctive Programming Formulation p. 65

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Introduce variables \(x^i\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\lambda_i\ge0\) for every disjunct. Define \[Q:=\left\{(x,x^1,\ldots,x^m,\lambda):x=\sum_{i=1}^m x^i,\ A_i x^i\le b_i\lambda_i,\ \sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i=1,\ \lambda\ge0\right\}.\] Then \[\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=\operatorname{conv}\left(\bigcup_{i=1}^mP_i\right).\] Consequently, linear inequalities may be generated from the extended system and subsequently projected or aggregated to obtain valid inequalities for the disjunctive hull in the original variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Disaggregate the original vector by disjunct and weight each polytope's constraints; projecting the resulting extended system gives the convex hull of the union.
knowledge_statements.title: Extended-Formulation Generation

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Disjunctive Programming and Extended Formulations p. 69
4.5.2 A Tighter Disjunctive Programming Formulation p. 65

children.title: Original-Space Projection
children.top_down_role: Transfer of generated inequalities back to the original variable space.

assumptions_latex: \(Q^c=\{(x,y):Ax+By\le d,\ \alpha^\top x+\gamma^\top y\le\beta\}\) is a nonempty polyhedron.
Projection is taken onto the original variable block \(x\in\mathbb R^n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The generated system \(Hx\le h\) satisfies \(\{x:Hx\le h\}=\operatorname{proj}_x(Q^c)\).

notation.meaning: Lifted relaxation after adding a generated cut.
An original-space inequality description of the projection.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact polyhedral elimination of auxiliary variables after adding a lifted cut.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Disjunctive Programming and Extended Formulations p. 69
6.6 The Complexity of Extended Formulations p. 105

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an inequality description of \(Q^c\) and an elimination order for \(y\). Initialize the working system with all inequalities defining \(Q^c\). Eliminate each component of \(y\) by an exact polyhedral projection procedure, such as Fourier--Motzkin elimination, removing redundant inequalities when this can be certified. After all auxiliary variables have been eliminated, output \(Hx\le h\). The stopping condition is exhaustion of the auxiliary-variable block, and correctness requires \[\{x:Hx\le h\}=\{x:\exists y\text{ with }(x,y)\in Q^c\}=\operatorname{proj}_x(Q^c).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminate every auxiliary variable from the cut-strengthened lifted polyhedron and output an inequality system describing exactly its projection in the original variables.
knowledge_statements.title: Original-Space Projection

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Disjunctive Programming and Extended Formulations p. 69
6.6 The Complexity of Extended Formulations p. 105

children.title: Lifted-Cut Recovery
children.top_down_role: Recovery and representation of useful cuts derived in higher dimensions.

assumptions_latex: \(Q=\{(x,y):Ax+By\le d\}\) and \(\alpha^\top x+\gamma^\top y\le\beta\) is a valid lifted cut.
Multipliers satisfy \(\mu\ge0\), \(\tau\ge0\), and \(\mu^\top B+\tau\gamma^\top=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\mu^\top A+\tau\alpha^\top)x\le\mu^\top d+\tau\beta\) is valid for \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q^c)\).

notation.meaning: Nonnegative multipliers for the lifted formulation rows.
Nonnegative multiplier for the lifted cut.
Lifted polyhedron strengthened by the cut.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier certificate recovering an original-space cut from a lifted inequality.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 5. Disjunctive Programming and Extended Formulations p. 69

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q^c:=Q\cap\{(x,y):\alpha^\top x+\gamma^\top y\le\beta\}\). A pair \((\mu,\tau)\) satisfying \(\mu\ge0\), \(\tau\ge0\), and \(\mu^\top B+\tau\gamma^\top=0\) certifies cancellation of every auxiliary-variable coefficient. Aggregating the rows of \(Q\) with \(\mu\) and the lifted cut with \(\tau\) yields \[(\mu^\top A+\tau\alpha^\top)x\le\mu^\top d+\tau\beta.\] This inequality is directly checkable and valid for \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q^c)\). It is a separating recovered cut for \(\bar x\) exactly when its left side at \(\bar x\) exceeds its right side.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative row multipliers that cancel all auxiliary coefficients certify a valid original-space inequality recovered from the lifted formulation and lifted cut.
knowledge_statements.title: Lifted-Cut Recovery

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 5. Disjunctive Programming and Extended Formulations p. 69

children.title: Separation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Separation systems classified by completeness and computational organization.

children.title: Exact Separation
children.top_down_role: Complete resolution of a designated separation problem.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact separation relative to a designated normalized inequality family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\varepsilon\ge0\), and \(\mathcal F\). Compute exactly \[v^*:=\max_{(a,b)\in\mathcal F}\{a^\top\bar x-b\}.\] If \(v^*>\varepsilon\), output an attaining inequality \(a^\top x\le b\); it is valid for \(S\) and violated by \(\bar x\). If \(v^*\le\varepsilon\), stop with the certificate that no member of \(\mathcal F\) is violated beyond tolerance. Exactness refers to complete resolution over the designated family, not necessarily over every valid inequality for \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact separator completely maximizes violation over its designated cut family, returning a violated cut or certifying that none exceeds tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
\(\mathcal F\) is a normalized family of inequalities \(a^\top x\le b\) valid for \(S\).
The maximum of \(a^\top\bar x-b\) over \((a,b)\in\mathcal F\) is attained and can be resolved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The oracle returns a violated member of \(\mathcal F\) or certifies that \(a^\top\bar x\le b+\varepsilon\) for every \((a,b)\in\mathcal F\).

children.title: Heuristic Separation
children.top_down_role: Incomplete but economical discovery of useful violated cuts.

assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal F\) contains only inequalities valid for \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
A search rule examines a budget-dependent subset \(\mathcal F_B(\bar x)\subseteq\mathcal F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every returned cut is valid, but failure to return one does not certify \(a^\top\bar x\le b+\varepsilon\) for all \((a,b)\in\mathcal F\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Budgeted, incomplete separation with validity preserved but no completeness certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(\bar x\), a budget \(B\), a tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), and a validity-preserving generator for \(\mathcal F\). Initialize an empty incumbent. Until budget \(B\) is exhausted, generate candidates in \(\mathcal F_B(\bar x)\), evaluate \(a^\top\bar x-b\), and retain a candidate of largest observed violation. Output the incumbent if its violation exceeds \(\varepsilon\); otherwise output no cut. Because only \(\mathcal F_B(\bar x)\) is searched, a no-cut outcome does not imply that \(\bar x\) satisfies every inequality in \(\mathcal F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A heuristic separator searches only budget-selected valid cuts; returned cuts remain valid, but a no-cut outcome is not a separation certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Heuristic Separation

children.title: Combinatorial Search Separation Family
children.top_down_role: Structured searches over combinatorial inequality families.

children.title: Explicit Enumerative Separation
children.top_down_role: Search over explicitly represented members of an inequality family.

knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Enumerative Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete linear scan of a finite, explicitly materialized cut family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\varepsilon\ge0\), and the explicit nonempty list \(\mathcal C\). Initialize \(i^*=1\) and \(v^*=a_1^\top\bar x-b_1\). For \(i=2,\ldots,N\), compute \(v_i:=a_i^\top\bar x-b_i\) and update \((i^*,v^*)\) whenever \(v_i>v^*\). After the final candidate, output \(a_{i^*}^\top x\le b_{i^*}\) if \(v^*>\varepsilon\); otherwise certify that no member of \(\mathcal C\) is violated beyond tolerance. The method is exact for the designated family precisely when \(\mathcal C\) lists that family completely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate every cut in a nonempty finite explicit list and return the most violated one, or certify that no listed cut exceeds tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
\(\mathcal C=\{(a_i,b_i):i=1,\ldots,N\}\), with \(N\ge1\), is a finite list of inequalities valid for \(S\).
Each candidate's violation at \(\bar x\) can be evaluated exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns an index maximizing \(a_i^\top\bar x-b_i\), or certifies that no listed inequality is violated beyond \(\varepsilon\).

children.title: Implicit Enumerative Separation
children.top_down_role: Structured enumeration without materializing the full candidate family.

knowledge_statements.title: Implicit Enumerative Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tree search over cuts represented implicitly rather than stored as a complete list.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\varepsilon\ge0\), and the root of \(T\). Initialize a live-node set with the root and incumbent violation \(v^*=-\infty\). Repeatedly select a live node \(u\). Prune it when \(U(u)\le\max\{v^*,\varepsilon\}\); otherwise expand it, or evaluate and update the incumbent if it is a leaf. If no live nodes remain, return the incumbent when \(v^*>\varepsilon\); otherwise certify that no leaf inequality is violated beyond tolerance. Exhaustive completion with valid bounds is exact for the separation decision and returns a maximally violated leaf whenever the maximum violation exceeds \(\varepsilon\). Stopping at a resource limit provides no completeness certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search an implicit tree of cuts using valid violation bounds; exhaustive completion decides separation exactly and recovers a most violated cut when one exceeds tolerance, while early termination is heuristic.
assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
Candidate cuts are leaves of a finite rooted search tree \(T\), and every leaf inequality is valid for \(S\).
Each node \(u\) has a valid upper bound \(U(u)\) on the violations attainable by its descendant leaves.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exhaustive termination certifies whether any leaf violation exceeds \(\varepsilon\) and returns a maximally violated leaf when the maximum exceeds \(\varepsilon\); resource-limited termination remains heuristic.

notation.meaning: Upper bound on descendant violation at node \(u\).

children.title: Dynamic-Programming Separation
children.top_down_role: State-based structured search for violated inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic-Programming Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact separation when cut violation admits a finite-state additive decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(G=(V,E)\), its source \(s\in V\), its nonempty terminal set \(V_T\subseteq V\), \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\varepsilon\ge0\). Set \(D(s)=0\) and \(D(v)=-\infty\) for \(v\ne s\). Process states in topological order using \[D(v):=\max_{(u,v)\in E}\{D(u)+w_{uv}(\bar x)\},\] storing an attaining predecessor whenever \(D(v)\) is finite. After all reachable terminal states are processed, let \(D^*:=\max_{t\in V_T}D(t)\). If \(D^*>\varepsilon\), backtrack from an attaining terminal and output the cut encoded by that path; otherwise certify that no represented cut is violated beyond tolerance. Exactness requires the graph to represent every candidate and each path reward to equal the encoded cut's violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximize additive cut violation over source-to-terminal paths in an acyclic state graph; terminal values decide separation and predecessor backtracking reconstructs a most violated represented cut.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite acyclic graph with designated source \(s\in V\) and nonempty terminal set \(V_T\subseteq V\).
Every candidate cut corresponds to a path from \(s\) to a member of \(V_T\), and every such encoded cut is valid for \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
The violation of an encoded cut at \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\) equals the sum of its transition rewards \(w_e(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The value \(\max_{t\in V_T}D(t)\) equals the maximum represented cut violation, and predecessor backtracking recovers an attaining cut when the value is finite.

notation.meaning: Maximum reward of a path from the source to state \(v\).

children.title: State-Space Complexity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Computational limits arising from enumeration size or dynamic-programming state growth.

assumptions_latex: An explicit family has \(N\) candidates with evaluation cost at most \(T_{\mathrm{eval}}\).
A dynamic program uses a finite acyclic graph \(G=(V,E)\) with constant-time transition updates.
Input integers are encoded in binary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Explicit scanning costs \(O(NT_{\mathrm{eval}})\), whereas the graph dynamic program costs \(O(|V|+|E|)\); these may be exponential or pseudo-polynomial in input length.

notation.meaning: State-transition graph used by dynamic programming.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Output-size and state-count boundaries for enumerative and dynamic-programming separators.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Problems, algorithms, and complexity p. 14
source_refs.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A complete explicit scan performs \(N\) candidate evaluations and has time \(O(NT_{\mathrm{eval}})\); without exploitable structure, an adversarial black-box list requires inspecting all \(N\) entries to certify no violation. An acyclic dynamic-programming separator has time \(O(|V|+|E|)\) and storage \(O(|V|)\). These bounds are polynomial only when \(N\), or respectively \(|V|+|E|\), is polynomial in the binary input length. If states index a numerical capacity \(W\), a bound polynomial in \(W\) is merely pseudo-polynomial and can be exponential in \(\log W\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Enumeration scales with the number of cuts; dynamic programming scales with its state graph, which may still be exponential or only pseudo-polynomial in encoded input size.
knowledge_statements.title: State-Space Complexity Boundaries

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Problems, algorithms, and complexity p. 14
source_witnesses.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

children.title: Optimization-Based Separation
children.top_down_role: Auxiliary optimization models used as separation engines.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimization-Based Separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Auxiliary optimization of cut violation over a parametrized valid-inequality family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(\varepsilon\ge0\), and an auxiliary model for the nonempty set \(U\). Solve \[v^*:=\max_{u\in U}\{a(u)^\top\bar x-b(u)\}.\] Maintain the best feasible parameter encountered. If a feasible \(u\) has value greater than \(\varepsilon\), its inequality \(a(u)^\top x\le b(u)\) is a valid separating cut and may be returned immediately. If the model is solved globally and \(v^*\le\varepsilon\), certify that no represented inequality is violated beyond tolerance. Local, truncated, or otherwise incomplete solution makes the procedure heuristic but does not compromise validity of returned cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimize cut violation over a nonempty auxiliary parameter model; a global attained optimum gives exact separation for the represented family, while incomplete solution is heuristic.
assumptions_latex: \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
The nonempty set \(U\) parametrizes normalized inequalities \(a(u)^\top x\le b(u)\) valid for \(S\).
The auxiliary model represents \(U\) and the violation function correctly, and the maximum violation over \(U\) is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A global optimizer returns an attaining parameter and gives exact separation over \(U\); any feasible \(u\) with objective above \(\varepsilon\) yields a valid separating cut.

notation.meaning: Nonempty feasible parameter set for candidate cuts.
Violation objective of parameter \(u\) at the query point.

children.title: Separation Complexity Boundary
children.top_down_role: Algorithmic consequences of separation complexity without duplicating the general optimization–separation theorem developed elsewhere.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

children.title: Polynomial-Separation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Cut families with theoretically tractable separation problems.

assumptions_latex: The cut family is indexed by rationally encoded instances \(I\), with relaxation \(P_I\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n(I)}\).
Candidate points and returned inequalities have binary encodings.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Membership in \(P_I\) can be decided, and a violated family inequality produced when necessary, in time polynomial in the input encoding length.

notation.meaning: Relaxation defined by the indexed cut family

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bit-complexity definition for rational polyhedral cut families.

source_refs.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cut family is in a polynomial-separation regime if an algorithm exists that, given \(I\) and \(\bar x\in\mathbb{Q}^{n(I)}\), either certifies \(\bar x\in P_I\) or returns a rational inequality \(a^Tx\leq b\), valid for \(P_I\), with \(a^T\bar x>b\). Its running time and the encoding length of \((a,b)\) must be bounded by a polynomial in the encoding length of \((I,\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A family is polynomially separable when membership or a polynomial-size violated cut can be produced in polynomial bit complexity.
knowledge_statements.title: Polynomial-Separation Regimes

source_witnesses.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

children.title: Hard-Separation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Cut families requiring restricted, approximate, or heuristic separation.

assumptions_latex: The cut family is indexed by rationally encoded instances \(I\), and \(P_I\) is the intersection of all inequalities in the indexed family.
Candidate points \(\bar x\in\mathbb{Q}^{n(I)}\) and returned inequalities have binary encodings.
The separation decision problem asks whether \(\bar x\in P_I\), equivalently whether an inequality in the family is violated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unless \(\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}\), no polynomial-time exact separator exists for all encoded instances of an NP-hard separation problem.

notation.meaning: Polyhedron defined as the intersection of the indexed family inequalities
Rational candidate point tested for separation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complexity boundary for exact separation; NP-hardness must be established separately for each concrete cut family.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. Problems, algorithms, and complexity p. 14
source_refs.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A cut family is in a hard-separation regime when deciding whether \(\bar x\in P_I\), equivalently whether some indexed family inequality is violated by \(\bar x\), is NP-hard under polynomial-time reductions. Unless \(\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}\), no polynomial-time exact separator then exists for all encoded instances. A polynomial-time routine must therefore restrict attention to a tractable instance class or subfamily, or be incomplete, approximate, or heuristic and possibly return no cut despite \(\bar x\notin P_I\). An unrestricted exact method may instead require superpolynomial time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact separation is a hard regime when its decision problem is NP-hard. Unless P equals NP, polynomial-time routines must restrict the problem or sacrifice completeness, while unrestricted exact methods may require superpolynomial time.
knowledge_statements.title: Hard-Separation Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. Problems, algorithms, and complexity p. 14
source_witnesses.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

children.title: Oracle-to-Implementation Gap
children.top_down_role: Boundary between theoretical oracle equivalence and effective solver separation.

assumptions_latex: The theoretical oracle uses exact rational arithmetic and polynomial-length encodings.
The oracle reduction counts arithmetic and bit operations but does not prescribe solver data structures.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Polynomial oracle complexity alone does not imply numerically stable or practically efficient separation.

notation.meaning: Rational point submitted to the separation oracle

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates bit-model oracle guarantees from numerical and engineering performance.

source_refs.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A polynomial-time separation oracle guarantees only that exact input \(\bar x\) yields, in polynomial bit complexity, either membership or an exactly valid separator \((a,b)\) of polynomial encoding length. This guarantee supplies no bound on hidden constants, floating-point conditioning, cut density, data conversion, or the cost of constructing the combinatorial structures used by an implementation. Consequently, replacing exact tests such as \(a^T\bar x>b\) by tolerance-based tests may alter the oracle's decisions unless rounding and validation errors are controlled explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oracle polynomiality is an exact bit-model result; it does not ensure stable, sparse, or fast separation in an actual solver.
knowledge_statements.title: Oracle-to-Implementation Gap

source_witnesses.source_title: Theory of Linear and Integer Programming

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact-bit-model versus numerical-implementation distinction fits this failure-boundary leaf, but the cited complexity section does not inspectably support the claims about conditioning, cut density, data conversion, solver structures, or tolerance behavior. A numerical optimization or solver implementation source with a specific locator is required.

children.title: Cut Strengthening-Postprocessing Pipeline
children.top_down_role: Transformations applied after generation and before selection or admission.

children.title: Lifting-Coefficient Strengthening Family
children.top_down_role: Families for improving the strength of generated inequalities.

children.title: Sequential Lifting
children.top_down_role: Coefficient extension organized by an ordering of omitted variables.

assumptions_latex: The feasible set satisfies \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\).
The inequality \(\sum_{i\in B}a_ix_i\leq b\) is valid on the face \(x_j=0\) for every \(j\notin B\).
Every lifting subproblem displayed below is feasible and attains its maximum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output inequality is valid for \(X\).

notation.meaning: Indices appearing in the initial face inequality

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Up-lifting of binary variables initially fixed to zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize with the valid face inequality and an order \((j_1,\ldots,j_k)\) for \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus B\). For \(t=1,\ldots,k\), set \[\alpha_t=b-\max\left\{\sum_{i\in B}a_ix_i+\sum_{s<t}\alpha_sx_{j_s}:x\in X,\ x_{j_t}=1,\ x_{j_s}=0\ \text{for }s>t\right\}.\] After the last update, output \[\sum_{i\in B}a_ix_i+\sum_{t=1}^k\alpha_tx_{j_t}\leq b.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lift fixed binary variables one at a time by solving an exact residual optimization problem for each coefficient.
knowledge_statements.title: Sequential Lifting

children.title: Simultaneous Lifting
children.top_down_role: Joint treatment of multiple variables during lifting.

assumptions_latex: The feasible set satisfies \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\).
The inequality \(\sum_{i\in B}a_ix_i\leq b\) is valid on the face defined by \(x_j=0\) for every \(j\in L\), where \(L=\{1,\ldots,n\}\setminus B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(\alpha\in\mathcal{L}\) produces a simultaneously lifted inequality valid for \(X\).

notation.meaning: Indices of variables absent from the initial face inequality
Vector of simultaneous lifting coefficients indexed by L
Feasible region of simultaneous lifting coefficients

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary simultaneous up-lifting represented by its feasible coefficient region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The simultaneous lifting region is \[\mathcal{L}=\left\{\alpha\in\mathbb{R}^{L}:\max_{x\in X}\left(\sum_{i\in B}a_ix_i+\sum_{j\in L}\alpha_jx_j\right)\leq b\right\}.\] Simultaneous lifting selects all coefficients at once from \(\mathcal{L}\) and returns \[\sum_{i\in B}a_ix_i+\sum_{j\in L}\alpha_jx_j\leq b.\] Unlike sequential lifting, this representation contains no ordering of \(L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Simultaneous lifting chooses a full coefficient vector whose augmented inequality remains valid over the original binary feasible set, without imposing an order on the lifted variables.
knowledge_statements.title: Simultaneous Lifting

children.title: Coefficient Tightening
children.top_down_role: Direct improvement of generated cut coefficients.

assumptions_latex: The set satisfies \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), and \(a^Tx\leq b\) is valid for \(X\).
The set \(\{x\in X:x_j=1\}\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing \(a_j\) by \(\widehat a_j\) preserves validity and dominates the original inequality on \([0,1]^n\).

notation.meaning: Largest valid coefficient with all other coefficients fixed

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact one-coordinate tightening for a binary less-than-or-equal cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Keeping \(b\) and every coefficient other than \(a_j\) fixed, compute \[\widehat a_j=b-\max\left\{\sum_{i\neq j}a_ix_i:x\in X,\ x_j=1\right\}.\] Validity of the original inequality gives \(\widehat a_j\geq a_j\). Replace \(a_j\) by \(\widehat a_j\) and output \[\sum_{i\neq j}a_ix_i+\widehat a_jx_j\leq b.\] The new inequality is valid for \(X\); because \(x_j\geq0\), it implies the original inequality throughout \([0,1]^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A binary cut coefficient is tightened to the largest value allowed by feasible points having that variable equal to one.
knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient Tightening

children.title: Lifting-Order Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Variation in strengthened cuts caused by lifting choices.

assumptions_latex: Sequential lifting is applied to a binary feasible set using the exact residual subproblems.
Two admissible orders \(\pi\) and \(\sigma\) contain the same variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Validity is order-independent, but the coefficient vector and resulting cut strength need not be order-independent.

notation.meaning: Coefficient vector generated under order pi
Coefficient vector generated under order sigma

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order dependence of exact sequential binary lifting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Each lifting coefficient is the residual slack after coefficients of earlier variables have been installed and later variables remain fixed. Hence changing the order changes the feasible objective in subsequent lifting subproblems. Both orders produce valid inequalities, but generally \(\alpha^{\pi}\neq\alpha^{\sigma}\), and neither resulting inequality need dominate the other on \([0,1]^n\). Order invariance holds when every variable's residual lifting value is unchanged by which other lifted variables were processed earlier; absent this marginal-invariance condition, equality of the outputs is not guaranteed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sequential lifting always preserves validity, but different variable orders can produce different and mutually incomparable strengthened cuts.
knowledge_statements.title: Lifting-Order Sensitivity

children.title: Cut Scaling-Normalization Calculus
children.top_down_role: Representational choices affecting cut comparison and numerical behavior.

children.title: Canonical Cut Normalization
children.top_down_role: Canonical representations used for comparison and storage.

assumptions_latex: The rational vector \((a,b)\in\mathbb{Q}^{n+1}\) is nonzero and represents \(a^Tx\leq b\).
Only positive scalar multiples are regarded as equivalent representations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The construction gives the unique primitive integer representative on the positive ray generated by \((a,b)\).

notation.meaning: Least common multiple of coefficient denominators
Greatest common divisor of the scaled integer entries

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: primitive integer normalization of a rational inequality is algebraically unambiguous
REQUEST_SOURCES: cut-normalization reference with an exact locator is absent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primitive-integer normalization for rational cuts with fixed inequality orientation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write every entry of \((a,b)\) in reduced rational form. Let \(d>0\) be the least common multiple of their positive denominators, let \(z=d(a,b)\in\mathbb{Z}^{n+1}\), and let \(g\) be the greatest common divisor of the absolute nonzero entries of \(z\). The canonical normalized cut is \[\frac{d}{g}a^Tx\leq\frac{d}{g}b.\] Its concatenated coefficient vector is integral and primitive. Multiplication by a negative scalar is excluded because it reverses the inequality orientation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clear rational denominators and divide by the common integer gcd to obtain the unique primitive representative of a cut's positive scaling class.
knowledge_statements.title: Canonical Cut Normalization

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The primitive-integer normalization is mathematically coherent and fits a definition container, but no inspectable source with a specific locator is supplied. Standard-field rationale alone does not satisfy the requested source review.

children.title: Coefficient Scaling
children.top_down_role: Rescaling choices intended to improve numerical behavior.

assumptions_latex: The inequality is \(a^Tx\leq b\) with \((a,b)\neq0\).
The scaling factor satisfies \(\lambda>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Positive coefficient-and-right-hand-side scaling preserves the cut halfspace, while all raw residuals scale by \(\lambda\).

notation.meaning: Signed cut residual at a candidate point

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: positive scaling invariance follows directly from ordered-field algebra
REQUEST_SOURCES: solver-oriented cut-scaling reference is absent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact-arithmetic invariance under common positive scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(\lambda>0\), the inequalities \[a^Tx\leq b\qquad\text{and}\qquad (\lambda a)^Tx\leq\lambda b\] define the same halfspace. At a point \(\bar x\), the signed residual becomes \((\lambda a)^T\bar x-\lambda b=\lambda r(\bar x)\), and the coefficient norm becomes \(\|\lambda a\|=\lambda\|a\|\) for every absolutely homogeneous norm. Thus feasibility and exact dominance are invariant, whereas unnormalized violation magnitudes and coefficient sizes are not.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplying every coefficient and the right-hand side by one positive factor preserves the cut but rescales residuals and norms.
knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient Scaling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The positive-scaling invariance and residual scaling claims are correct and fit a property container, but the record has no cited source or locator. A cut-scaling or numerical optimization reference is required.

children.title: Right-Hand-Side Scaling
children.top_down_role: Treatment of the cut right-hand side during rescaling.

assumptions_latex: The cut is \(a^Tx\leq b\) with \(b\neq0\).
The scaling factor must be positive to preserve orientation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Right-hand-side normalization by \(|b|\) preserves the halfspace and produces right-hand side \(\operatorname{sgn}(b)\).

notation.meaning: Sign of the nonzero right-hand side

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: normalization by a positive nonzero right-hand-side magnitude is elementary
REQUEST_SOURCES: exact cut-scaling locator is absent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalization using a nonzero right-hand side as the common scale.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Dividing the complete inequality by the positive quantity \(|b|\) gives the equivalent representation \[\left(\frac{a}{|b|}\right)^Tx\leq\frac{b}{|b|}=\operatorname{sgn}(b).\] If \(b>0\), the normalized right-hand side is \(1\); if \(b<0\), it is \(-1\). Dividing by \(b<0\) without reversing the comparison is invalid. When \(b=0\), right-hand-side normalization is undefined and a positive coefficient norm must supply the scale instead.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Divide the entire cut by the positive magnitude of a nonzero right-hand side, obtaining an equivalent cut with right-hand side plus or minus one.
knowledge_statements.title: Right-Hand-Side Scaling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Normalization by the positive quantity |b| is mathematically correct for nonzero b and the representation content kind fits the leaf, but no inspectable source with an exact locator is provided.

children.title: Scale-Sensitivity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Comparison and stability limits caused by poorly chosen scales.

assumptions_latex: A solver accepts a cut at \(\bar x\) when \(a^T\bar x-b>\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}+\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}s(a,b,\bar x)\).
The scale function is positively homogeneous: \(s(\lambda a,\lambda b,\bar x)=\lambda s(a,b,\bar x)\) for \(\lambda>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The numerical acceptance decision is scale-invariant exactly when the absolute tolerance is zero or is scaled by the same factor.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: boundary follows by substituting a positive scaled inequality into the tolerance test
REQUEST_SOURCES: numerical cut-validation reference is absent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of scaling invariance under mixed absolute-relative cut tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After common scaling by \(\lambda>0\), the test becomes \[\lambda(a^T\bar x-b)>\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}+\lambda\varepsilon_{\mathrm{rel}}s(a,b,\bar x).\] Dividing by \(\lambda\) changes the effective absolute tolerance to \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{abs}}/\lambda\). Therefore exact violation and purely relative tests are invariant under positive scaling, but a fixed nonzero absolute tolerance is not. Very small scaling may hide a genuinely violated cut, while very large scaling may expose residuals dominated by floating-point error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact cut validity is scale-invariant, but a fixed absolute violation tolerance changes its effective meaning when the cut is rescaled.
knowledge_statements.title: Scale-Sensitivity Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algebra showing how a fixed absolute tolerance changes under scaling is sound, but the phrase 'exactly when' needs explicit universal quantification over cuts, points, and positive scaling factors; individual decisions can coincide accidentally. The floating-point-error claim also needs a numerical validation source with a specific locator.

children.title: Cut Density-Coefficient Control System
children.top_down_role: Controls for density, dynamism, and encoding growth.

children.title: Support Sparsification
children.top_down_role: Reduction of cut support to control relaxation density.

assumptions_latex: The valid inequality is \(a^Tx\leq b\) for \(X\subseteq[\ell,u]\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
The index set \(S\) identifies coefficients to remove, and all relevant bounds are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sparsified inequality is valid for \(X\), although generally weaker than the original cut.

notation.meaning: Indices removed from the cut support
Minimum omitted contribution over the bounding box

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: validity follows from bounding the omitted linear terms over the variable box
REQUEST_SOURCES: cut-sparsification reference with strength analysis is absent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity-preserving support removal using finite variable bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute the lower bound on the omitted contribution \[L_S=\sum_{i\in S}\min\{a_i\ell_i,a_iu_i\}.\] Delete the coefficients indexed by \(S\), compensate the right-hand side, and output \[\sum_{i\notin S}a_ix_i\leq b-L_S.\] For every \(x\in X\), one has \(\sum_{i\in S}a_ix_i\geq L_S\); combining this bound with \(a^Tx\leq b\) establishes validity. The output has support at most \(n-|S|\), but compensation can substantially reduce separation strength.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Remove selected coefficients and compensate the right-hand side by the smallest omitted contribution allowed by the variable bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Support Sparsification

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The box-bound compensation formula preserves validity and appropriately describes a support-sparsification algorithm, but no source with a specific locator supports the construction or its strength claim.

children.title: Coefficient-Magnitude Control
children.top_down_role: Management of large or highly disparate coefficient magnitudes.

knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient-Magnitude Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational control after exact rational normalization; the threshold is an algorithm parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(d\) be the least positive integer such that \((da,d\beta)\in\mathbb Z^{n+1}\), and let \(g\) be the greatest common divisor of the absolute values of the entries of \((da,d\beta)\). Set \((\bar a,\bar\beta)=(da/g,d\beta/g)\). Because the inequality is represented with the fixed sense \(\le\), do not negate this tuple. Retain the cut only if \(\max\{\|\bar a\|_\infty,|\bar\beta|\}\le M\); otherwise reject it or replace it only by a separately validated inequality. This test is invariant under multiplication of the original cut by a positive rational scalar.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clear denominators using a positive multiplier, divide by the common integer factor without reversing the inequality, and retain the cut only when every primitive coefficient is within the prescribed magnitude limit.
assumptions_latex: The candidate cut is a rational inequality \(a^\top x\le \beta\) in \(n\) variables with \((a,\beta)\ne 0\).
A coefficient limit \(M\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1}\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The retained primitive integer representation satisfies \(\max\{\|\bar a\|_\infty,|\bar\beta|\}\le M\).

notation.meaning: Rational coefficient vector and right-hand side of the candidate cut.
Primitive integer coefficient vector and right-hand side with the original inequality orientation preserved.

children.title: Cut-Dynamism Control
children.top_down_role: Controls targeting extreme coefficient ratios.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Dynamism Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-invariant acceptance condition for numerical coefficient spread.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(S(a)=\{i:a_i\ne0\}\), define the cut dynamism by \[D(a)=\frac{\max_{i\in S(a)}|a_i|}{\min_{i\in S(a)}|a_i|}.\] The dynamism-control predicate accepts the cut only when \(D(a)\le\Delta\). Because \(D(\lambda a)=D(a)\) for every \(\lambda\ne0\), the exact test is independent of cut scaling. An implementation that removes numerically negligible coefficients must use a fixed scale-homogeneous support rule before evaluating the predicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut passes dynamism control when the largest nonzero coefficient divided by the smallest nonzero coefficient does not exceed a fixed threshold; any numerical support rule must preserve scaling.
assumptions_latex: The cut is \(a^\top x\le\beta\) with \(a\ne0\).
A maximum dynamism \(\Delta\ge 1\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A retained cut satisfies \(D(a)\le\Delta\).

notation.meaning: Coefficient dynamism over the nonzero support.

children.title: Encoding-Growth Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Storage and arithmetic limits associated with expanding coefficient encodings.

assumptions_latex: The normalized cut has primitive integer data \((\bar a,\bar\beta)\in\mathbb{Z}^{n+1}\).
An encoding budget \(B\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cut is admissible only if \(L(\bar a,\bar\beta)\le B\).

notation.meaning: Primitive integer representation of the cut.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bit-length boundary for storing and processing a normalized rational cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an integer \(z\), set \(\ell(z)=1+\lceil\log_2(|z|+1)\rceil\), where the additional unit records a sign. Define \[L(\bar a,\bar\beta)=\ell(\bar\beta)+\sum_{i=1}^n\ell(\bar a_i).\] An encoding-growth boundary accepts the normalized cut only if \(L(\bar a,\bar\beta)\le B\). For a sequence of generated cuts, imposing a polynomially bounded \(B\) prevents any single stored cut from having superpolynomial coefficient encoding length relative to the chosen input-size measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Measure the binary length of all primitive integer coefficients and the right-hand side; reject a cut whose total representation exceeds the fixed budget.
knowledge_statements.title: Encoding-Growth Boundaries

children.title: Redundancy-Relation Filtering System
children.top_down_role: Filtering of redundant or mutually unhelpful candidate cuts.

children.title: Duplicate-Cut Detection
children.top_down_role: Identification of equivalent candidate inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Duplicate-Cut Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact duplicate detection for rational inequalities represented with a common inequality sense.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each cut \(a^\top x\le\beta\), multiply \((a,\beta)\) by the least positive integer that clears its denominators and divide the resulting integer tuple by the greatest common divisor of the absolute values of its entries. Preserve the resulting sign pattern to obtain the canonical key \(\kappa(a,\beta)\). Store previously accepted keys in a set. A new cut \(c^\top x\le\delta\) is rejected as a duplicate if and only if \(\kappa(c,delta)\) is already stored; otherwise its key is inserted.
