Equivalently, the two cuts are exact duplicates precisely when \((c,\delta)=\lambda(a,beta)\) for some \(\lambda>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Normalize each rational inequality by positive denominator clearing and common-factor removal while preserving its orientation, then reject a candidate exactly when its primitive integer key is already stored.
assumptions_latex: Each rational cut is represented as \(a^\top x\le\beta\) with \((a,\beta)\ne0\).
Normalization uses exact arithmetic, positive denominator clearing, and the fixed inequality sense \(\le\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Two cuts are duplicates exactly when \(\kappa(a,\beta)=\kappa(c,\delta)\).

notation.meaning: Orientation-preserving primitive integer key of a rational inequality.

children.title: Parallelism Filtering
children.top_down_role: Removal of candidates that add little directional diversity.

assumptions_latex: Candidate cuts have nonzero normal vectors \(a,c\in\mathbb{R}^n\).
An angular similarity threshold \(\tau\in[0,1]\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A candidate is parallel-filtered when \(\rho(a,c)\ge\tau\) for a retained normal \(c\).

notation.meaning: Absolute cosine similarity of two cut normals.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric near-parallelism filter; validity of cuts is unaffected because only candidates are discarded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \[\rho(a,c)=\frac{|a^\top c|}{\|a\|_2\|c\|_2}.\] Process candidates in a fixed priority order. For a candidate with normal \(a\), compare it with every retained normal \(c\); if \(\rho(a,c)\ge\tau\), retain at most one member of the pair according to a fixed quality score and deterministic tie-breaker. If no such retained normal exists, accept the candidate. The absolute value treats opposite normals as geometrically parallel, while any orientation-sensitive dominance test is performed separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare cut normals by absolute cosine similarity and keep at most one near-parallel candidate according to a fixed quality ranking.
knowledge_statements.title: Parallelism Filtering

children.title: Dominance Filtering
children.top_down_role: Comparison of candidates through relative strength or redundancy.

assumptions_latex: Cuts are written with the same nonzero normal direction as \(a^\top x\le\beta\) and \(c^\top x\le\delta\).
Comparisons use exact arithmetic or certified tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(c=\lambda a\) and \(\delta\ge\lambda\beta\) for \(\lambda>0\), then the second cut is redundant relative to the first.

notation.meaning: Positive scaling factor aligning the normals.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise dominance for cuts having exactly the same oriented normal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(c=\lambda a\) for some \(\lambda>0\). If \(\delta\ge\lambda\beta\), then \[\{x:a^\top x\le\beta\}\subseteq\{x:c^\top x\le\delta\}.\] Hence \(c^\top x\le\delta\) is dominated by \(a^\top x\le\beta\) and may be discarded whenever both cuts would be imposed on the same relaxation. If \(\delta=\lambda\beta\), the cuts are duplicates; if \(\delta<\lambda\beta\), the dominance direction is reversed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Among cuts with the same oriented normal, the smaller scaled right-hand side defines the tighter halfspace and dominates the weaker cut.
knowledge_statements.title: Dominance Filtering

children.title: Filter-Conflict Resolution
children.top_down_role: Resolution of competing retention signals from multiple filters.

assumptions_latex: The finite candidate set is \(C\), and each candidate has a deterministic priority key.
A symmetric conflict relation \(E\subseteq\{\{p,q\}:p,q\in C,\ p\ne q\}\) is given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(K\subseteq C\) is conflict-free and maximal in the processing order.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic reconciliation of pairwise filtering decisions, not a claim of globally optimal cut selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(K=\varnothing\). Sort \(C\) by decreasing quality score and then by a fixed unique identifier. Scan candidates in that order, adding \(p\) to \(K\) exactly when \(\{p,q\}\notin E\) for every \(q\in K\). Output \(K\). Then no two retained candidates conflict, and every rejected candidate conflicts with a candidate retained earlier. Thus \(K\) is a deterministic maximal independent set of the conflict graph, although it need not have maximum cardinality or maximum total score.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Order candidates deterministically and greedily retain each one that conflicts with none already retained, producing a maximal conflict-free set.
knowledge_statements.title: Filter-Conflict Resolution

children.title: Integrated Branching-Cutting Architecture
children.top_down_role: Integration of node relaxation, separation, cut management, branching, primal information, and global search state.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Separation, cut-pool, cut-selector, and branching interfaces

children.title: Node-Processing Subsystems
children.top_down_role: Major services coordinated while processing a branch-and-cut node.

children.title: Node Relaxation-Bound State Representation
children.top_down_role: Relaxation and bound information maintained for the current subproblem.

children.title: Node Relaxation State
children.top_down_role: Current relaxation representation maintained for a search node.

knowledge_statements.title: Node Relaxation State
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization convention with optimal, infeasible, and unbounded relaxation statuses represented explicitly.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A node relaxation state is a tuple \(\mathcal R_v=(R_v,s_v,\hat x_v,b_v)\), where \(R_v\) is the current relaxation region, \(s_v\) is its solve status, and \(b_v=\inf\{c^\top x:x\in R_v\}\in\overline{\mathbb R}\). When the infimum is attained, \(\hat x_v\in R_v\) is an optimizer satisfying \(c^\top\hat x_v=b_v\); otherwise \(\hat x_v\) is absent. Under the conventions \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\) and \(b_v=-\infty\) for an unbounded-below relaxation, inclusion \(X_v\subseteq R_v\) gives \(b_v\le\inf\{c^\top x:x\in X_v\}\). If \(R_v=\varnothing\), the node is infeasible and may be pruned.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The node relaxation state stores the relaxation, its solve status, an optimizer when one exists, and an extended-real objective bound, including explicit infeasible and unbounded cases.
assumptions_latex: The mixed-integer problem is a minimization problem with objective \(c^\top x\).
Node \(v\) has relaxation region \(R_v\supseteq X_v\), where \(X_v\) is its integer-feasible region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The state records a valid extended-real node lower bound \(b_v\le\inf\{c^\top x:x\in X_v\}\).

notation.meaning: Conditional relaxation optimizer and extended-real relaxation value.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

children.title: Local Bound State
children.top_down_role: Bound information specific to the active subproblem.

assumptions_latex: Node \(v\) descends from a root mixed-integer model.
Every branching decision and local cut on the root-to-node path is recorded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The local region is \(X_v=X\cap\{\ell_v\le x\le u_v\}\cap\bigcap_{h\in H_v}h\).

notation.meaning: Node-specific componentwise lower and upper bounds.
Node-local branching constraints and valid cuts.
Feasible region inherited from the root model.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: State representation of restrictions applying only within one node subtree.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The local bound state at node \(v\) is \(\mathcal L_v=(\ell_v,u_v,H_v)\), where \(\ell_v\le x\le u_v\) are node-specific variable bounds and \(H_v\) contains other branching restrictions and locally valid cuts inherited along the root-to-\(v\) path. Its associated integer-feasible region is \[X_v=X\cap\{x:\ell_v\le x\le u_v\}\cap\bigcap_{h\in H_v}h.\] For a child node \(w\), the state must satisfy \(X_w\subseteq X_v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local bound state collects variable bounds, branching restrictions, and local cuts inherited by a node; every child region must be contained in its parent's region.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Bound State

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

children.title: Global Bound Contribution
children.top_down_role: Contribution of node information to search-wide bound tracking.

assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
The active-node set \(A\) is finite and each node \(v\in A\) has a valid lower bound \(b_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The active tree contributes the global lower bound \(L=\min_{v\in A}b_v\).

notation.meaning: Valid lower bound associated with node v.
Global lower bound contributed by active nodes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global lower-bound aggregation for minimization branch-and-bound.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the active nodes partition or cover every integer-feasible solution not already fathomed, and \(b_v\) is a valid lower bound for each \(v\in A\), then \[L=\min_{v\in A}b_v\] is a valid global lower bound on every still-possible solution. If \(A=\varnothing\), no unexplored solution remains. With incumbent value \(U\), any node satisfying \(b_v\ge U\) may be pruned, and termination with \(A=\varnothing\) certifies incumbent optimality when an incumbent exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The smallest valid lower bound among active nodes is a global lower bound; nodes whose bounds reach the incumbent value can be pruned.
knowledge_statements.title: Global Bound Contribution

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

children.title: Bound-State Consistency
children.top_down_role: Consistency requirements across relaxation changes and node transitions.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-State Consistency
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency invariant linking local restrictions, the current relaxation, solve status, and an extended-real minimization bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A node state is bound-consistent when \(X_v\subseteq R_v\), the stored status equals the status of minimizing \(c^\top x\) over \(R_v\), and \(b_v=\inf_{x\in R_v}c^\top x\in\overline{\mathbb R}\). Consequently, \(b_v\le\inf_{x\in X_v}c^\top x\). After adding valid cuts to obtain \(R'_v\) with \(X_v\subseteq R'_v\subseteq R_v\), the old solve status and bound must be invalidated until the relaxation is re-solved. Once re-solved, \(b'_v=\inf_{x\in R'_v}c^\top x\ge b_v\), using \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A consistent node state contains the local integer region in its relaxation, stores that relaxation's extended-real bound and actual status, and invalidates then recomputes both whenever cuts change the relaxation.
assumptions_latex: The problem is minimized over an integer-feasible root region \(X\).
Every relaxation cut is valid for the node region to which it is attached.
Infima are interpreted in \(\overline{\mathbb R}\), with \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Consistency requires \(X_v\subseteq R_v\) and \(b_v=\inf_{x\in R_v}c^\top x\le\inf_{x\in X_v}c^\top x\).

notation.meaning: Current relaxation region at node v.

children.title: Separation-Round State
children.top_down_role: State coordinating repeated separator calls and candidate processing.

knowledge_statements.title: Separation-Round State
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite state representation coordinating repeated separation and candidate postprocessing at one search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A separation-round state is \(\Sigma_r=(r,\hat x_r,\mathcal S,P_r,K_r,\sigma_r)\), where \(r\in\{0,\ldots,R_{\max}\}\) is the round index, \(\hat x_r\) is the current relaxation solution, \(\mathcal S\) is a finite ordered family of separators, \(P_r\) is the pool of at most \(K_{\max}\) candidates collected in the current round, \(K_r\subseteq P_r\) is the accepted set after validation and postprocessing, and \(\sigma_r\) records the active or terminal status and its stopping reason. From an active state, the stored policy calls separators in order subject to their budgets, constructs \(P_r\), and computes \(K_r\). If \(K_r=\varnothing\), a resource limit is reached, or a prescribed progress test fails, the next state is terminal. Otherwise the cuts in \(K_r\) are added, the relaxation is reoptimized, and the next active state is initialized with \(r+1\), \(P_{r+1}=\varnothing\), and \(K_{r+1}=\varnothing\). No transition starts another round when \(r=R_{\max}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The separation-round state records the round index, current relaxation solution, ordered separators, bounded candidate pool, accepted cuts, and stopping status, with explicit initialization of each subsequent round.
assumptions_latex: A node relaxation solution \(\hat x_0\) and a finite ordered family of terminating separators \(\mathcal S\) are available.
The round limit satisfies \(R_{\max}\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}\), and the candidate limit satisfies \(K_{\max}\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\).
Separator budgets, candidate validation, postprocessing, progress tests, and stopping priorities are fixed by the implementation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The state reaches a terminal status after at most \(R_{\max}\) separation rounds, each containing finitely many bounded separator calls and at most \(K_{\max}\) stored candidates.

notation.meaning: Complete state of separation round r.
Finite ordered family of terminating separation procedures.
Current bounded candidate pool and accepted cut set.
Active or terminal status together with any stopping reason.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

children.title: Incumbent-Primal State Representation Pair
children.top_down_role: Feasible-solution information used in bounding and pruning.

children.title: Incumbent Record
children.top_down_role: Search-wide storage of the best accepted feasible solution.

assumptions_latex: The mixed-integer problem is a minimization problem over feasible set \(F\).
Objective values are compared in the extended reals \(\overline{\mathbb R}=\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U=\inf\{c^\top x:x\in I\}\), with \(U=+\infty\) when \(I=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Set of accepted feasible incumbent solutions retained by the solver.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimization convention; the record may retain one or several tied incumbents.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization mixed-integer problem with feasible set \(F\), an incumbent record is a pair \((I,U)\) such that \(I\subseteq F\) is the set of accepted feasible solutions retained by the algorithm and \(U=\inf\{c^\top x:x\in I\}\). If \(I=\varnothing\), set \(U=+\infty\). When only one incumbent is retained, \(I=\{x^I\}\) and \(U=c^\top x^I\). Any auxiliary metadata, such as discovery node or time, does not alter the represented primal bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The incumbent record stores accepted feasible solutions and their best objective value, using positive infinity until a feasible solution is known.
knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Record

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the Incumbent Record leaf and is internally coherent under the minimization convention, but no citation supports the proposed pair (I,U), the retention of multiple incumbents, or the metadata claim. The local inventory contains no inspectable branch-and-cut incumbent-record source.

children.title: Primal Candidate State
children.top_down_role: Feasible or provisionally feasible solution information at a node.

assumptions_latex: A node relaxation supplies a point \(\hat x\) for a minimization mixed-integer problem.
Feasibility and integrality are tested using stated solver tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s(\hat x)=(f(\hat x),i(\hat x),z(\hat x),a(\hat x))\) determines whether \(\hat x\) may challenge the incumbent.

notation.meaning: Candidate point produced during node processing.
Candidate objective value and acceptance indicator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract solver state, independent of a particular feasibility-pump or primal-heuristic implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A primal candidate state associated with a point \(\hat x\) is the tuple \(s(\hat x)=(f(\hat x),i(\hat x),z(\hat x),a(\hat x))\), where \(f(\hat x)\in\{0,1\}\) records satisfaction of the original constraints within prescribed tolerances, \(i(\hat x)\in\{0,1\}\) records satisfaction of all integrality restrictions, \(z(\hat x)=c^\top\hat x\) when the objective is evaluable, and \(a(\hat x)\in\{0,1\}\) records acceptance for incumbent comparison. Incumbent eligibility requires \(f(\hat x)=i(\hat x)=a(\hat x)=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal candidate state records feasibility, integrality, objective value, and whether the point is eligible for incumbent comparison.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Candidate State

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the Primal Candidate State leaf, but the four-component state and especially the separate acceptance indicator are solver-schema choices rather than a standard canonical definition. No cited source supports this exact formulation or its eligibility condition.

children.title: Incumbent Update Events
children.top_down_role: State transitions caused by improved feasible solutions.

assumptions_latex: The problem is minimized and the current incumbent record is \((I,U)\).
A candidate \(\hat x\) has passed feasibility, integrality, and acceptance tests.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((I,U)\leftarrow(I',U')\) with \(U'=\min\{U,c^\top\hat x\}\).

notation.meaning: Current incumbent set and primal bound.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strict-improvement update for a minimization solver, with an optional tied-incumbent policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an incumbent record \((I,U)\), an accepted feasible candidate \(\hat x\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon_p\ge 0\), compute \(z=c^\top\hat x\). If \(z<U-\varepsilon_p\), emit an improvement event and set \((I,U)\leftarrow(\{\hat x\},z)\). If \(|z-U|\le\varepsilon_p\) and tied incumbents are retained, emit a tie event and set \(I\leftarrow I\cup\{\hat x\}\) while leaving \(U\) unchanged. Otherwise emit a rejection event and preserve \((I,U)\). The updated record is the output.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An accepted candidate replaces the incumbent when it improves the primal bound, may join tied incumbents, and otherwise leaves the record unchanged.
knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Update Events

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the update-event leaf, but the conclusion U'=min{U,c^T x-hat} conflicts with the stated tolerance policy: when U-epsilon_p <= z < U, the procedure may preserve U even though the displayed minimum is z. A source is also required to establish the strict-improvement, tie, and rejection event semantics before choosing the correct repair.

children.title: Primal-State Pruning Effects
children.top_down_role: Influence of feasible-solution information on node elimination.

assumptions_latex: The problem is minimized and each active node \(v\) has a valid relaxation lower bound \(L_v\).
The incumbent value \(U\) is the objective value of a feasible solution or \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_v\ge U-\varepsilon_g\Rightarrow v\) may be pruned without removing any solution improving \(U\) by more than \(\varepsilon_g\).

notation.meaning: Valid lower bound for node v.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound-dominance pruning under a minimization convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every active node \(v\), suppose \(L_v\le c^\top x\) for every integer-feasible solution \(x\) in that node. If the incumbent value changes from \(U\) to \(U'\le U\), every node satisfying \(L_v\ge U'-\varepsilon_g\) may be pruned: no solution in that node has objective value below \(U'-\varepsilon_g\). Thus an improving incumbent can only enlarge the set of nodes eligible for bound pruning, while leaving previously valid relaxation lower bounds unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A better incumbent strengthens bound pruning: any node whose valid lower bound cannot beat the incumbent within tolerance may be discarded.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal-State Pruning Effects

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the Primal-State Pruning Effects leaf and the absolute-tolerance implication is mathematically coherent for valid minimization lower bounds. However, no branch-and-bound source with a specific locator is cited for the pruning rule or its tolerance convention.

children.title: Branching Transition State
children.top_down_role: Information governing the transition from strengthening to subdivision.

assumptions_latex: Node \(v\) remains feasible and unpruned after its prescribed strengthening rounds.
The strengthened relaxation solution \(x_v^*\) violates at least one required integrality condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_v=(v,P_v,x_v^*,L_v,B_v,\mathcal C_v)\) contains the information required to create exhaustive child subproblems.

notation.meaning: Current node subproblem and strengthened relaxation solution.
Valid node lower bound and admissible branching choices.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract state passed from relaxation strengthening to branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The branching transition state at node \(v\) is a tuple \(T_v=(v,P_v,x_v^*,L_v,B_v,\mathcal C_v)\), where \(P_v\) is the current subproblem, \(x_v^*\) is its strengthened relaxation solution, \(L_v\) is a valid node bound, \(B_v\) is the set of admissible branching disjunctions, and \(\mathcal C_v\) is the active local constraint-and-cut context. A selected disjunction from \(B_v\) must define child regions whose union contains every integer-feasible point of \(P_v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The transition state packages the strengthened node, relaxation solution, bound, active constraints, and exhaustive branching choices needed to create children.
knowledge_statements.title: Branching Transition State

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is an appropriate kind for this state-oriented container, and the exhaustiveness requirement on a branching disjunction is relevant. The exact tuple, the meaning of B_v, and the assertion that it contains the information required to create children are architecture-specific and unsupported by any cited source.

children.title: Search-Tree Separation Architecture Family
children.top_down_role: Architectures distinguished by the location and intensity of separation in the search tree.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Cutting Planes from the Branch-and-Bound Tree: Challenges and Opportunities
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Cutting Planes from the Branch-and-Bound Tree: Challenges and Opportunities

children.title: Root-Node Cutting Systems
children.top_down_role: Intensive relaxation strengthening before substantial enumeration.

assumptions_latex: The root relaxation is \(P_0\supseteq F\), where \(F\) is the mixed-integer feasible set.
Every accepted cut is valid for all points in \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\subseteq P_0^{t+1}\subseteq P_0^t\) for every completed root cutting round \(t\).

notation.meaning: Root relaxation after t cutting rounds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic multi-round root separation before substantial tree enumeration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(P_0^0=P_0\). At root round \(t\), solve the current relaxation \(P_0^t\), invoke designated separation oracles at its solution, filter generated inequalities for validity, violation, numerical acceptability, and redundancy, and let \(C_t\) be the accepted cuts. Set \(P_0^{t+1}=P_0^t\cap\{x:a^\top x\le b\text{ for every }(a,b)\in C_t\}\). Stop when \(C_t=\varnothing\), a progress test fails, or a root resource limit is reached; output the strengthened root relaxation and its bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Root cutting repeatedly solves, separates, filters, and adds globally valid cuts until progress or resource criteria stop the process.
knowledge_statements.title: Root-Node Cutting Systems

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the correct role for the Root-Node Cutting Systems leaf, and the nested-relaxation invariant follows under the stated validity assumption. No cited source supports the complete solve-separate-filter-repeat procedure, its filtering stages, or its stopping policy; the inventory entries are not attached to the record and do not clearly cover integrated root-node cutting systems.

children.title: In-Tree Node Separation
children.top_down_role: Selective separation within nonroot subproblems.

assumptions_latex: Each processed nonroot node \(v\) has relaxation \(P_v\supseteq F_v\).
Every accepted cut is valid for the node-feasible mixed-integer set \(F_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_v\subseteq P_v^{t+1}\subseteq P_v^t\), and node bounds remain valid after separation.

notation.meaning: Relaxation at node v after t local cutting rounds.
Mixed-integer feasible set restricted to node v.
Cuts accepted at node v during round t.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selective separation at nonroot branch-and-cut nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a selected nonroot node \(v\), initialize \(P_v^0=P_v\). For round \(t\), solve \(P_v^t\), invoke only separators enabled by the node policy, and accept a filtered set \(C_{v,t}\) of inequalities valid for \(F_v\). Define \(P_v^{t+1}=P_v^t\cap\{x:a^\top x\le b\text{ for every }(a,b)\in C_{v,t}\}\). Stop when no acceptable cut is found, predicted benefit is insufficient, or the node budget is exhausted; return the strengthened node relaxation and bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At selected nonroot nodes, enabled separators add valid local or global cuts until benefit or resource tests terminate separation.
knowledge_statements.title: In-Tree Node Separation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and nonroot scope match the leaf, and cut validity for F_v yields the displayed containment. The separator-selection, benefit test, resource stopping rule, and returned-bound behavior lack a supporting citation with a specific locator.

children.title: Context-Adaptive Separation Policy Family
children.top_down_role: Separation policies conditioned on search context and available resources.

children.title: Depth-Adaptive Separation
children.top_down_role: Separation intensity conditioned on search-tree depth.

assumptions_latex: Every node \(v\) has a nonnegative depth \(d_v\).
Each separator \(j\) has a depth-dependent eligibility rule and round limit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(j\) is invoked at \(v\) only if \(e_j(d_v)=1\) and fewer than \(r_j(d_v)\) rounds have been used.

notation.meaning: Depth of node v, with root depth zero.
Depth-dependent eligibility indicator for separator j.
Maximum separation rounds allowed at depth d.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: A parameterized depth policy rather than a claim that deeper nodes always receive fewer cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For separator \(j\), specify functions \(e_j:\mathbb Z_+\to\{0,1\}\) and \(r_j:\mathbb Z_+\to\mathbb Z_+\). At node \(v\) of depth \(d_v\), activate \(j\) only when \(e_j(d_v)=1\), and perform at most \(r_j(d_v)\) invocations or rounds there. After each invocation, apply the ordinary validity and acceptance filters. Stop separator \(j\) when its depth allowance is exhausted or no accepted cut is returned; pass all accepted cuts to the node relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Depth-adaptive separation uses explicit depth-dependent eligibility and round limits to decide which separators run at each node.
knowledge_statements.title: Depth-Adaptive Separation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The parameterized algorithm fits Depth-Adaptive Separation and avoids claiming that effort must decrease with depth. Nevertheless, the eligibility and round-limit schema is a proposed policy abstraction with no cited source supporting this exact formulation or invocation semantics.

children.title: Node-Context Adaptation
children.top_down_role: Separator choices conditioned on local node characteristics.

assumptions_latex: A node \(v\) has an observable context vector \(q_v\).
Each separator \(j\) has a deterministic or randomized decision rule defined on the context space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_{v,j}=\pi_j(q_v)\) determines activation and permitted effort for separator \(j\) at node \(v\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Context includes only information available when the activation decision is made.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Form a node-context vector \(q_v\) from information available at node \(v\), such as relaxation status, fractionality, bound gap, degeneracy indicators, cut history, and node type. For each separator \(j\), evaluate a policy \(a_{v,j}=\pi_j(q_v)\), where \(a_{v,j}\) specifies whether \(j\) is invoked and its effort limit. Invoke the selected separators subject to those limits, validate and filter their cuts, update the relaxation, and recompute the context before any subsequent adaptive round.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Node-context adaptation maps observable relaxation and search information to separator activation and effort decisions, then refreshes context after strengthening.
knowledge_statements.title: Node-Context Adaptation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the Node-Context Adaptation leaf, but the context vector, policy output, effort semantics, and recomputation rule are unsupported. The assumptions allow randomized policies while the statement writes a_{v,j}=pi_j(q_v) without introducing randomness or a probability kernel, so a source is needed to determine the intended mathematical formulation.

children.title: Progress-Responsive Separation
children.top_down_role: Policy changes triggered by recent separation effectiveness.

assumptions_latex: Successive separation rounds produce measurable strengthening or search-progress statistics.
Thresholds and patience limits are fixed before each policy decision.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_t<\tau\) for \(p\) consecutive rounds triggers termination or reduced separator effort.

notation.meaning: Measured progress after separation round t.
Number of consecutive low-progress rounds tolerated.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Progress may be measured by bound improvement, violation removal, or another prespecified statistic.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a progress statistic \(g_t\ge 0\), threshold \(\tau\ge 0\), and patience \(p\in\mathbb N\). After separation round \(t\), compute \(g_t\) from prespecified data, for example relative node-bound improvement or reduction in aggregate cut violation. If \(g_t\ge\tau\), reset the low-progress counter and retain or increase eligible effort. Otherwise increment the counter. When the counter reaches \(p\), terminate separation or reduce the eligible separator set according to a fixed fallback rule; output the current relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Progress-responsive separation continues or expands useful rounds and stops or reduces effort after a prescribed run of insufficient improvement.
knowledge_statements.title: Progress-Responsive Separation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits Progress-Responsive Separation, but no source supports the threshold-and-patience controller or its fallback behavior. The statement should also require p>=1 explicitly because p in N is convention-dependent and may include zero.

children.title: Resource-Adaptive Separation
children.top_down_role: Policy changes conditioned on remaining computational resources.

assumptions_latex: Separation consumes measurable resources under a finite node or global budget.
Costs are charged to the budget when separator invocations complete.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b_{t+1}=b_t-c_t\ge 0\), and no invocation whose admissible cost exceeds \(b_t\) is started.

notation.meaning: Resource budget remaining before decision t.
Charged cost of the selected separation action.
Set of separation actions admissible under the remaining budget.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resource units may be time, oracle calls, generated cuts, memory, or a weighted combination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a finite separation budget \(b_0\ge 0\). At decision \(t\), form the admissible action set \(A(b_t)=\{a:c(a)\le b_t\}\), select an action \(a_t\in A(b_t)\) using the current separator scores, execute it, and charge realized cost \(c_t\ge 0\). Update \(b_{t+1}=b_t-c_t\). Stop when \(A(b_t)=\varnothing\), the remaining budget is reserved for other node processing, or the ordinary progress rule terminates separation; return all accepted valid cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resource-adaptive separation selects only actions affordable under the remaining budget and updates that budget after every separator invocation.
knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Adaptive Separation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits Resource-Adaptive Separation, but admissibility is defined using c(a) while the budget is charged a possibly different realized cost c_t. The assumptions do not ensure c_t<=b_t, so the claimed invariant b_{t+1}>=0 does not follow. A source is needed to determine whether costs are known bounds, estimates, or realized charges and to support the policy.

children.title: Multi-Separator Orchestration
children.top_down_role: Scheduling and coordination of heterogeneous separator families.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Separator plugins and separation-round return states

children.title: Separator Activation Policy System
children.top_down_role: Ordering, frequency, delay, and activation policies for separator families.

children.title: Separator Scheduling
children.top_down_role: Ordering and timing of separator-family execution.

assumptions_latex: There is a finite separator set \(J\).
Each separator has an eligibility predicate, priority, frequency rule, and effort limit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_t\) is an ordered list of eligible separators, and every scheduled invocation respects its frequency and effort constraints.

notation.meaning: Eligible separators at scheduling epoch t.
Ordered separator schedule for epoch t.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scheduling coordinates multiple separators within one node-processing epoch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At scheduling epoch \(t\), compute \(E_t=\{j\in J:e_j(q_t)=1\}\) from the current node context \(q_t\), activation frequencies, delays, and remaining budgets. Order \(E_t\) by nonincreasing priority score \(p_j(q_t)\), with a fixed tie rule, to obtain \(S_t\). Invoke separators in that order while their individual and shared effort limits remain feasible. After each invocation, record cost and accepted cuts; recompute \(S_t\) when the policy requires rescheduling. Stop when the schedule is empty or a node-level stopping test holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Separator scheduling filters eligible separators, orders them by context-sensitive priority, and invokes them while frequency, delay, and budget constraints remain satisfied.
knowledge_statements.title: Separator Scheduling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the correct kind for the Separator Scheduling leaf, and the statement is locally consistent as a policy template. The eligibility computation, context-sensitive priority ordering, rescheduling behavior, and claimed compliance with frequency, delay, and effort constraints have no cited support with an inspectable locator.

children.title: Separator Priority Assignment
children.top_down_role: Relative precedence assigned to available separator families.

assumptions_latex: The available separator families form a finite set \(\mathcal S\).
Every family \(s\in\mathcal S\) has a priority value \(p_s\in\mathbb R\) and deterministic tie-break key \(t_s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[s\prec s'\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (-p_s,t_s)<_{\mathrm{lex}}(-p_{s'},t_{s'}).\]

notation.meaning: Priority assigned to separator family s.
Deterministic tie-break key for family s.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Static priority ordering within one multi-separator activation policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A separator priority assignment on a finite portfolio \(\mathcal S\) is a map \(p:\mathcal S\to\mathbb R\) together with tie-break keys \(t_s\). At each eligible separation event, the policy orders active families by nonincreasing priority and resolves equal priorities by increasing \(t_s\). Thus family \(s\) precedes family \(s'\) exactly when \((-p_s,t_s)\) is lexicographically smaller than \((-p_{s'},t_{s'})\). Priority determines consideration order only; activation eligibility and computational budgets remain separate policy components.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A priority assignment ranks eligible separator families by numerical priority, with a deterministic key resolving ties; it does not itself decide eligibility or budget.
knowledge_statements.title: Separator Priority Assignment

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit the leaf, and the notation is internally consistent, but no cited source supports this particular priority-and-tie-break formalization.

children.title: Activation Frequency Policies
children.top_down_role: Controls governing how often each separator is invoked.

assumptions_latex: Separation events are indexed by \(r\in\mathbb N_0\).
Each separator family \(s\in\mathcal S\) has an integer period \(f_s\ge 1\) and phase \(q_s\in\{0,\ldots,f_s-1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[s\text{ is frequency-eligible at }r\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad r\equiv q_s\pmod{f_s}.\]

notation.meaning: Index of the current separation event.
Activation period of separator family s.
Activation phase of separator family s.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Periodic eligibility policy; other activation tests may still suppress execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A periodic activation-frequency policy assigns each separator family \(s\in\mathcal S\) a period \(f_s\ge 1\) and phase \(q_s\in\{0,\ldots,f_s-1\}\). At separation event \(r\in\mathbb N_0\), family \(s\) is frequency-eligible precisely when \(r\equiv q_s\pmod{f_s}\). Eligibility authorizes consideration but does not require execution: resource limits, delayed activation, or state-dependent filters may still suppress the call. The special choice \(f_s=1\) makes \(s\) eligible at every event.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A periodic frequency policy makes each separator eligible on events matching its assigned period and phase, subject to independent resource and activation filters.
knowledge_statements.title: Activation Frequency Policies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The periodic eligibility definition is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but the period-and-phase model is an uncited choice rather than a documented general separator-frequency policy.

children.title: Delayed-Activation Policies
children.top_down_role: Conditions under which separator invocation is postponed.

assumptions_latex: Solver states belong to a set \(\mathcal X\).
Each separator family \(s\in\mathcal S\) has an eligibility predicate \(E_s:\mathcal X\to\{0,1\}\) and release predicate \(D_s:\mathcal X\to\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[A_s(x)=E_s(x)D_s(x),\qquad A_s(x)=0\text{ whenever }D_s(x)=0.\]

notation.meaning: Ordinary eligibility predicate for separator s.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: State-based postponement of otherwise eligible separator families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A delayed-activation policy for separator family \(s\) consists of an ordinary eligibility predicate \(E_s\) and a release predicate \(D_s\) on solver states \(x\in\mathcal X\). Its activation indicator is \(A_s(x)=E_s(x)D_s(x)\). Consequently, an eligible family remains inactive while \(D_s(x)=0\) and becomes callable only after a state satisfying \(D_s(x)=1\) is reached. Typical release predicates may depend on search depth, elapsed rounds, incumbent availability, or measured relaxation stagnation, but the predicate must be fixed by the policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delayed activation suppresses an otherwise eligible separator until a specified solver-state predicate becomes true.
knowledge_statements.title: Delayed-Activation Policies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The predicate-based definition fits delayed activation, but no inspectable citation supports this exact abstraction or the listed release conditions.

children.title: Separation-Round Management
children.top_down_role: Organization and budgeting of repeated multi-family separation.

assumptions_latex: The current relaxation is \(P_0\), and every returned inequality is valid for the mixed-integer feasible set.
A finite family portfolio \(\mathcal S\), round limit \(R\), cut budget \(B\), and stopping tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\) are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[P_{r+1}=P_r\cap\bigcap_{c\in C_r}c,\qquad \sum_{r=0}^{k-1}|C_r|\le B,\qquad P_k\supseteq P_I.\]

notation.meaning: Relaxation available at the start of round r.
Accepted cuts generated during round r.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Budgeted repeated separation over multiple cut families at one search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(r=0\) and the accepted-cut count to zero. While \(r<R\) and the budget \(B\) is not exhausted, select frequency- and state-eligible families, invoke them in policy order on \(P_r\), filter their proposed inequalities for validity and acceptance, and retain a set \(C_r\) within the remaining budget. Set \(P_{r+1}=P_r\cap\bigcap_{c\in C_r}c\), reoptimize, and increment \(r\). Stop if \(C_r=\varnothing\), the prescribed relaxation-improvement measure is at most \(\varepsilon\), or a limit is reached; output the final relaxation and accepted cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Round management repeatedly schedules eligible separators, accepts valid cuts within a global budget, reoptimizes, and stops on exhaustion, stagnation, or an empty round.
knowledge_statements.title: Separation-Round Management

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is an appropriate kind for separation-round management, but the proposed integrated scheduling, budgeting, reoptimization, and stopping procedure has no supporting source. Its exact accepted-cut and improvement rules are policy-dependent.

children.title: Separator Portfolio Interaction Regimes
children.top_down_role: Coverage gains and redundant effort arising from interactions among cut families.

children.title: Separator Complementarity
children.top_down_role: Coverage gains produced by combining distinct separator families.

assumptions_latex: Two separator families \(s,t\) are evaluated at the same solver state \(x\).
A normalized benefit function \(V_x(C)\) is defined for finite accepted-cut sets and satisfies \(V_x(\varnothing)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\Gamma_x(s,t)>0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad V_x(C_s\cup C_t)>V_x(C_s)+V_x(C_t).\]

notation.meaning: Accepted cuts produced by separator family s at state x.
Benefit assigned to an accepted-cut set at state x.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise complementarity relative to an explicitly chosen cut-set benefit measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For separator outputs \(C_s\) and \(C_t\) at state \(x\), define their complementarity score by \(\Gamma_x(s,t)=V_x(C_s\cup C_t)-V_x(C_s)-V_x(C_t)\), where \(V_x(\varnothing)=0\). The families are complementary at \(x\) relative to \(V_x\) when \(\Gamma_x(s,t)>0\): their combined accepted cuts provide more measured benefit than the sum of their separate benefits. They are additive when \(\Gamma_x(s,t)=0\), and substitutive under this measure when \(\Gamma_x(s,t)<0\). The classification is meaningless unless the state, acceptance rule, and benefit function are held fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two separator families are complementary when their jointly accepted cuts yield more measured benefit than the sum obtained from each family separately.
knowledge_statements.title: Separator Complementarity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits separator complementarity only relative to the declared benefit function. The superadditive score is a plausible constructed metric, but no source establishes it as a recognized separator-complementarity notion.

children.title: Redundant Separation Effort
children.top_down_role: Duplicated work across separators targeting similar violations.

assumptions_latex: Accepted cuts are normalized by a canonical map \(n\) that identifies positive scalar multiples.
The reference relaxation is \(P\), and \(C_s,C_t\) are finite cut sets returned by families \(s,t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[R_{m dup}(s,t)=\frac{|n(C_s)\cap n(C_t)|}{|n(C_s)\cup n(C_t)|},\qquad R_{m dup}(s,t)\in[0,1].\]

notation.meaning: Canonical normalization of inequalities modulo positive scaling.
Cuts produced by separator family s.
Duplicate-effort ratio for families s and t.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact duplicate effort after canonical inequality normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For two finite accepted-cut sets \(C_s\) and \(C_t\), let \(n(C)\) denote their canonical normalized inequalities, identifying inequalities that differ only by a positive scalar. Define exact redundant separation effort by the Jaccard ratio \(R_{\rm dup}(s,t)=|n(C_s)\cap n(C_t)|/|n(C_s)\cup n(C_t)|\), with value zero when both normalized sets are empty. The ratio lies in \([0,1]\); value one means the families return identical normalized cut sets, while value zero means no exact duplicates. This measure does not identify distinct inequalities that induce the same relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact redundant effort is the fraction of normalized cuts duplicated across two separator outputs; it excludes distinct cuts that happen to define the same relaxation.
knowledge_statements.title: Redundant Separation Effort

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Jaccard formula is well defined with the stated empty-set convention and accurately measures exact duplicate cuts, but it is an uncited bespoke metric and covers only one narrow form of redundant separation effort.

children.title: Cross-Family Interference
children.top_down_role: Adverse computational effects caused by interactions among cut families.

assumptions_latex: A deterministic separator \(t\) maps each relaxation \(P\) to a finite candidate set \(C_t(P)\).
A cut set \(C_s\) from another family is accepted first, producing \(P'=P\cap\bigcap_{c\in C_s}c\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[C_t(P')\ne C_t(P)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\text{the execution of }s\text{ interferes with the subsequent output of }t.\]

notation.meaning: Candidate cuts returned by family t on relaxation P.
Relaxation after accepting cuts from family s.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order-dependent change in one family caused by cuts from another.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let deterministic separator family \(t\) return \(C_t(P)\) on relaxation \(P\). After family \(s\) contributes accepted cuts \(C_s\), set \(P'=P\cap\bigcap_{c\in C_s}c\). Family \(s\) interferes with \(t\) at \(P\) when \(C_t(P')\ne C_t(P)\), provided all solver state other than the relaxation is fixed. Interference is suppressive when a previously returned cut disappears, generative when a new cut appears, and modifying when retained cuts change. This definition records order dependence and does not by itself imply that the interaction harms performance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cross-family interference occurs when accepting cuts from one family changes another family’s subsequent cut output under otherwise fixed solver state.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Family Interference

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The order-dependent definition is coherent under determinism and fixed auxiliary solver state, but no source supports this exact use of interference or its suppressive, generative, and modifying subclasses.

children.title: Portfolio-Coverage Gaps
children.top_down_role: Relevant inequality structures missed by the active separator portfolio.

assumptions_latex: The target cut universe \(\mathcal U(P)\) and portfolio \(\mathcal S\) are fixed for relaxation \(P\).
Each family \(s\) can generate a subset \(G_s(P)\subseteq\mathcal U(P)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[H(P)=\mathcal U(P)\setminus\bigcup_{s\in\mathcal S}G_s(P),\qquad H(P)\ne\varnothing\text{ signifies a coverage gap}.\]

notation.meaning: Target universe of valid separating cuts at relaxation P.
Target cuts generable by separator family s.
Cuts not covered by any family in the portfolio.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coverage is relative to a declared target universe, not all valid inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a target universe \(\mathcal U(P)\) of valid cuts that separate points of the current relaxation \(P\) from the mixed-integer feasible set. For each portfolio family \(s\in\mathcal S\), let \(G_s(P)\subseteq\mathcal U(P)\) be the cuts it can generate under the allowed resource limits. The portfolio-coverage gap is \(H(P)=\mathcal U(P)\setminus\bigcup_{s\in\mathcal S}G_s(P)\). A nonempty \(H(P)\) means that at least one targeted cut is inaccessible to every configured family. Because the set of all valid inequalities is generally impractical, \(\mathcal U(P)\) must be declared operationally.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A portfolio has a coverage gap when some cut in a declared target universe cannot be generated by any configured separator family.
knowledge_statements.title: Portfolio-Coverage Gaps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The set-difference definition fits the leaf once an operational target universe and resource model are fixed, but those choices determine the claim and no source supports the proposed coverage formalization.

children.title: Adaptive Separator Configuration Family
children.top_down_role: Instance- and state-dependent configuration of separator portfolios.

children.title: State-Adaptive Configuration
children.top_down_role: Configuration changes driven by current solver state.

assumptions_latex: Solver states form a set \(\mathcal X\), and admissible configurations form a set \(\Theta\).
A state descriptor \(\phi:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R^d\) and decision rule \(\pi:\mathbb R^d\to\Theta\) are fixed before execution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\theta_r=\pi(\phi(x_r)),\qquad C_r=\operatorname{Separate}(P_r;\theta_r).\]

notation.meaning: Solver state at separation event r.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Online configuration changes driven by the current search state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At separation event \(r\), observe the current solver state \(x_r\), compute features \(z_r=\phi(x_r)\), and select the admissible configuration \(\theta_r=\pi(z_r)\). Invoke the configured separator portfolio on relaxation \(P_r\) to obtain candidate cuts, apply the fixed validity and acceptance filters, and record the resulting state transition. Repeat at the next eligible event, allowing \(\theta_{r+1}\ne\theta_r\). Stop according to the enclosing branch-and-cut limits. The policy is state-adaptive because its configuration may vary within one instance as the search state changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: State-adaptive configuration recomputes separator settings from the current search state at each eligible event, so one instance may use several configurations.
knowledge_statements.title: State-Adaptive Configuration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The procedure correctly distinguishes within-instance state adaptation and algorithm is a defensible kind, but no cited source supports this exact feature-policy configuration scheme.

children.title: Instance-Adaptive Configuration
children.top_down_role: Portfolio configuration conditioned on instance characteristics.

assumptions_latex: Problem instances belong to a set \(\mathcal I\), and admissible configurations form a set \(\Theta\).
An instance descriptor \(\psi:\mathcal I\to\mathbb R^d\) and selection rule \(g:\mathbb R^d\to\Theta\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\theta(I)=g(\psi(I)),\qquad \theta_r=\theta(I)\text{ for every separation event }r.\]

notation.meaning: Static feature vector of instance I.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: One configuration is selected per instance from static instance information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given instance \(I\in\mathcal I\), compute its static descriptor \(z=\psi(I)\) before branch-and-cut search and select \(\theta(I)=g(z)\in\Theta\). Initialize the separator portfolio using \(\theta(I)\), then retain this configuration at every separation event for that instance. Run the enclosing solver until its ordinary stopping condition and return its incumbent or status. The procedure is instance-adaptive because different instances may receive different configurations, but it is not state-adaptive: for every event \(r\) on the same instance, \(\theta_r=\theta(I)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Instance-adaptive configuration chooses separator settings once from static instance features and retains them throughout that instance’s search.
knowledge_statements.title: Instance-Adaptive Configuration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record coherently defines one static configuration per instance and distinguishes it from state adaptation, but the algorithmic formulation lacks an inspectable supporting citation.

children.title: Learned Separator Configuration
children.top_down_role: Data-driven selection of separator settings.

assumptions_latex: Training data are \(D=\{(z_i,y_i)\}_{i=1}^n\), with descriptors \(z_i\) and observed configuration losses \(y_i:\Theta\to\mathbb R\).
A hypothesis class \(\Pi\) of policies \(\pi:z\mapsto\theta\) and regularizer \(\Omega\) are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\widehat\pi\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\pi\in\Pi}\left\{\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n y_i(\pi(z_i))+\lambda\Omega(\pi)\right\},\qquad \theta=\widehat\pi(z).\]

notation.meaning: Training observations of descriptors and configuration losses.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Empirical-risk formulation for learning a separator-configuration policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given training observations \(D=\{(z_i,y_i)\}_{i=1}^n\), choose \(\widehat\pi\) to minimize regularized empirical configuration loss over \(\Pi\): \(\widehat\pi\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\pi\in\Pi}\{n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n y_i(\pi(z_i))+\lambda\Omega(\pi)\}\), where \(\lambda\ge0\). For a new instance or solver state with descriptor \(z\), select \(\theta=\widehat\pi(z)\), execute the corresponding separator configuration, and retain the enclosing solver's stopping rule. The loss must include the intended resource measure, such as time, nodes, or primal-dual progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A learned configuration policy minimizes regularized empirical solver loss, then maps new instance or state features to separator settings.
knowledge_statements.title: Learned Separator Configuration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The empirical-risk algorithm fits learned configuration, but it assumes full configuration-loss functions for every training descriptor and supplies no source supporting that learning protocol or its separator-specific interpretation.

children.title: Configuration-Generalization Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Reliability limits when adaptive policies encounter unfamiliar search regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Configuration-Generalization Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distribution-shift boundary for bounded-loss learned configurations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R_\mu(\pi)=\mathbb E_{z\sim\mu}[\ell(\pi,z)]\) and suppose \(0\le\ell(\widehat\pi,z)\le M\). Then \(|R_Q(\widehat\pi)-R_P(\widehat\pi)|\le M\operatorname{TV}(P,Q)\). Hence performance measured under training distribution \(P\) controls deployment performance only when the distribution shift is controlled or additional invariance assumptions are supplied. Without such control the boundary is sharp: distributions with disjoint support can have \(\operatorname{TV}(P,Q)=1\), and a bounded loss may be zero on the support of \(P\) but equal to \(M\) on the support of \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Training performance need not transfer under unrestricted distribution shift; for bounded loss, the risk change is controlled only by a distribution distance or stronger assumptions.
assumptions_latex: Training descriptors have distribution \(P\), while deployment descriptors have distribution \(Q\).
The learned policy \(\widehat\pi\) has bounded loss \(0\le\ell(\widehat\pi,z)\le M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\bigl|R_Q(\widehat\pi)-R_P(\widehat\pi)\bigr|\le M\,\operatorname{TV}(P,Q),\qquad R_\mu(\pi)=\mathbb E_{z\sim\mu}[\ell(\pi,z)].\]

notation.meaning: Expected loss under descriptor distribution mu.
Uniform upper bound on configuration loss.
Total-variation distance between training and deployment distributions.

children.title: Cut Admission Decision System
children.top_down_role: Selection of a compatible and computationally manageable subset of candidate cuts.

children.title: Cut Quality Criteria
children.top_down_role: Efficacy, support, density, objective alignment, stability, and predicted progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Quality Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines normalized criteria for ranking valid inequalities at a fixed relaxation solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the current relaxation be \(P\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let \(\bar x\in P\), and let a candidate valid cut be \(a^Tx\le b\) with \(a\ne0\). Its efficacy is \(e=(a^T\bar x-b)_+/\lVert a\rVert_2\); density is \(d=\lVert a\rVert_0/n\); objective alignment is \(o=|a^Tc|/(\lVert a\rVert_2\lVert c\rVert_2)\) when \(c\ne0\); and normalized support is \(s=1-d\). Given normalized stability and predicted-progress scores \(t,p\in[0,1]\), a cut-quality score is \(Q=w_e\hat e+w_ss+w_oo+w_tt+w_pp\), where the nonnegative weights sum to one. Larger \(Q\) denotes preferred admission.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cut quality combines normalized violation, sparsity, objective alignment, numerical stability, and predicted progress using an explicitly weighted score.
assumptions_latex: \(a^Tx\le b\) is valid for the integer-feasible set.
\(w_e,w_s,w_o,w_t,w_p\ge0\) and \(w_e+w_s+w_o+w_t+w_p=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\in[0,1]\) whenever \(\hat e,s,o,t,p\in[0,1]\).

notation.meaning: positive part, equal to max of u and zero

source_refs.locator: 10.2 Most Violated Cut Selection Rule p. 126

source_witnesses.locator: 10.2 Most Violated Cut Selection Rule p. 126

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited most-violated-cut section does not inspectably support the composite efficacy, sparsity, alignment, stability, and predicted-progress policy. Moreover, \(\hat e\) is not defined from \(e\), and \(s=1-d\) is sparsity rather than normalized support. An authoritative source or an explicit, fully specified policy rationale is required.

children.title: Cut Redundancy Geometry Filters
children.top_down_role: Controls for redundancy among admitted cuts.

children.title: Cut-Diversity Measurement
children.top_down_role: Representations used to assess variation within a candidate set.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Diversity Measurement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Measures directional diversity within a finite pool of nonzero cut normals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonzero candidate-cut normals \(a_1,\ldots,a_m\in\mathbb R^n\), define directional similarity by \(s_{ij}=|a_i^Ta_j|/(\lVert a_i\rVert_2\lVert a_j\rVert_2)\) and distance by \(\delta_{ij}=1-s_{ij}\). For a selected index set \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\), its minimum diversity is \(D_{\min}(S)=1\) when \(|S|\le1\), and otherwise \(D_{\min}(S)=\min_{i\ne j,\ i,j\in S}\delta_{ij}\). Its average diversity is \(D_{\mathrm{avg}}(S)=2\sum_{i<j,\ i,j\in S}\delta_{ij}/(|S|(|S|-1))\) when \(|S|\ge2\). Both measures are invariant under nonzero rescaling of individual cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Diversity is one minus absolute cosine similarity between cut normals, aggregated by the minimum or average pairwise distance.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i\ne0\) for every candidate cut.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_{\min}(S),D_{\mathrm{avg}}(S)\in[0,1]\) whenever their displayed formulas apply.

notation.meaning: normal vector of candidate cut i

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent and fits the diversity-measurement leaf, but no inspectable source supports the choice of absolute-cosine distance or these aggregations as cut-diversity measures.

children.title: Directional Parallelism Detection
children.top_down_role: Identification of candidates with closely aligned coefficient directions.

knowledge_statements.title: Directional Parallelism Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Detects nearly parallel or antiparallel cuts using normalized normal vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let two cuts have nonzero normals \(a_i,a_j\in\mathbb R^n\), and fix a tolerance \(\tau_{\parallel}\in[0,1]\). They are directionally parallel at tolerance \(\tau_{\parallel}\) precisely when \[\frac{|a_i^Ta_j|}{\lVert a_i\rVert_2\lVert a_j\rVert_2}\ge1-\tau_{\parallel}.\] If orientation matters, replace the absolute numerator by \(a_i^Ta_j\); the resulting one-sided test recognizes only similarly oriented normals. The absolute-cosine test is invariant under multiplication of either inequality by a nonzero scalar and therefore compares directions rather than coefficient magnitudes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two cuts are directionally parallel when the absolute cosine between their normals lies within a prescribed tolerance of one.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i\ne0\) and \(a_j\ne0\).

children.title: Diversity-Preserving Selection
children.top_down_role: Retention policies favoring complementary candidate cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Diversity-Preserving Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Greedy quality selection subject to a minimum angular-separation requirement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given candidates \(C=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), quality scores \(Q_i\), budget \(k\), and diversity threshold \(\eta\in[0,1]\), initialize \(S=\varnothing\). Process indices in nonincreasing order of \(Q_i\), using a fixed deterministic tie rule. Admit \(i\) exactly when \(|S|<k\) and \(1-|a_i^Ta_j|/(\lVert a_i\rVert_2\lVert a_j\rVert_2)\ge\eta\) for every \(j\in S\). Stop after all candidates are processed or \(|S|=k\), and output the cuts indexed by \(S\). The output contains at most \(k\) cuts and has pairwise directional diversity at least \(\eta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Greedily admit high-quality cuts only when each remains sufficiently directionally distinct from every previously selected cut.
assumptions_latex: Each candidate normal \(a_i\) is nonzero.
\(k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) and \(\eta\in[0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|S|\le k\) and \(D_{\min}(S)\ge\eta\).
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The greedy procedure and its stated pairwise-diversity guarantee are coherent, and algorithm is the correct content kind. No source establishes this particular quality-ordered selection policy in the cut-admission setting.

children.title: Parallel-Cut Rejection
children.top_down_role: Admission controls for near-parallel candidate inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel-Cut Rejection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rejects a candidate dominated in score by an already retained parallel cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let candidate \(i\) and retained cut \(j\) have nonzero normals, quality scores \(Q_i,Q_j\), and normalized right-hand sides \(\beta_i=b_i/\lVert a_i\rVert_2\), \(\beta_j=b_j/\lVert a_j\rVert_2\) after orienting their normalized normals consistently. For tolerances \(\tau_{\parallel},\tau_b,\tau_Q\ge0\), reject \(i\) as parallel-redundant when \[\frac{a_i^Ta_j}{\lVert a_i\rVert_2\lVert a_j\rVert_2}\ge1-\tau_{\parallel},\qquad |\beta_i-\beta_j|\le\tau_b,\qquad Q_i\le Q_j+\tau_Q.\] The right-hand-side test prevents angular similarity alone from discarding substantially displaced inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reject a nearly parallel candidate only when its normalized offset is similar and it offers no meaningful quality improvement.
assumptions_latex: The inequalities are oriented so their normalized normals point consistently.
\(a_i\ne0\), \(a_j\ne0\), and all tolerances are nonnegative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed conjunction is the parallel-cut rejection predicate.

notation.meaning: normalized right-hand side of cut i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed conjunction can define a solver policy, but similar direction and offset plus lower score do not mathematically establish redundancy. A source must support the intended rejection policy and terminology.

children.title: Relaxation Growth Budget System
children.top_down_role: Resource policies limiting admitted cuts and relaxation growth.

children.title: Per-Round Cut Budgets
children.top_down_role: Limits on cuts admitted during one separation round.

knowledge_statements.title: Per-Round Cut Budgets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits admissions during one separation-and-reoptimization round.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(v\) and cutting round \(r\), let \(C_{v,r}\) be the candidate pool, let \(S_{v,r}\subseteq C_{v,r}\) be the admitted set, and let \(B_r\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) be the round budget. Feasible admission requires \(|S_{v,r}|\le B_r\). If candidates have nonnegative row costs \(w_i\) and the budget is weighted, the condition becomes \(\sum_{i\in S_{v,r}}w_i\le B_r\). Once the applicable inequality is tight, no further candidate is admitted in that round; unused capacity does not carry forward unless an explicit carryover rule is defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cutting round may admit no more than its cardinality or weighted row budget, with carryover disabled by default.
assumptions_latex: \(S_{v,r}\subseteq C_{v,r}\).
\(B_r\ge0\), and \(w_i\ge0\) in the weighted version.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|S_{v,r}|\le B_r\), or \(\sum_{i\in S_{v,r}}w_i\le B_r\) under weighted accounting.

notation.meaning: candidate pool at node v in round r

children.title: Per-Node Cut Budgets
children.top_down_role: Limits on cumulative cut activity at a search node.

knowledge_statements.title: Per-Node Cut Budgets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounds cumulative cut admissions over all rounds processed at one search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a branch-and-bound node \(v\), let \(S_{v,r}\) denote the cuts admitted in round \(r\), and let \(B_v\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) be the node budget. Under admission accounting, feasibility requires \(\sum_r|S_{v,r}|\le B_v\). Under active-row accounting, let \(A_{v,r}\) be the locally generated cuts still active after round \(r\); feasibility instead requires \(|A_{v,r}|\le B_v\) for every \(r\). The accounting convention must be fixed in advance: deleting a cut restores capacity only under active-row accounting, not under cumulative admission accounting.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node budget limits either cumulative admissions or simultaneously active local cuts; deletion restores capacity only in the latter convention.
assumptions_latex: \(B_v\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\).
Exactly one accounting convention is fixed for node \(v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_r|S_{v,r}|\le B_v\) or \(|A_{v,r}|\le B_v\) for every \(r\), according to the chosen convention.

notation.meaning: active locally generated cuts after round r

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The two accounting conventions are plausible, but the range of rounds in \(\sum_r\) is not stated and the deletion-capacity behavior is solver-specific. A supporting source is required.

children.title: Relaxation-Row Caps
children.top_down_role: Controls on the total active row count.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Row Caps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Enforces a hard bound on rows in the active node relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_v^0\) be the number of indispensable formulation rows at node \(v\), let \(A_v\) be the active removable cut rows, and let \(R_v\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) be the relaxation-row cap. The active relaxation is admissible only if \(m_v^0+|A_v|\le R_v\). Before adding a set \(S\) of new cuts, deletion or rejection must ensure \(m_v^0+|A_v\cup S|\le R_v\). If \(m_v^0>R_v\), the cap is infeasible and cannot be restored by deleting removable cuts; the node must retain the indispensable rows and report a cap exception.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The number of indispensable and active cut rows cannot exceed the cap; an undersized cap creates an explicit exception.
assumptions_latex: Indispensable formulation rows are not eligible for deletion.
\(R_v\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_v^0+|A_v|\le R_v\) is the row-cap feasibility condition.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The row-count condition is coherent, but the indispensable/removable classification and mandatory cap-exception behavior are implementation policies without cited support.

children.title: Budget-Exhaustion Regimes
children.top_down_role: Selection behavior after available cut or row capacity is consumed.

knowledge_statements.title: Budget-Exhaustion Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies cut admission when round, node, or row capacity is exhausted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a candidate set \(C\) and remaining capacities \(q_r,q_v,q_R\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) for the round, node, and relaxation rows, define effective capacity \(q=\min\{q_r,q_v,q_R\}\). The regime is open when \(q\ge|C|\), selective when \(0<q<|C|\), and exhausted when \(q=0\). In the open regime every otherwise admissible candidate may be accepted; in the selective regime admission must choose at most \(q\) candidates; in the exhausted regime no row-consuming candidate may be accepted unless capacity is restored by an allowed deletion or accounting reset.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Effective capacity is the smallest remaining budget; it induces open, selective, and exhausted admission regimes.
assumptions_latex: \(q_r,q_v,q_R\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\).
Each admitted candidate consumes one unit of every applicable capacity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The maximum number of immediately admissible row-consuming cuts is \(\min\{|C|,q\}\).

notation.meaning: remaining round, node, and row capacities

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The classification is correct under the stated unit-consumption assumption and definition is an appropriate content kind. No source supports these named regimes or their applicability to the solver architecture.

children.title: Learned Cut Selection
children.top_down_role: Data-driven ranking and portfolio selection for candidate cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Learned Cut Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines deterministic inference-time ranking by a trained cut-scoring model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given candidate cuts \(C\), a fixed trained scoring map \(f_\theta:\mathbb R^d\to\mathbb R\), feature vectors \(\phi(i)\in\mathbb R^d\), feasibility filters \(F(i)\in\{0,1\}\), and budget \(k\), compute \(s_i=f_\theta(\phi(i))\). Discard every \(i\) with \(F(i)=0\), rank the remainder by nonincreasing \(s_i\) using a fixed tie rule, and scan that order. Admit a candidate only if adding it preserves every active diversity and resource constraint. Stop when the list is exhausted or \(k\) cuts have been admitted, and output the selected set together with scores and model identifier \(\theta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed trained model scores candidates; deterministic ranking and hard feasibility, diversity, and budget filters determine the selected portfolio.
assumptions_latex: The model parameters \(\theta\), feature map \(\phi\), and tie rule are fixed during inference.
Every admitted cut is independently verified as valid before insertion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output has at most \(k\) cuts and satisfies all enforced hard constraints.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the correct content kind, but no machine-learning cut-selection source is cited. The domain of \(k\) is also unstated, and the training target and model provenance needed to characterize learned selection are unspecified.

children.title: Admission Threshold Policies
children.top_down_role: Threshold systems governing entry into the active relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Admission Threshold Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Converts quality, violation, stability, and diversity scores into an admission predicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For candidate cut \(i\), let \(Q_i\in[0,1]\) be its aggregate quality, \(e_i\ge0\) its efficacy, \(t_i\in[0,1]\) its stability, and \(D(i,S)=\min_{j\in S}\delta_{ij}\), with \(D(i,\varnothing)=1\). Given thresholds \(\tau_Q,\tau_e,\tau_t,\tau_D\), the conjunctive policy declares \(i\) threshold-admissible exactly when \[Q_i\ge\tau_Q,\qquad e_i\ge\tau_e,\qquad t_i\ge\tau_t,\qquad D(i,S)\ge\tau_D.\] Thresholds may depend on node depth or round, but their values must be fixed before scoring that candidate pool. Resource budgets and validity checks remain separate mandatory constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A candidate passes thresholding only if quality, efficacy, stability, and diversity each meet their predeclared minimum.
assumptions_latex: \(0\le\tau_Q,\tau_t,\tau_D\le1\) and \(\tau_e\ge0\).
Every candidate has already passed a validity check.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed conjunction defines threshold admissibility relative to retained set \(S\).

source_refs.locator: 10.2 Most Violated Cut Selection Rule p. 126

source_witnesses.locator: 10.2 Most Violated Cut Selection Rule p. 126

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conjunctive predicate is coherent and fits a threshold-policy leaf, but the cited most-violated-cut section does not inspectably support the added stability, diversity, and aggregate-quality thresholds or their adaptive schedule.

children.title: Admission Conflict Resolution
children.top_down_role: Resolution of incompatible or jointly excessive candidate subsets.

knowledge_statements.title: Admission Conflict Resolution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resolves competing admission rules by hard-constraint precedence and deterministic constrained ranking.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given candidate set \(C\), hard-admissibility predicate \(H(i,S)\), priority score \(Q_i\), budget \(k\), and deterministic tie order, initialize \(S=\varnothing\). Permanently reject every candidate failing validity. Rank the remainder by nonincreasing \(Q_i\). Scan this order and admit \(i\) exactly when \(|S|<k\) and \(H(i,S)=1\), where \(H\) conjunctively enforces threshold, diversity, numerical, and resource constraints. A hard constraint always overrides a favorable score; among candidates satisfying all hard constraints, score and then the tie order decide precedence. Output \(S\) and a rejection reason for every excluded candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Validity and hard constraints override scores; feasible conflicts are settled by quality ranking and a deterministic tie rule.
assumptions_latex: Validity is a nonoverridable hard constraint.
The score order and tie rule are fixed for the candidate pool.
\(k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|S|\le k\) and \(H(i,S_{<i})=1\) for every admitted candidate \(i\).

notation.meaning: cuts retained before candidate i is processed

children.title: Cut Storage-Lifecycle System
children.top_down_role: Separation among transient candidates, active rows, reusable global cuts, and locally scoped cuts.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Separation storage, global cut pools, delayed cut pools, and cut aging

children.title: Candidate-Cut Storage
children.top_down_role: Transient collections awaiting selection or rejection.

knowledge_statements.title: Candidate-Cut Storage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines transient storage before cut admission, postponement, or rejection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a branch-and-cut node \(v\), candidate-cut storage is a finite collection \(Q_v=\{(a_i,b_i,m_i):i\in I_v\}\), where each inequality \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\) has passed validity checking but has not entered the active relaxation. Metadata \(m_i\) records its validity scope, efficacy score, generator, and duplication status. A selection operation partitions \(Q_v\) into admitted, delayed, and rejected subsets; admitted cuts leave \(Q_v\), while rejected cuts are discarded unless explicitly transferred to another eligible store.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Candidate-cut storage holds valid generated cuts temporarily, with selection metadata, until each cut is admitted, delayed, transferred, or rejected.
assumptions_latex: Every stored inequality has been validated for its recorded scope.
The candidate collection is finite at each selection round.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_v=Q_v^{\mathrm{adm}}\mathbin{\dot\cup}Q_v^{\mathrm{delay}}\mathbin{\dot\cup}Q_v^{\mathrm{rej}}\).

notation.meaning: selection and validity metadata for cut i
