intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the Candidate-Cut Storage container and is internally coherent, but no citation supports the asserted lifecycle, metadata fields, or admitted/delayed/rejected partition. These conventions are implementation-dependent and cannot be reviewed reliably without a solver or branch-and-cut architecture source with a specific locator.

children.title: Active Relaxation Rows
children.top_down_role: Cuts currently participating in node relaxation optimization.

knowledge_statements.title: Active Relaxation Rows
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines cuts currently enforced in a node relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For node \(v\), let \(R_v\) denote its base continuous relaxation and let \(A_v\) be a finite set of admitted cuts. The active relaxation rows are precisely the inequalities in \(A_v\) included in the optimization model \[R_v^{\mathrm{act}}=R_v\cap\bigcap_{(a,b)\in A_v}\{x:a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\}.\] A stored cut is active only while its row participates in solving \(R_v^{\mathrm{act}}\); removal from the row system changes its status to inactive without invalidating or deleting it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Active rows are admitted cuts presently included in the node relaxation; removal from the model deactivates but does not necessarily delete them.
assumptions_latex: Each member of \(A_v\) is valid throughout the node's associated feasible region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(R_v^{\mathrm{act}}\subseteq R_v\), and every integer-feasible point associated with node \(v\) remains in \(R_v^{\mathrm{act}}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record fits Active Relaxation Rows, and the displayed relaxation construction is mathematically consistent. However, no cited source supports the distinction between removal, inactivity, retention, and deletion, so the lifecycle claim requires a specific source locator.

children.title: Reusable Global Cut Pool System
children.top_down_role: Repositories for globally valid cuts intended for later reuse.

children.title: Global Cut Pools
children.top_down_role: Repositories for reusable globally valid inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Cut Pools
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines reusable storage for globally valid inactive cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A global cut pool is a finite indexed collection \(G=\{(a_i,b_i,m_i):i\in I\}\) whose inequalities \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\le b_i\) are valid for every feasible solution of the original mixed-integer problem, independently of the node where they were generated. A pool member need not be active at any node. Subject to capacity and duplicate-management rules, it may be retrieved and inserted into the relaxation of any node whose formulation uses the same variable space and compatible presolve mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global cut pool stores globally valid, usually inactive inequalities that may be retrieved for compatible relaxations anywhere in the search tree.
assumptions_latex: Stored inequalities are globally valid for the original feasible set.
Any node using a stored row has a compatible variable mapping.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every search node \(v\) and \((a,b,m)\in G\), the node-feasible set is contained in \(\{x:a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\}\).

notation.meaning: cut metadata, including origin and activity history

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind and statement match Global Cut Pools, but the finiteness, inactive-row convention, capacity management, duplicate handling, and compatible-presolve retrieval semantics are implementation-specific and uncited. A source specifically documenting global cut-pool behavior is required.

children.title: Delayed Cut Pools
children.top_down_role: Repositories holding valid cuts outside the active relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Delayed Cut Pools
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines temporary storage for admissible cuts deferred from activation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(v\), a delayed cut pool \(D_v\) is a finite collection of valid, currently inactive cuts that were not selected for immediate insertion but remain eligible for reconsideration. Each cut \(c\in D_v\) carries a next-eligibility state \(t(c)\) and retention metadata. At a later relaxation state \(k\), only cuts satisfying \(k\ge t(c)\) are eligible for rescoring; selected cuts move to the active-row set, retained cuts remain delayed, and expired or dominated cuts leave \(D_v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A delayed pool retains valid cuts omitted from immediate activation and makes them eligible for rescoring at specified later relaxation states.
assumptions_latex: Every member is valid for every node at which its metadata permits retrieval.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_v^{k+1}=(D_v^k\setminus(S_k\cup P_k))\cup N_k\), where \(S_k\) is activated, \(P_k\) is expired, and \(N_k\) is newly delayed.

notation.meaning: delayed cut pool at node v
next state at which cut c may be reconsidered

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition belongs in Delayed Cut Pools, but the next-eligibility state, rescoring rule, and state-update equation describe a particular policy rather than a source-independent definition. No evidence is cited for that policy, so its mathematical formulation cannot be endorsed as written.

children.title: Pool Retrieval Policies
children.top_down_role: Policies governing reconsideration of stored cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Pool Retrieval Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies score-based retrieval of stored cuts for a node relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a pool \(G\), node relaxation solution \(\bar x_v\), eligibility predicate \(E_v(c)\), score \(s_v(c)\), threshold \(\tau\), and row budget \(B\). Form \(H_v=\{c\in G:E_v(c)=1,\ s_v(c)\ge\tau\}\), remove duplicates and cuts incompatible with the node formulation, order the remainder by nonincreasing score, and return at most the first \(B\) cuts. If fewer than \(B\) cuts qualify, return all qualifying cuts; if none qualify, return the empty set. Returned cuts enter candidate storage or the active relaxation according to the admission policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Filter pooled cuts for validity and compatibility, discard duplicates, rank qualifying cuts by score, and retrieve no more than the row budget.
assumptions_latex: \(B\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) and the pool is finite.
Eligibility implies validity at node \(v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned set \(S_v\) satisfies \(S_v\subseteq G\), \(|S_v|\le B\), and \(E_v(c)=1\) for every \(c\in S_v\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the correct content kind for Pool Retrieval Policies, and the inputs and output guarantees are clear. The threshold-and-budget ranking procedure is nevertheless one specific retrieval policy with no supporting citation; a solver manual or algorithm source with a precise locator is required.

children.title: Cross-Node Cut Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse of globally valid cuts across search nodes.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Node Cut Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes when a stored cut may be reused at another search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let cut \(c\) be generated at node \(u\) and considered at node \(v\). Cross-node reuse is admissible exactly when \(c\) is valid for the feasible region represented by \(v\) and its coefficients can be mapped consistently into the formulation of \(v\). In particular, every globally valid cut is scope-eligible at every compatible node. A locally valid cut whose scope is the subtree rooted at \(u\) is eligible at \(v\) only if \(v\) is a descendant of \(u\); otherwise reuse can remove feasible solutions and is forbidden.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut may be reused at another node only when its validity scope contains that node and its coefficients match the node formulation.
assumptions_latex: Each stored cut has explicit validity-scope metadata.
Node formulations provide consistent coefficient mappings.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{reuse}(c,v)\iff F_v\subseteq\{x:c(x)\le0\}\) and the formulation mapping for \(c\) is defined at \(v\).

notation.meaning: mixed-integer feasible region represented by node v
admissibility of reusing cut c at node v

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition is an appropriate content kind and the scope-safety principle matches Cross-Node Cut Reuse. However, the exact biconditional and formulation-mapping requirement have no cited support, and reuse can depend on transformations and solver-specific validity metadata. A specific authoritative source is required.

children.title: Local Cut Storage
children.top_down_role: Scope-aware storage for cuts restricted to designated subtrees.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Cut Storage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines scope-aware storage for subtree-valid cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A local cut store is a collection \(L=\{(c_i,r_i,m_i):i\in I\}\), where \(c_i\) is valid throughout a designated search subtree rooted at \(r_i\), but global validity is not asserted. At node \(v\), the eligible local cuts are \[L(v)=\{c_i:(c_i,r_i,m_i)\in L,\ v\text{ is a descendant of }r_i\}.\] Retrieval outside this scope is prohibited. When the subtree rooted at \(r_i\) is closed, its cuts may be purged unless another recorded scope independently justifies retention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local cut storage associates each cut with a subtree root and permits retrieval only at descendants within that validity scope.
assumptions_latex: The search tree has a well-defined ancestor relation.
Every stored cut is valid throughout its recorded subtree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(c\in L(v)\), the node-feasible set \(F_v\) satisfies \(F_v\subseteq\{x:c(x)\le0\}\).

notation.meaning: root of cut i's validity subtree
local cuts eligible at node v

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition matches Local Cut Storage and consistently models subtree validity. No citation supports the asserted storage, retrieval, and subtree-closure purging semantics, which are branch-and-cut implementation conventions rather than a uniquely standardized mathematical definition.

children.title: Cut Retirement Lifecycle
children.top_down_role: Lifecycle controls for removing ineffective or obsolete cuts.

children.title: Cut Aging
children.top_down_role: Tracking of declining cut activity or usefulness over time.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Aging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies inactivity-based aging of stored or active cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each retained cut \(c\), initialize its age by \(a_0(c)=0\). After relaxation solve \(k\), compute an activity predicate \(q_k(c)\), equal to one when the cut is sufficiently tight or otherwise credited by the retention rule. Update \[a_{k+1}(c)=\begin{cases}0,&q_k(c)=1,\\a_k(c)+1,&q_k(c)=0.\end{cases}\] A cut with \(a_{k+1}(c)\ge A\) becomes eligible for deactivation or purging, but aging alone does not alter validity. The output is the updated age and retirement eligibility flag.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut's age resets when it is credited as active and otherwise increases; reaching a threshold makes the cut eligible for retirement.
assumptions_latex: The age threshold satisfies \(A\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\).
The activity predicate is evaluated after each designated relaxation solve.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_k(c)\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\), and retirement eligibility occurs when \(a_k(c)\ge A\).

notation.meaning: age of cut c after state k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is suitable for the Cut Aging leaf, and the recurrence is well formed. The activity predicate, reset behavior, threshold interpretation, and resulting retirement eligibility are solver-dependent choices with no supporting source, so the particular algorithm needs direct evidence.

children.title: Cut Deactivation
children.top_down_role: Temporary removal of cuts from the active relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Deactivation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies removal of a cut from the active row system without deletion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an active-row set \(A_v\), retained-cut store \(P_v\), and an eligible cut \(c\in A_v\). Remove the row of \(c\) from the node relaxation and update \(A_v'=A_v\setminus\{c\}\). If retention is authorized, set \(P_v'=P_v\cup\{c\}\) with its validity scope and lifecycle metadata; otherwise pass \(c\) to the purging decision. Reoptimize or mark the relaxation stale. Deactivation changes enforcement status only and must not relabel a local cut as globally valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deactivation removes a cut from the active relaxation while optionally retaining it, with unchanged validity scope, for possible later reuse.
assumptions_latex: The cut belongs to the active-row set.
Any retained cut keeps its original validity-scope metadata.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c\notin A_v'\), and if retained then \(c\in P_v'\) with unchanged validity scope.

notation.meaning: inactive retained-cut store at node v

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits Cut Deactivation and clearly distinguishes deactivation from deletion. Its transfer to an inactive store, optional purging path, and stale-relaxation handling are implementation-specific and unsupported by any citation with an inspectable locator.

children.title: Cut Reactivation
children.top_down_role: Return of stored cuts when they become relevant again.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Reactivation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies validity-checked restoration of an inactive cut to a relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input node \(v\), inactive store \(P_v\), active-row set \(A_v\), and cut \(c\in P_v\). Verify that \(c\)'s validity scope contains \(v\), its formulation mapping is defined, and its reactivation score meets threshold \(\tau\). If all tests pass, set \(A_v'=A_v\cup\{c\}\), remove or mark \(c\) active in \(P_v\), reset its age, and reoptimize or mark the relaxation stale. If any test fails, leave \(A_v\) unchanged and return the failed condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reactivation restores an inactive cut only after scope, formulation, and score checks; successful restoration resets its age and invalidates the previous relaxation solution.
assumptions_latex: The inactive store preserves the cut's coefficients and validity scope.
The reactivation threshold \(\tau\) is fixed for the decision.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Successful reactivation gives \(c\in A_v'\) and preserves all node-feasible points; unsuccessful reactivation gives \(A_v'=A_v\).

notation.meaning: inactive cut store at node v

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm belongs in Cut Reactivation, but the mandatory score threshold, age reset, inactive-store update, and stale-relaxation behavior define a particular solver policy. No source is supplied to establish that this is the intended reactivation procedure.

children.title: Cut Purging
children.top_down_role: Permanent removal of obsolete or ineffective cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Purging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specifies permanent removal from managed cut stores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input managed stores \(S_1,\ldots,S_p\) and a cut \(c\) eligible for deletion. First ensure that \(c\) is not required as an active relaxation row, a validity certificate, or a referenced ancestor-scope record. If unreferenced and the purge predicate holds—such as expiration, domination, duplication, or a capacity decision—remove \(c\) and its lifecycle metadata from every \(S_j\). Otherwise retain it or deactivate it. Purging is irreversible within the current stored state, although an equivalent inequality may later be regenerated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Purging permanently removes an unneeded cut and its metadata from all managed stores after reference and retention checks succeed.
assumptions_latex: The set of managed stores is finite.
Reference checks cover active rows and required certificates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: On successful purging, \(c\notin\bigcup_{j=1}^{p}S_j\); otherwise the stores remain unchanged except for permitted deactivation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is an appropriate kind for Cut Purging, but the required reference checks, certificate retention, ancestor-scope handling, purge predicates, and removal from every managed store are implementation-specific and uncited. Direct documentation is needed before accepting this procedure.

children.title: Branching-Cutting Coupling
children.top_down_role: Mutual influence of relaxation strengthening, branching information, and search-tree evolution.

children.title: Cutting-Branching Transition Policy
children.top_down_role: Policies allocating effort between further strengthening and subdivision.

children.title: Cut-Saturation Detection
children.top_down_role: Signals indicating diminishing value from further separation.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Saturation Detection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a finite-window trigger for ending a cutting phase.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z_k\) be the valid relaxation bound after cutting round \(k\), and let \(V_k\) be the best violation or efficacy among newly separated admissible cuts. For window length \(w\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), tolerances \(\varepsilon_z,\varepsilon_v\ge0\), and minimum round \(k_0\), declare cut saturation at round \(k\ge k_0+w\) when \[|z_k-z_{k-w}|\le\varepsilon_z\max\{1,|z_k|\}\quad\text{and}\quad\max_{k-w<j\le k}V_j\le\varepsilon_v.\] The condition is an operational transition trigger, not a certificate that no stronger valid cut exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cutting is declared saturated when recent bound improvement and the best newly separated cut value both remain below prescribed tolerances.
assumptions_latex: All \(z_j\) use the same bound convention and objective scaling.
All \(V_j\) use a common nonnegative efficacy measure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If the displayed predicate holds, the policy may terminate the cutting phase and branch; it does not certify closure of the relaxation gap.

notation.meaning: relaxation bound after cutting round k
best new-cut violation or efficacy at round k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition is the correct role for Cut-Saturation Detection, and the statement appropriately denies that the trigger is an optimality certificate. The finite-window conjunction, normalization, efficacy statistic, and transition rule are a particular heuristic policy with no cited source, so the exact predicate requires evidence.

children.title: Branching-Transition Triggers
children.top_down_role: Conditions prompting subdivision of the current search node.

assumptions_latex: \(P_t\) is the current node relaxation after cut round \(t\).
The separation oracle reports candidate cuts with normalized efficacy and estimated processing cost.
At least one fractional integer variable is eligible for branching.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(B_t=1\) initiates branching; \(B_t=0\) permits another separation round.

notation.meaning: maximum normalized efficacy among cuts returned at round t
cumulative separation effort at the node

review_flags: Exact trigger thresholds and resource accounting are solver-policy dependent.
No supplied locator directly supports this transition predicate.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A deterministic node-level trigger combining cut exhaustion, diminishing improvement, and a separation budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix thresholds \(\varepsilon_e,\varepsilon_z,\bar w>0\), and let \(z_t\) be the relaxation bound after round \(t\). Define the branching-transition trigger by
\[
B_t=\mathbf 1\!\left\{e_t\leq\varepsilon_e\;\lor\; |z_t-z_{t-1}|\leq\varepsilon_z\;\lor\;w_t\geq\bar w\right\}.
\]
If \(B_t=1\) and the relaxation solution is not integer feasible, separation stops at the node and an eligible branching disjunction is selected. If \(B_t=0\), another separation round may be performed. Infeasibility, integral feasibility, and incumbent pruning remain terminal node outcomes rather than branching transitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch when useful cuts are exhausted, recent bound improvement is negligible, or the node’s separation budget is spent, provided a fractional branching candidate remains.
knowledge_statements.title: Branching-Transition Triggers

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition fits the leaf, but the disjunctive trigger and thresholds are solver-policy choices with no supporting source or locator.

children.title: Residual-Separation Value
children.top_down_role: Assessment of remaining strengthening potential before branching.

assumptions_latex: \(x^t\) is an optimal solution of the current node relaxation.
Every candidate inequality \(a^cx\leq b\) is valid for the node’s integer-feasible set.
Cut costs are strictly positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_t\) quantifies the best remaining normalized violation per unit separation cost, and \(V_t=0\) when no candidate separates \(x^t\).

notation.meaning: cuts still available from the separation family at the current node
positive computational cost assigned to cut c

review_flags: The normalization and cost model are policy choices rather than canonical branch-and-cut definitions.
No supplied locator directly supports this metric.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A local value metric for deciding whether further separation justifies delaying branching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(c=(a,b)\in\mathcal C_t\), define its scale-normalized violation at \(x^t\) by
\[
\nu(c;x^t)=\frac{(a^cx^t-b)_+}{\max\{1,\lVert a\rVert_2\}}.
\]
The residual-separation value is
\[
V_t=\sup_{c\in\mathcal C_t}\frac{\nu(c;x^t)}{\kappa(c)},
\]
with \(\sup\varnothing=0\). Thus \(V_t\geq0\); it is zero precisely when the available family contains no cut violated by \(x^t\), and it is positive when further separation can remove the current solution. A transition policy may compare \(V_t\) with a prescribed threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual-separation value is the largest scale-normalized violation obtainable from the remaining cut family per unit estimated separation cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Separation Value

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is internally coherent and fits the leaf, but its normalization and cost-adjusted supremum are proposed policy choices unsupported by a cited source.

children.title: Transition-Mistiming Consequences
children.top_down_role: Search effects caused by branching too early or cutting too long.

assumptions_latex: Each separation round and each processed search node has positive computational cost.
The chosen cuts and branching decisions preserve all integer-feasible solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A transition is mistimed relative to the stated cost model when it increases total work without improving correctness.

notation.meaning: number of additional separation rounds before branching
number of subsequently processed search nodes

review_flags: This formalizes a cost-model boundary; quantitative consequences depend on solver and instance behavior.
No supplied locator directly supports the comparative-work statement.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A work-based boundary distinguishing premature branching from excessive separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(c_s>0\) be the cost per separation round and \(c_n>0\) the average cost per processed node, and define
\[
W(r)=r c_s+c_nN(r).
\]
Relative to a minimizing choice \(r^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{r\geq0}W(r)\), branching too early means choosing \(r<r^*\): saved separation work is outweighed by the larger tree, so \(c_n[N(r)-N(r^*)]>(r^*-r)c_s\). Branching too late means choosing \(r>r^*\): any tree reduction is outweighed by extra separation, so \((r-r^*)c_s>c_n[N(r^*)-N(r)]\). Both choices preserve validity but increase work.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Premature branching can enlarge the tree; delayed branching can spend more on cuts than it saves in node processing. Both preserve correctness but increase modeled work.
knowledge_statements.title: Transition-Mistiming Consequences

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, but the strict inequalities do not follow when the argmin contains multiple choices, and the domain of the integer round count r is not specified. A source or corrected mathematical version is required.

children.title: Cut Effects on Branching Evidence
children.top_down_role: Changes in fractional structure and branching information after separation.

assumptions_latex: A valid cut is added to a node relaxation and the relaxation is reoptimized.
Branching scores are computed from the relaxation solution, basis, reduced costs, or predicted child bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Branching evidence depending on altered relaxation data must be recomputed or explicitly certified invariant before reuse.

notation.meaning: node relaxation before adding the cut

review_flags: The recomputation rule is standard solver hygiene, but the supplied locators do not directly document it.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effects of separation on relaxation-derived branching scores at one search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a valid inequality \(a^cx\leq b\), let \(P'=P\cap\{x:a^cx\leq b\}\). Then \(P'\subseteq P\), so the optimal relaxation solution, active set, basis, reduced costs, fractional variables, and estimated child bounds may change after reoptimization. Consequently, a score \(S_j(P)\) derived from any changed datum need not equal \(S_j(P')\). Reusing \(S_j(P)\) is valid only when the score definition supplies an invariance certificate for the modification or when it is retained merely as historical evidence with its age recorded. Current-solution branching eligibility must be evaluated on \(P'\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut can change the fractional solution and all branching evidence derived from it. Such scores require recomputation or an explicit invariance certificate before current use.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut Effects on Branching Evidence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Cuts can change relaxation-derived branching data, but the mandatory recomputation/invariance-certificate rule is an implementation policy not supported by a cited source.

children.title: Tree Information for Cut Generation
children.top_down_role: Use of branching disjunctions, node bounds, and explored-tree information in separation.

assumptions_latex: The integer-feasible set \(X_I\) is covered by a finite branching disjunction.
Each proposed inequality is valid on the corresponding disjunctive term.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The common inequality is globally valid for \(X_I\) and may be exchanged from tree analysis to the cut system.

notation.meaning: integer-feasible set of the original formulation
a common inequality inferred from all disjunctive terms

review_flags: A direct source for tree-derived globally valid cuts is not present among the supplied locators.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global cut inference from a complete branching disjunction, rather than reuse of node-local bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose
\[
X_I\subseteq\bigcup_{k=1}^m D_k
\]
and the explored branching information establishes
\[
\alpha^cx\leq\beta\quad\text{for every }x\in X_I\cap D_k,
\qquad k=1,\ldots,m.
\]
Then \(\alpha^cx\leq\beta\) is valid for every \(x\in X_I\), because each such point belongs to at least one disjunctive term. Node bounds, infeasible children, and solved child relaxations may be used to establish the termwise premises. If the analyzed terms do not cover \(X_I\), the resulting inequality is valid only within the covered subtree unless independent global validity is established.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut inferred from tree information is globally valid when the analyzed branching terms cover every integer-feasible point and the cut is valid on every term.
knowledge_statements.title: Tree Information for Cut Generation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The covering argument is mathematically sound and the principle kind fits the topic, but no citation or inspectable locator supports the tree-information interpretation and exchange claim.

children.title: Branching–Separation Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Allocation of bounding effort between stronger cuts and more informative branching.

assumptions_latex: Separation and branching alternatives have estimated positive computational costs.
Their predicted bound gains are measured on a common nonnegative scale.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The next action maximizes predicted bound gain per unit cost, subject to validity and resource limits.

notation.meaning: predicted bound gain from another separation round
predicted aggregate child-bound gain from branching
estimated costs of separation and branching

review_flags: The gain-per-cost decision rule is a formal policy model, not a universal optimality theorem.
No supplied locator directly supports this allocation principle.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A myopic resource-allocation principle for choosing separation or branching at a fractional node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define the marginal efficiencies
\[
\rho_s=\frac{g_s}{c_s},\qquad \rho_b=\frac{g_b}{c_b}.
\]
Subject to the remaining node budget, choose separation when \(\rho_s>\rho_b\), choose branching when \(\rho_b>\rho_s\), and resolve equality by a fixed tie rule. Here \(g_s\) must account for the expected strengthening from admissible cuts, while \(g_b\) must aggregate both children under the solver’s stated scoring convention. Estimates based on stale relaxation data are not comparable without recalibration. This rule defines a local allocation policy and does not assert global minimization of the eventual search-tree cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allocate the next unit of bounding effort to cuts or branching according to predicted bound gain per unit cost, using current and comparably calibrated evidence.
knowledge_statements.title: Branching–Separation Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record clearly labels a myopic policy rather than a theorem, but the gain-per-cost rule and aggregation convention have no supporting source.

children.title: Solver Subsystem Interface Suite
children.top_down_role: Interfaces between branch-and-cut and adjacent solver subsystems.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Constraint handlers, separators, branching rules, and row-management interfaces

children.title: Presolve Cut-Mapping Interface
children.top_down_role: Transformation, recovery, and validity tracking across original and presolved models.

children.title: Presolve Transformation Space
children.top_down_role: Transformed model space in which solver-side cut processing occurs.

assumptions_latex: Presolve records every substitution, fixing, aggregation, and deleted constraint needed for reconstruction.
The recorded transformation is exact on the feasible sets under consideration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The presolved feasible set and original feasible set correspond through the recorded affine reconstruction map.
review_flags: Presolve equivalence and integrality preservation require a dedicated solver or textbook source.
The supplied locators do not directly address presolve transformation maps.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: An exact affine model of the variable space exposed by the presolve cut-mapping interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the original feasible set and \(F_p\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) the presolved feasible set. The presolve transformation space is represented by an affine map \(R(y)=Ty+r\) together with a transformation ledger such that
\[
F=R(F_p)=\{Ty+r:y\in F_p\}.
\]
For mixed-integer models, the ledger must additionally certify that every \(y\in F_p\) satisfying the presolved integrality restrictions maps to an original point satisfying the original integrality restrictions, and that every original mixed-integer feasible point has at least one presolved preimage. Conditional transformations carry their activation scope in the ledger.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Presolve exposes a reduced variable space plus an affine reconstruction map and ledger that exactly recover original feasible points and preserve required integrality.
knowledge_statements.title: Presolve Transformation Space

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: An affine reconstruction is a useful restricted representation, but general presolve transformations need not yield the stated exact affine feasible-set equality. The assumptions and integrality correspondence require dedicated sourcing.

children.title: Forward Cut Mapping
children.top_down_role: Transfer of cut information into the presolved representation.

assumptions_latex: The exact presolve reconstruction is \(x=Ty+r\).
The original-space inequality \(a^cx\leq b\) is valid on the transformation’s declared scope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The substituted inequality \((T^ca)^cy\leq b-a^cr\) is valid for all presolved points in that scope.

notation.meaning: original-space cut normal and right-hand side
presolved-space cut normal and right-hand side

review_flags: The algebraic substitution is unambiguous, but a source specific to presolve cut mapping is still required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine forward mapping of an original-space inequality into presolved coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Substitution of \(x=Ty+r\) into the original-space cut \(a^cx\leq b\) gives
\[
a^c(Ty+r)=(T^ca)^cy+a^cr\leq b.
\]
Hence the forward-mapped presolved cut is
\[
\pi^cy\leq\delta,
\qquad \pi=T^ca,
\qquad \delta=b-a^cr.
\]
It is valid for every presolved point whose reconstruction lies in the validity scope of the original cut. If the original cut is node-local or depends on conditional presolve reductions, the mapped cut inherits that same scope; affine substitution alone does not make a local inequality global.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Map an original cut forward by substituting the affine presolve reconstruction. The mapped cut inherits every locality or conditional-validity restriction of its source.
knowledge_statements.title: Forward Cut Mapping

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The affine substitution is algebraically correct and the representation kind fits, but no source with a specific locator supports the presolve cut-mapping interface and scope inheritance.

children.title: Original-Space Cut Recovery
children.top_down_role: Recovery of cut representations in original model coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Original-Space Cut Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact recovery of a presolved cut through an affine reconstruction map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The presolved cut \(\pi^T y\leq\delta\) has an exact affine original-space recovery if and only if there exists \(a\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying
\[
T^T a=\pi.
\]
For any such \(a\), set \(b=\delta+a^T r\). Then
\[
a^T x=a^T(Ty+r)=\pi^T y+a^T r\leq\delta+a^T r=b
\]
for every reconstructed point in the cut's declared scope. Thus recoverability is equivalent to \(\pi\in\operatorname{range}(T^T)\). If this condition fails, the cut cannot be represented by a single original-space inequality through this affine map and must remain in presolved space or be recovered through the full transformation ledger.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A presolved cut has a single affine original-space recovery exactly when its normal lies in the range of the transpose of the reconstruction matrix.
assumptions_latex: The presolve reconstruction is \(x=Ty+r\).
A presolved inequality \(\pi^T y\leq\delta\) is valid on a declared scope.
The transformation ledger is available for checking recoverability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An original-space affine recovery exists exactly when \(\pi\in\operatorname{range}(T^T)\), subject to inherited scope restrictions.
review_flags: Recovery through non-affine or inequality-generating presolve transformations is outside this formulation.
A dedicated source for solver cut postsolve is required.

children.title: Mapping-Validity Tracking
children.top_down_role: Tracking of validity scope across model transformations.

knowledge_statements.title: Mapping-Validity Tracking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A ledger certificate governing where mapped cuts may safely be installed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A mapping-validity certificate for \(c\) is the tuple
\[
\mathcal V(c)=(L(c),S(c),v,\sigma),
\]
where \(v\) identifies the active presolve-transformation version and \(\sigma\) records numerical tolerances and rounding operations. Each entry of \(L(c)\) states a source inequality, a validity-preserving transformation, and its required scope. The checker accepts \(\mathcal V(c)\) at node \(u\) only if every ledger step is applicable under version \(v\), \(u\in S(c)\), and all conditional reductions used by the mapping remain active at \(u\). Failure of any check forbids installation or requires remapping from a valid ancestor representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Track each mapped cut with a transformation ledger, scope, version, and numerical policy. Install it only where every recorded validity condition still holds.
assumptions_latex: Every presolve transformation and cut-mapping operation is recorded in an append-only derivation ledger.
Every validity scope has a machine-checkable representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A cut may be installed only where its ledger certificate establishes validity under all active transformations and scope restrictions.

notation.meaning: ordered derivation ledger for the cut
set of search nodes where the cut is certified valid

review_flags: The certificate fields describe an interface contract needing implementation-specific sourcing.
No supplied locator directly addresses mapping-validity tracking.

children.title: Propagation-Conflict Exchange Interface
children.top_down_role: Exchange of domain deductions, infeasibility explanations, and strengthened rows.

children.title: Domain Propagation Exchange
children.top_down_role: Transfer of domain deductions between solver components.

assumptions_latex: Each exchanged propagator is sound: every returned bound is implied by the current constraints and input bounds.
Bounds are updated monotonically by intersection.
Variable domains admit finite stabilization or a prescribed tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exchange terminates at a common propagation fixpoint or reports an empty domain as infeasibility.

notation.meaning: current Cartesian product of variable domains
sound domain contractor supplied by subsystem i

review_flags: A source for the subsystem exchange protocol and its termination assumptions is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous exchange of implied variable bounds among propagation-capable solver subsystems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input the node constraints and initial domain \(D^0\). At iteration \(k\), query each subsystem for a sound contraction \(P_i(D^k)\subseteq D^k\), and update
\[
D^{k+1}=D^k\cap\bigcap_{i=1}^m P_i(D^k).
\]
Attach to every tightened bound its scope and an implication explanation. If any component of \(D^{k+1}\) is empty, stop and return node infeasibility with the collected explanations. If \(D^{k+1}=D^k\), or no bound changes beyond the declared tolerance, stop and return \(D^k\). Otherwise broadcast the tightened bounds to all affected subsystems and repeat. Local bounds are never exported outside their certified subtree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly exchange sound bound tightenings among subsystems until no domain changes. Empty domains certify node infeasibility; local bounds retain their subtree scope.
knowledge_statements.title: Domain Propagation Exchange

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits and finite stabilization is explicitly assumed, but the exchange protocol, explanation requirements, and fixpoint claim lack a supporting source with a specific locator.

children.title: Conflict Explanation Exchange
children.top_down_role: Transfer of infeasibility explanations for conflict processing.

knowledge_statements.title: Conflict Explanation Exchange
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Machine-checkable exchange of conflict and propagation explanations between solver subsystems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A conflict explanation is accepted when a checker verifies
\[
C\land\bigwedge_{\ell\in E}\ell\models\bot.
\]
A propagation explanation for a bound literal \(q\) is accepted when the checker verifies
\[
C\land\bigwedge_{\ell\in E}\ell\models q.
\]
The exchanged certificate contains \(E\), identifiers for the constraints of \(C\) used by the check, the conclusion, and the intersection of all premise scopes. A receiving subsystem may derive a learned constraint or perform propagation only within that certified scope. Explanations involving deleted or transformed constraints must include a valid reconstruction ledger; otherwise the exchange is rejected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exchange a conflict or propagated bound only with premises that mechanically imply it, plus constraint identifiers, transformation history, and the common validity scope.
assumptions_latex: A finite set of bound literals \(E\) is claimed to imply a contradiction or propagated bound under the active constraint system \(C\).
Every literal and constraint used by the explanation carries a validity scope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A checked explanation certifies the exchanged conflict or bound implication throughout the intersection of its premises' scopes.

notation.meaning: finite set of bound literals forming the explanation
propagated bound literal when the explanation is not a conflict

review_flags: The logical certificate is standard, but encoding and checking rules require a dedicated conflict-analysis source.

children.title: Strengthened-Row Exchange
children.top_down_role: Transfer of strengthened relaxation rows derived from deductions.

assumptions_latex: The node relaxation is \(P_N=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:A_Nx\le b_N,\ \ell_N\le x\le u_N\}\).
The incoming inequality \(\alpha^\top x\le\beta\) carries a validity scope \(S\) and is valid for every integer-feasible point in \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exchange receives \((\alpha,\beta,S)\), checks dimensional consistency and the declared scope, and computes the violation \(v=\alpha^\top\bar x-\beta\) at the current relaxation solution \(\bar x\). If \(v>\varepsilon\), it installs \(\alpha^\top x\le\beta\) at every node whose domain is contained in \(S\); otherwise it leaves the relaxation unchanged. The output is the updated row set together with the row's scope tag, or a rejection status when validity or scope compatibility cannot be established.

notation.meaning: Current branch-and-bound node and its relaxation
Current relaxation solution and acceptance tolerance
Validity scope of the exchanged row

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-independent contract for accepting and installing a strengthened relaxation row.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The exchange receives \((\alpha,\beta,S)\), checks dimensional consistency and the declared scope, and computes the violation \(v=\alpha^\top\bar x-\beta\) at the current relaxation solution \(\bar x\). If \(v>\varepsilon\), it installs \(\alpha^\top x\le\beta\) at every node whose domain is contained in \(S\); otherwise it leaves the relaxation unchanged. The output is the updated row set together with the row's scope tag, or a rejection status when validity or scope compatibility cannot be established.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strengthened row is accepted only with a compatible validity scope and sufficient violation, then installed precisely at nodes covered by that scope.
knowledge_statements.title: Strengthened-Row Exchange

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No cited source supports the claimed acceptance, violation-testing, installation, or rejection protocol. These interface semantics vary by solver, so the algorithm cannot be validated from the unrelated local inventory.

children.title: Exchange Scope Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Applicability limits for exchanged deductions, explanations, or rows.

assumptions_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be the original feasible set and \(D_N\) the domain imposed at node \(N\).
A contributed statement is represented by \(q(x)\le0\) with declared scope \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A contribution is global only if \(q(x)\le0\) for every \(x\in F\), and it is local to \(N\) only if \(q(x)\le0\) for every \(x\in F\cap D_N\). A local contribution may be inherited by a descendant \(M\) only when \(D_M\subseteq D_N\). Installing it at an ancestor, sibling, or unrelated node without an independent validity check can remove a feasible point and invalidate the search. Thus scope metadata must accompany every exchanged bound, explanation, or row and must not be widened by the receiver.

notation.meaning: Predicate supplied by a callback subsystem

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes global validity from node-local validity and identifies scope leakage.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A contribution is global only if \(q(x)\le0\) for every \(x\in F\), and it is local to \(N\) only if \(q(x)\le0\) for every \(x\in F\cap D_N\). A local contribution may be inherited by a descendant \(M\) only when \(D_M\subseteq D_N\). Installing it at an ancestor, sibling, or unrelated node without an independent validity check can remove a feasible point and invalidate the search. Thus scope metadata must accompany every exchanged bound, explanation, or row and must not be widened by the receiver.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global contributions hold on the full feasible set; local ones hold only within a node domain and may pass only to contained descendant domains.
knowledge_statements.title: Exchange Scope Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The global-versus-local validity distinction is mathematically plausible and failure_boundary fits the container, but the mandatory metadata and inheritance contract lack a cited, inspectable source.

children.title: Warm-Start Basis-Reoptimization System
children.top_down_role: Reoptimization infrastructure for repeatedly modified node relaxations.

children.title: Warm-Start State Transfer
children.top_down_role: Reusable optimization state across modified node relaxations.

assumptions_latex: The previous LP state contains basis-status vectors, a basis matrix \(B\), and optional factorization and pricing data.
Rows and columns have stable identifiers across the model transition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Given an old state \(W\) and a modified LP, the transfer maps statuses through stable row and column identifiers, discards entries for deleted objects, and initializes each new row or column with a solver-valid default status. It reuses the stored factorization only when the mapped basis matrix is unchanged and numerically compatible; otherwise it marks the factorization stale. The mapped state is then checked for a square nonsingular basis. If that check succeeds, the algorithm outputs a warm-start state \(W'\); otherwise it invokes basis repair or returns a cold-start request.

notation.meaning: Basis matrix represented by the old state

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract state-transfer protocol for simplex reoptimization after LP modification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an old state \(W\) and a modified LP, the transfer maps statuses through stable row and column identifiers, discards entries for deleted objects, and initializes each new row or column with a solver-valid default status. It reuses the stored factorization only when the mapped basis matrix is unchanged and numerically compatible; otherwise it marks the factorization stale. The mapped state is then checked for a square nonsingular basis. If that check succeeds, the algorithm outputs a warm-start state \(W'\); otherwise it invokes basis repair or returns a cold-start request.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Warm-start transfer maps basis states by stable identifiers, reuses compatible numerical data, and requests repair or a cold start when the mapped basis is invalid.
knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Start State Transfer

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Stable-identifier mapping, default statuses, factorization reuse, compatibility checks, and cold-start behavior are implementation-dependent and unsupported by any citation.

children.title: Basis Preservation
children.top_down_role: Retention of compatible basis information after relaxation changes.

assumptions_latex: An LP has constraint matrix \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and a basis index set \(I\) with \(|I|=m\).
The associated basis matrix \(B=A_I\) is nonsingular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The basis \(I\) is preservable across a model update when the update neither removes nor changes any basic column and the resulting matrix \(B=A_I\) remains square and nonsingular. Changes only to the objective vector, right-hand side, or variable bounds do not destroy this algebraic basis, although they may destroy primal feasibility, dual feasibility, or both. In that case the preserved basis remains a valid simplex starting basis, and reoptimization may begin by restoring the violated feasibility conditions rather than constructing a new basis.

notation.meaning: Basis matrix formed from basic columns

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic preservation condition for a simplex basis under common LP updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The basis \(I\) is preservable across a model update when the update neither removes nor changes any basic column and the resulting matrix \(B=A_I\) remains square and nonsingular. Changes only to the objective vector, right-hand side, or variable bounds do not destroy this algebraic basis, although they may destroy primal feasibility, dual feasibility, or both. In that case the preserved basis remains a valid simplex starting basis, and reoptimization may begin by restoring the violated feasibility conditions rather than constructing a new basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A basis is preserved when all basic columns survive unchanged and remain square and nonsingular; changed bounds, costs, or right-hand sides may still require feasibility restoration.
knowledge_statements.title: Basis Preservation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algebraic preservation condition is plausible and condition is an appropriate knowledge kind, but no simplex reference with a specific locator is supplied to support the modeling convention and reoptimization claims.

children.title: Basis Repair After Modifications
children.top_down_role: Restoration of usable basis states after structural changes.

assumptions_latex: The modified LP has \(m'\) independent equality rows after slack-variable augmentation.
A mapped candidate basis may contain deleted, unavailable, duplicate, or linearly dependent columns.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Repair first removes mapped basic columns that are absent or linearly dependent in the modified matrix. It then scans eligible slack, structural, and artificial columns in a fixed priority order, adding a column only when it increases the current rank, until \(m'\) columns have been selected. Statuses of displaced columns are reset to admissible nonbasic bounds. If the resulting matrix \(B'\) satisfies \(\operatorname{rank}(B')=m'\), the algorithm outputs the repaired basis and refactorizes it; if no such completion is found, it reports repair failure and requests basis reconstruction or a cold start.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-based basis repair following row or column modifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Repair first removes mapped basic columns that are absent or linearly dependent in the modified matrix. It then scans eligible slack, structural, and artificial columns in a fixed priority order, adding a column only when it increases the current rank, until \(m'\) columns have been selected. Statuses of displaced columns are reset to admissible nonbasic bounds. If the resulting matrix \(B'\) satisfies \(\operatorname{rank}(B')=m'\), the algorithm outputs the repaired basis and refactorizes it; if no such completion is found, it reports repair failure and requests basis reconstruction or a cold start.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Basis repair deletes unavailable or dependent basic columns and adds rank-increasing eligible columns until it obtains a nonsingular basis or declares failure.
knowledge_statements.title: Basis Repair After Modifications

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rank-completion idea is plausible, but the eligible-column classes, fixed priority order, status resets, artificial-column use, and failure behavior require an authoritative simplex implementation source.

children.title: Reoptimization Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where retained state becomes incompatible or counterproductive.

assumptions_latex: Warm-start reoptimization attempts to reuse a basis factorization after structural or numerical modification.
For \(\delta\ge0\), consider \(B_\delta=\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1+\delta\end{pmatrix}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At \(\delta=0\), the candidate basis \(B_0\) is singular because \(\det(B_0)=0\), so no simplex basis inverse exists. For \(\delta>0\), \(\det(B_\delta)=\delta\), while the condition number diverges as \(\delta\downarrow0\); consequently a previously acceptable factorization may become numerically unusable under an arbitrarily small modification. More generally, deleted basic columns, changed row dimension, rank loss, incompatible scaling, or stale identifier mappings defeat direct state reuse. Warm starting therefore carries no unconditional guarantee of fewer pivots or lower time than basis reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural and numerical mechanisms that invalidate simplex warm starts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(\delta=0\), the candidate basis \(B_0\) is singular because \(\det(B_0)=0\), so no simplex basis inverse exists. For \(\delta>0\), \(\det(B_\delta)=\delta\), while the condition number diverges as \(\delta\downarrow0\); consequently a previously acceptable factorization may become numerically unusable under an arbitrarily small modification. More generally, deleted basic columns, changed row dimension, rank loss, incompatible scaling, or stale identifier mappings defeat direct state reuse. Warm starting therefore carries no unconditional guarantee of fewer pivots or lower time than basis reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Warm-start reuse fails when the mapped basis is singular, structurally incompatible, or ill-conditioned, and it does not guarantee faster reoptimization.
knowledge_statements.title: Reoptimization Failure Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The singularity example is correct, but the condition-number convention and broader numerical-reuse and performance claims are not sourced. The selected failure_boundary kind fits the leaf.

children.title: User-Cut Callbacks
children.top_down_role: Extension interfaces for user-generated relaxation-strengthening inequalities.

assumptions_latex: The original mixed-integer feasible set is \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), and the current node relaxation has solution \(\bar x\).
The callback can generate inequalities \(\alpha^\top x\le\beta\) valid for every \(x\in F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At an eligible relaxation callback, initialize an empty candidate set and evaluate the separation routine at \(\bar x\). For each returned inequality \(\alpha^\top x\le\beta\), verify its dimensions and declared global validity, then submit it when \(\alpha^\top\bar x>\beta+\varepsilon\). The solver adds accepted inequalities to the relaxation and resolves it. The callback terminates when separation finds no sufficiently violated valid inequality or when its prescribed cut budget is exhausted. Its output is a set of relaxation-strengthening inequalities; it must not submit an inequality that excludes any point of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-independent semantics of globally valid user cuts at relaxation solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At an eligible relaxation callback, initialize an empty candidate set and evaluate the separation routine at \(\bar x\). For each returned inequality \(\alpha^\top x\le\beta\), verify its dimensions and declared global validity, then submit it when \(\alpha^\top\bar x>\beta+\varepsilon\). The solver adds accepted inequalities to the relaxation and resolves it. The callback terminates when separation finds no sufficiently violated valid inequality or when its prescribed cut budget is exhausted. Its output is a set of relaxation-strengthening inequalities; it must not submit an inequality that excludes any point of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A user-cut callback separates a relaxation solution, submits sufficiently violated globally valid inequalities, and stops when no useful cut remains or its budget is exhausted.
knowledge_statements.title: User-Cut Callbacks

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is suitable for the callback topic, but callback eligibility, cut validation, acceptance, reoptimization, and termination behavior vary by solver and have no supporting citation.

children.title: Dynamic Constraint Enforcement Callbacks
children.top_down_role: Interfaces for dynamically enforcing omitted model constraints.

children.title: Lazy-Constraint Submission
children.top_down_role: Submission of omitted model constraints through lazy callbacks.

assumptions_latex: The intended feasible set is \(F=F_0\cap\bigcap_{j\in J}\{x:g_j(x)\le0\}\), where the indexed constraints are initially omitted.
A callback solution \(\bar x\in F_0\) and a separation oracle for the omitted family are available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: On invocation, the callback computes \(V(\bar x)=\{j\in J:g_j(\bar x)>\varepsilon\}\). If \(V(\bar x)\ne\varnothing\), it submits one or more constraints \(g_j(x)\le0\) with \(j\in V(\bar x)\), causing \(\bar x\) to be rejected or the relaxation to be resolved. If \(V(\bar x)=\varnothing\) and the oracle is complete, the omitted family is satisfied at \(\bar x\). The procedure ends after no violation is found or a submission budget is reached, and returns the submitted model-enforcing constraints.

notation.meaning: Violated omitted constraints at the callback solution

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dynamic submission of omitted constraints that define the intended feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: On invocation, the callback computes \(V(\bar x)=\{j\in J:g_j(\bar x)>\varepsilon\}\). If \(V(\bar x)\ne\varnothing\), it submits one or more constraints \(g_j(x)\le0\) with \(j\in V(\bar x)\), causing \(\bar x\) to be rejected or the relaxation to be resolved. If \(V(\bar x)=\varnothing\) and the oracle is complete, the omitted family is satisfied at \(\bar x\). The procedure ends after no violation is found or a submission budget is reached, and returns the submitted model-enforcing constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lazy submission detects omitted model constraints violated by a callback solution, submits them, and rejects or reoptimizes that solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Lazy-Constraint Submission

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dynamic-enforcement algorithm is plausible, but invocation timing, rejection versus reoptimization, budget termination, and tolerance assumptions require an authoritative lazy-constraint source.

children.title: Incumbent Enforcement
children.top_down_role: Constraint enforcement when candidate integer solutions are inspected.

assumptions_latex: The intended feasible set is \(F=F_0\cap\bigcap_{j\in J}\{x:g_j(x)\le0\}\).
The separation oracle is complete for the omitted family at every integer candidate \(\hat x\in F_0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For an integer candidate \(\hat x\), the callback certificate is the oracle result \(V(\hat x)=\{j\in J:g_j(\hat x)>\varepsilon\}\). If \(V(\hat x)\ne\varnothing\), any returned violated constraint certifies that \(\hat x\notin F\), so the candidate must be rejected and the constraint submitted. If \(V(\hat x)=\varnothing\), completeness of the oracle certifies \(g_j(\hat x)\le\varepsilon\) for every \(j\in J\); hence \(\hat x\) satisfies the omitted family to tolerance and may pass this enforcement stage.

notation.meaning: Index set of omitted model constraints

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle certificate for accepting or rejecting an incumbent against omitted constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an integer candidate \(\hat x\), the callback certificate is the oracle result \(V(\hat x)=\{j\in J:g_j(\hat x)>\varepsilon\}\). If \(V(\hat x)\ne\varnothing\), any returned violated constraint certifies that \(\hat x\notin F\), so the candidate must be rejected and the constraint submitted. If \(V(\hat x)=\varnothing\), completeness of the oracle certifies \(g_j(\hat x)\le\varepsilon\) for every \(j\in J\); hence \(\hat x\) satisfies the omitted family to tolerance and may pass this enforcement stage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A violated omitted constraint certifies incumbent infeasibility; a complete oracle returning none certifies satisfaction of the omitted family to tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Enforcement

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The oracle result can serve as a certificate under completeness, but the Incumbent Enforcement container may call for an enforcement algorithm rather than only a certificate. Source evidence is needed to settle the exact semantics and tolerance convention.

children.title: Relaxation Enforcement
children.top_down_role: Enforcement opportunities arising during relaxation processing.

assumptions_latex: The intended feasible set includes constraints \(g_j(x)\le0\) for \(j\in J\), and the current relaxation solution is \(\bar x\).
The solver permits model-enforcing submissions at the current relaxation callback.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The callback separates \(\bar x\) over the omitted constraint family and selects indices satisfying \(g_j(\bar x)>\varepsilon\). It submits the corresponding constraints \(g_j(x)\le0\), or globally valid relaxations of them, with correct validity metadata. The solver incorporates accepted contributions and resolves the node relaxation before using \(\bar x\) further. Repetition continues until no eligible violation exceeds \(\varepsilon\) or a callback budget is exhausted. Unlike incumbent-only enforcement, this procedure may act at fractional \(\bar x\), but only through contributions valid for every feasible point in their declared scope.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Enforcement of omitted constraints at eligible fractional relaxation solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The callback separates \(\bar x\) over the omitted constraint family and selects indices satisfying \(g_j(\bar x)>\varepsilon\). It submits the corresponding constraints \(g_j(x)\le0\), or globally valid relaxations of them, with correct validity metadata. The solver incorporates accepted contributions and resolves the node relaxation before using \(\bar x\) further. Repetition continues until no eligible violation exceeds \(\varepsilon\) or a callback budget is exhausted. Unlike incumbent-only enforcement, this procedure may act at fractional \(\bar x\), but only through contributions valid for every feasible point in their declared scope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxation enforcement separates fractional solutions and adds scope-valid model constraints or relaxations before the solver continues using those solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Enforcement

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Fractional enforcement and the permitted contribution types are API-dependent. No source supports the submission, incorporation, re-solve, or repetition contract.

children.title: Callback Eligibility Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Invocation contexts where model-enforcing contributions are permitted.

assumptions_latex: Let \(E\) be the set of solver events and \(C\subseteq E\) the events at which a callback action is documented as admissible.
At event \(e\), let \(I(e)\) denote the information exposed with guaranteed validity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A callback contribution is eligible only when \(e\in C\), every datum used to construct it belongs to \(I(e)\), and its declared validity scope contains the solver state where it will be installed. Incumbent rejection additionally requires an integer-candidate event, while fractional relaxation enforcement requires an event exposing a current relaxation point and permitting constraint or cut submission. At \(e\notin C\), or when required data are absent or stale, submission is undefined and must be refused. Eligibility therefore does not follow merely from the callback being invoked; it is action-specific and event-specific.

notation.meaning: Events eligible for a specified callback action
Guaranteed information available at event e

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract eligibility predicate; concrete event sets depend on the solver API.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A callback contribution is eligible only when \(e\in C\), every datum used to construct it belongs to \(I(e)\), and its declared validity scope contains the solver state where it will be installed. Incumbent rejection additionally requires an integer-candidate event, while fractional relaxation enforcement requires an event exposing a current relaxation point and permitting constraint or cut submission. At \(e\notin C\), or when required data are absent or stale, submission is undefined and must be refused. Eligibility therefore does not follow merely from the callback being invoked; it is action-specific and event-specific.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A callback action is eligible only at permitted events, using guaranteed current data, with a validity scope compatible with where its contribution is installed.
knowledge_statements.title: Callback Eligibility Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition fits the boundary container, but the admissible event set, guaranteed information, and permitted actions are defined by vendor-specific callback contracts, none of which is cited.

children.title: Callback Validity Responsibility System
children.top_down_role: Correctness boundaries for user-generated global, local, and model-enforcing information.

children.title: Global Callback Contributions
children.top_down_role: Responsibilities attached to globally reusable callback information.

assumptions_latex: The original mixed-integer feasible set is \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
A callback contribution has predicate \(q(x)\le0\) and is intended for unrestricted reuse in the search tree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The contribution is global precisely when \(q(x)\le0\) holds for every \(x\in F\), independently of the current node bounds, incumbent, relaxation solution, or branching history. A globally valid inequality or bound may therefore be installed at the root and inherited by every node without excluding a feasible solution. If its validity argument uses a node-local domain restriction \(D_N\), then the contribution is not global unless the same predicate is separately shown valid on all of \(F\). The callback producer owns the mathematical validity claim; the solver's acceptance does not establish it.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mathematical validity criterion for callback contributions reusable throughout the tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The contribution is global precisely when \(q(x)\le0\) holds for every \(x\in F\), independently of the current node bounds, incumbent, relaxation solution, or branching history. A globally valid inequality or bound may therefore be installed at the root and inherited by every node without excluding a feasible solution. If its validity argument uses a node-local domain restriction \(D_N\), then the contribution is not global unless the same predicate is separately shown valid on all of \(F\). The callback producer owns the mathematical validity claim; the solver's acceptance does not establish it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A callback contribution is global exactly when it holds for every original feasible point, independently of node-specific information or search history.
knowledge_statements.title: Global Callback Contributions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition is appropriate and the mathematical global-validity criterion is plausible, but root installation, universal inheritance, producer responsibility, and solver-acceptance semantics need an inspectable callback reference.

children.title: Local Callback Contributions
children.top_down_role: Responsibilities attached to node-limited callback information.

assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is the feasible set of the original mixed-integer model.
\(R_v\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is the branching domain at node \(v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^Tx\leq b\) may be imposed only at \(v\) and nodes \(w\) satisfying \(R_w\subseteq R_v\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a node-local callback inequality is valid only on the generating node domain and its subsets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines validity and permitted propagation of a node-local callback inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A callback contribution \(a^Tx\leq b\) generated at node \(v\) is local when \(a^Tx\leq b\) holds for every \(x\in F\cap R_v\), while validity for every \(x\in F\) is not established. The contribution may be enforced at \(v\) and at any descendant node \(w\) whose branching domain satisfies \(R_w\subseteq R_v\). It must not be activated at a node whose domain is not contained in \(R_v\), nor entered into a globally reusable cut pool.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local callback inequality is valid only within its generating node domain and may propagate solely to descendants whose domains are contained in that domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Callback Contributions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent and fits the local-contribution leaf, but the permitted propagation and global-pool prohibition are solver-interface claims requiring a specific callback reference.

children.title: Model-Enforcing Contributions
children.top_down_role: Responsibilities for dynamically supplied model constraints.

assumptions_latex: \(F=\{x\in X:g_j(x)\leq0\text{ for all }j\in J\}\) is the intended feasible set.
A subset of the defining constraints may be omitted initially and separated by callback.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted solution must belong to \(F\), so each violated omitted constraint must be enforced before acceptance.

notation.meaning: Intended feasible set of the complete model.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: model-enforcing callbacks restore deliberately omitted defining constraints before solution acceptance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes model-defining callback constraints from optional relaxation-strengthening cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A callback contribution is model-enforcing when it supplies an omitted constraint \(g_j(x)\leq0\) from the definition \(F=\{x\in X:g_j(x)\leq0\text{ for all }j\in J\}\). Unlike an optional strengthening cut, such a contribution is required for equivalence between the implemented model and \(F\). Whenever a candidate \(\bar x\in X\) satisfies \(g_j(\bar x)>0\) for some omitted index \(j\), the callback must reject \(\bar x\) and add a constraint sufficient to exclude it before the solver may accept it as feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model-enforcing contribution restores an omitted defining constraint; any candidate violating that constraint must be rejected before it can be accepted as feasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Model-Enforcing Contributions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distinction from optional strengthening cuts fits the leaf, but the rejection and enforcement obligations depend on callback semantics not supported by a cited source.

children.title: Validity Ownership
children.top_down_role: Allocation of correctness obligations between callers, callbacks, and solver infrastructure.

assumptions_latex: Each callback contribution is submitted with a declared validity domain \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
The solver can restrict activation to nodes whose feasible regions lie in \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Correctness requires both \(F_v\subseteq D\) at every activation node \(v\) and a justified proof that the contribution holds on \(F\cap D\).

notation.meaning: Feasible region represented at node v.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: correctness separates the contributor's validity obligation from the solver's activation-scope obligation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Assigns complementary validity obligations to the callback contributor and solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a submitted inequality \(h(x)\leq0\) with declared domain \(D\), the contributor owns the obligation to justify \(h(x)\leq0\) for every \(x\in F\cap D\) and to declare whether \(D\) is global, node-local, or model-enforcing. The solver owns the obligation to activate the contribution only at nodes \(v\) for which \(F_v\subseteq D\), and to preserve that restriction during copying, pooling, and transformation. Correctness fails if either the validity justification or the declared activation scope is absent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The contributor must justify and declare a contribution's domain; the solver must enforce it only where the current node region lies inside that domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Validity Ownership

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle is internally consistent, but its allocation of obligations between contributor and solver, including copying, pooling, and transformation behavior, requires authoritative interface documentation.

children.title: Scope Leakage Failures
children.top_down_role: Misuse of callback information beyond its certified applicability.

assumptions_latex: Node \(v\) has branching domain \(R_v=\{x:x_1=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Treating the locally valid inequality \(x_2\leq0\) as global removes the feasible point \((1,1)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the finite example directly demonstrates loss of a globally feasible point through scope leakage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure caused by promoting a node-local inequality to global scope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{(0,0),(1,1)\}\subseteq\{0,1\}^2\), and consider a node \(v\) with \(R_v=\{x:x_1=0\}\). Then \(F\cap R_v=\{(0,0)\}\), so \(x_2\leq0\) is valid at \(v\). It is not valid for the original model because \((1,1)\in F\) violates it. If a callback labels this inequality global, inserts it into a global pool, or activates it at a node not contained in \(R_v\), the algorithm can delete \((1,1)\) and return an incorrect optimum or infeasibility conclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a two-point feasible set, a cut valid under the branch fixing the first variable to zero deletes another feasible point if reused globally.
knowledge_statements.title: Scope Leakage Failures

children.title: Validity-Bound Correctness Invariant System
children.top_down_role: Scope-sensitive invariants preserving feasible integer solutions and sound node and global bounds.

children.title: Global Cut Validity
children.top_down_role: Validity over the original integer-feasible region and its consequences for global activation and reuse.

children.title: Original-Model Validity
children.top_down_role: Global scope relative to the unbranched model.

assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is the feasible set before branching and node-local domain restrictions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality is globally valid exactly when \(F\subseteq\{x:a^Tx\leq b\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global validity is measured against the complete unbranched feasible set.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An inequality \(a^Tx\leq b\) has original-model validity if and only if \(a^Tx\leq b\) for every \(x\in F\), equivalently \(F\subseteq\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:a^Tx\leq b\}\). The set \(F\) includes all original constraints and integrality requirements but excludes branching decisions, temporary bounds, and other node-local restrictions. Consequently, validity merely on \(F\cap R_v\) for one node domain \(R_v\) does not establish original-model validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut is globally valid precisely when every feasible solution of the complete unbranched mixed-integer model satisfies it.
knowledge_statements.title: Original-Model Validity

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

children.title: Transformation-Safe Cut Recovery
children.top_down_role: Global validity across preprocessing and representation changes.

children.title: Transformed-Space Cut Validity
children.top_down_role: Validity of global cuts in preprocessed or reformulated representations.

assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is the original feasible set.
\(T:F\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is the recorded transformation into solver space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A transformed cut is valid when \(a^TT(x)\leq b\) for every \(x\in F\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: transformed-space validity is validity on the exact image of the original feasible set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines transformed validity through the image of original feasible solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a recorded transformation \(T:F\to\mathbb{R}^m\), an inequality \(a^Ty\leq b\) has transformed-space validity relative to the original model exactly when \(a^TT(x)\leq b\) for every \(x\in F\). Equivalently, \(T(F)\subseteq\{y\in\mathbb{R}^m:a^Ty\leq b\}\). If validity was established only on the transformed image of a node-restricted set \(F\cap R_v\), the inequality is node-local unless an independent argument establishes validity on all of \(T(F)\).
