knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transformed cut is globally valid when it holds on the transformed image of every original-model feasible solution, not merely one node's image.
knowledge_statements.title: Transformed-Space Cut Validity

children.title: Original-Space Cut Recovery
children.top_down_role: Recovery of transformed cuts in the original model representation.

assumptions_latex: \(T(x)=Mx+q\) is an exact affine transformation on the original feasible set \(F\).
\(a^Ty\leq b\) is valid for every \(y\in T(F)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recovered inequality is \((M^Ta)^Tx\leq b-a^Tq\), and it is valid for every \(x\in F\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: affine substitution gives the displayed pullback identity directly
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Affine pullback of a globally valid transformed-space inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the solver transformation is affine, \(y=T(x)=Mx+q\), for every \(x\in F\). Pulling back the transformed inequality \(a^Ty\leq b\) yields \(a^T(Mx+q)\leq b\), equivalently \((M^Ta)^Tx\leq b-a^Tq\). If \(a^Ty\leq b\) holds for every \(y\in T(F)\), then the recovered inequality holds for every \(x\in F\). Recovery is global only when the transformation identity and transformed validity both hold on the full original feasible set rather than a node-restricted subset.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under an exact affine transformation, substitute the original variables into the transformed cut; the resulting coefficient and right-hand-side formula preserves global validity.
knowledge_statements.title: Original-Space Cut Recovery

children.title: Transformation Provenance
children.top_down_role: Traceability of representation changes relevant to cut validity.

assumptions_latex: The transformation is a finite chain \(T=T_k\circ\cdots\circ T_1\).
Each step has a recorded domain containing the image of every original feasible point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The provenance record certifies that backward substitution produces an inequality valid on \(F\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: an auditable transformation chain certifies that each backward substitution preserves the stated domain
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate data required for auditable cut recovery through composed transformations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A transformation-provenance certificate for \(T=T_k\circ\cdots\circ T_1\) records, for every step \(T_i\), its input and output variables, defining equality or implication, validity domain, and inverse or pullback rule. It is valid for global cut recovery when every \(x\in F\) lies in the first domain, each intermediate image lies in the next domain, and every recorded pullback preserves implication. Starting from an inequality valid on \(T(F)\), applying the pullback rules in reverse order then certifies an inequality satisfied by every \(x\in F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A provenance certificate records every transformation and pullback domain, allowing reverse substitution to certify that a recovered cut remains valid for all original feasible points.
knowledge_statements.title: Transformation Provenance

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Certificate is the appropriate content kind, but the proposed certificate fields and the requirement that each pullback preserve implication are specialized and insufficiently defined without a transformation or presolve reference.

children.title: Recovery Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Transformation cases where valid recovery is unavailable or ambiguous.

assumptions_latex: \(F=\{0,1\}\), \(T(x)=x\), and an incorrect transformed feasible set is \(\widetilde F=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality \(y\leq0\) is valid on \(\widetilde F\) but its pullback \(x\leq0\) is invalid on \(F\).

notation.meaning: Set used to justify transformed validity.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the finite counterexample proves that missing image containment invalidates recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery fails when the validity set does not contain the true transformed image.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Safe pullback requires \(T(F)\subseteq\widetilde F\), where \(\widetilde F\) is the set on which the transformed inequality was proved valid. Without this containment, recovery can fail even for the identity transformation. Let \(F=\{0,1\}\), \(T(x)=x\), and \(\widetilde F=\{0\}\). The inequality \(y\leq0\) is valid on \(\widetilde F\), but its pullback \(x\leq0\) excludes the feasible point \(x=1\). Thus approximate, node-local, or undocumented transformations cannot support global recovery unless the required containment is independently certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cut recovery is unsafe when the set used to prove transformed validity omits a true transformed feasible point, as a one-variable example demonstrates.
knowledge_statements.title: Recovery Failure Boundaries

children.title: Global Cut Reuse Eligibility System
children.top_down_role: Architectural consequences of certified global scope.

children.title: Global Cut Activation
children.top_down_role: Activation of cuts certified for global use.

assumptions_latex: A candidate cut \(a^Tx\leq b\) has a declared validity domain \(D\).
Node \(v\) represents feasible region \(F_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Activate the cut at \(v\) only if \(F_v\subseteq D\) and its representation matches the active transformation.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: activation is sound exactly when node scope and transformation representation satisfy the recorded certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity-gated activation of a stored cut at a search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a node \(v\), its region \(F_v\), a stored cut \(a^Tx\leq b\), its validity domain \(D\), and its transformation-provenance record. First verify \(F_v\subseteq D\). Next verify that the stored coefficients are expressed in, or can be exactly recovered into, the transformation active at \(v\). If both checks succeed, activate the corresponding inequality in the node relaxation; otherwise leave it inactive or route it to a compatible local representation. Stop after the activation decision and return the active inequality together with its validity and transformation identifiers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Activate a stored cut only when the current node lies within its certified domain and its coefficients are compatible with the node's active transformation.
knowledge_statements.title: Global Cut Activation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is plausible, but it is solver-specific and describes activation for an arbitrary domain D rather than clearly restricting the input to a globally valid cut. A source is needed to determine the intended activation contract.

children.title: Global Pool Admission
children.top_down_role: Eligibility criteria for entry into globally reusable cut pools.

assumptions_latex: \(F\) is the complete unbranched feasible set.
A candidate inequality and its transformation history are available for verification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Admission is permitted only after certifying \(F\subseteq\{x:a^Tx\leq b\}\) in a reusable representation.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: global pooling requires original-model validity and a representation recoverable across intended activation contexts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary validity and provenance conditions for global cut-pool admission.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An inequality \(a^Tx\leq b\) is eligible for admission to a global cut pool only if original-model validity \(F\subseteq\{x:a^Tx\leq b\}\) is certified, its derivation does not depend on undeclared node-local restrictions, and its transformation provenance permits exact interpretation or recovery wherever reuse is intended. Failure of any condition requires rejection from the global pool, although the inequality may remain eligible for a correctly scoped local pool. Numerical usefulness, efficacy, or sparsity may govern retention but cannot replace the validity and provenance conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut may enter the global pool only after global validity, absence of hidden local assumptions, and reusable transformation provenance have been certified.
knowledge_statements.title: Global Pool Admission

children.title: Cross-Node Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse of globally valid cuts across the search tree.

assumptions_latex: \(a^Tx\leq b\) is valid for every \(x\in F\).
Each node \(w\) represents a restriction \(F_w=F\cap R_w\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every node \(w\), \(F_w\subseteq\{x:a^Tx\leq b\}\); hence the cut is reusable across nodes.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-theoretic basis for reusing a globally valid cut at multiple nodes.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(a^Tx\leq b\) is valid for every \(x\in F\), then it remains valid at every branch-and-bound node \(w\) because \(F_w=F\cap R_w\subseteq F\). Therefore \(F_w\subseteq\{x:a^Tx\leq b\}\) for every node, independently of the branching domain \(R_w\). Cross-node reuse is sound provided the inequality's representation is compatible with the transformation active at each destination node. This property establishes validity of reuse, not that activating the cut is computationally beneficial.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every node feasible set is a subset of the original feasible set, so an original-model-valid cut remains valid across nodes when represented compatibly.
knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Node Reuse

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

children.title: Pool-Eligibility Failures
children.top_down_role: Conditions preventing safe global storage or reuse.

knowledge_statements.title: Pool-Eligibility Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of global-pool admission for cuts valid only on a restricted node domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the global feasible set be \(F\), let a node domain be \(D_v\), and let \(c(x)\le 0\) be valid for \(F\cap D_v\). Global-pool eligibility requires \(c(x)\le 0\) for every \(x\in F\), unless the pool preserves and enforces the domain tag \(D_v\). This requirement can fail: for \(F=\{0,1\}\), \(D_v=\{0\}\), and \(c(x)=x\), the inequality \(x\le 0\) is node-valid but excludes the globally feasible point \(x=1\). Untagged global reuse is therefore invalid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node-valid cut cannot enter an unscoped global pool if it excludes any globally feasible point; a domain tag is necessary for restricted reuse.
assumptions_latex: \(F\neq\varnothing\).
Pool activation does not automatically restore the originating node domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Node validity alone does not imply global-pool eligibility.

children.title: Local Cut Validity
children.top_down_role: Validity restricted by node domains, branching decisions, or locally available bounds.

children.title: Node-Domain Validity
children.top_down_role: Validity within a designated branch-and-bound subproblem.

knowledge_statements.title: Node-Domain Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity of an inequality relative to one branch-and-bound subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization mixed-integer problem with global feasible set \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), let node \(v\) impose domain restrictions represented by \(D_v\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and define \(F_v=F\cap D_v\). An inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) is node-domain valid at \(v\) exactly when \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) holds for every \(x\in F_v\). The definition permits the inequality to fail on \(F\setminus F_v\); consequently, validity at \(v\) does not by itself authorize activation outside domains contained in its validity domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut is valid at a node precisely when every feasible integer point satisfying that node’s domain restrictions satisfies the cut.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is the original mixed-integer feasible set.
\(D_v\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) represents all restrictions defining node \(v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) is node-domain valid if and only if \(F_v\subseteq\{x:a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\}\).

children.title: Bound-Dependent Local Cuts
children.top_down_role: Cut families whose scope depends on locally tightened variable domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Dependent Local Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eligibility condition for cuts derived using locally tightened variable bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose node \(v\) has local box \(B_v=\{x:\ell^v\le x\le u^v\}\), and a derivation establishes \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) for every original feasible point in \(B_v\). At another node \(w\), the cut is valid whenever its feasible domain satisfies \(F_w\subseteq B_v\). The componentwise condition \(\ell^v\le\ell^w\le u^w\le u^v\) is sufficient when \(F_w\subseteq B_w\). If any bound used by the derivation is relaxed and containment is not otherwise certified, applicability must be revalidated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bound-dependent cut may be reused only where current feasible domains remain inside the bounds used to derive it.
assumptions_latex: The cut derivation is valid for all original feasible points in \(B_v\).
Node bounds are interpreted componentwise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_w\subseteq B_v\) implies validity of \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) at node \(w\).

notation.meaning: Box defined by the bounds used in the cut derivation.
Feasible set of the receiving node.
Local lower and upper bounds at the origin node.

children.title: Subtree Inheritance
children.top_down_role: Propagation of local scope through descendant subproblems.

assumptions_latex: \(F_w\subseteq F_v\).
\(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) is valid on \(F_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) is valid on \(F_w\).

notation.meaning: Feasible sets at the origin and descendant nodes.
Certified validity domain of cut c.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inheritance of a local cut by descendants whose domains only tighten.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v\) be a branch-and-bound node and let \(w\) be a descendant. If branching and propagation only add restrictions, then \(F_w\subseteq F_v\). Hence every inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) that is valid for all \(x\in F_v\) is also valid for all \(x\in F_w\). More generally, a cut with certified validity domain \(V_c\) is certifiably inherited by every descendant \(w\) for which \(F_w\subseteq V_c\). This containment is sufficient but need not be necessary for actual validity on \(F_w\); ancestry alone does not certify inheritance if later operations relax a restriction used in the cut derivation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local cut is inherited by descendants whose feasible sets remain inside its certified validity domain; this containment is a sufficient certificate, not a necessary characterization of every domain on which the inequality might happen to be valid.
knowledge_statements.title: Subtree Inheritance

children.title: Local-Cut Scope Lifecycle
children.top_down_role: Loss of applicability outside a cut's certified node domain.

children.title: Scope Expiration Events
children.top_down_role: Search transitions that end a local cut's certified applicability.

knowledge_statements.title: Scope Expiration Events
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Events that invalidate a previously certified local-cut activation scope.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Associate each local cut \(c\) with a scope predicate \(S_c(w)\) whose truth certifies validity at the current node \(w\). A scope-expiration event occurs when a search transition changes the node domain or derivation context so that \(S_c(w)\) becomes false or cannot be certified. Such events include leaving the cut’s origin subtree, relaxing a bound used in its derivation, or restoring a node state outside its validity domain. After expiration, the cut must not constrain the node relaxation unless validity is independently re-established.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local cut’s scope expires whenever a search transition destroys or leaves uncertified the domain conditions supporting its validity.
assumptions_latex: Each local cut carries a machine-checkable scope predicate.
A false or uncertified predicate is treated as ineligible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(S_c(w)\) is false or uncertified, cut \(c\) is ineligible for activation at \(w\).

notation.meaning: Predicate certifying that cut c is valid at node w.

children.title: Cut Deactivation
children.top_down_role: Removal of expired local cuts from active relaxations.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Deactivation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe removal of local cuts whose certified activation scope no longer holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a node \(w\), relaxation \(R_w\), active-cut set \(A_w\), and scope predicate \(S_c\) for every local cut \(c\). Initialize \(A'_w=A_w\). For each \(c\in A_w\), evaluate \(S_c(w)\); if it is false or uncertified, remove \(c\) from \(A'_w\) and remove its inequality from \(R_w\). Stop after every active local cut has been checked. Output the relaxation formed from the node’s base constraints and precisely the cuts remaining in \(A'_w\); only that relaxation may be used to compute the node bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Before solving a node relaxation, remove every local cut whose scope predicate is false or cannot be certified.
assumptions_latex: Global cuts are handled separately and remain globally valid.
Removing a cut restores, rather than deletes, the node’s base constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output active set is \(A'_w=\{c\in A_w:S_c(w)\text{ is certified true}\}\).

notation.meaning: Active cuts before the scope check.

children.title: Descendant Applicability
children.top_down_role: Persistence of local-cut validity within certified descendant domains.

assumptions_latex: Cut \(c\) is valid for every original feasible point in \(V_c\).
The receiving node has feasible set \(F_w\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_w\subseteq V_c\) implies that \(c\) is valid and certifiably applicable at \(w\).

notation.meaning: Certified validity domain of the local cut.
Feasible set at descendant node w.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Containment certificate for activating a local cut at a descendant node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a local cut \(c\) be certified on a validity domain \(V_c\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), meaning every original feasible point in \(V_c\) satisfies \(c\). At a descendant node \(w\), the containment \(F_w\subseteq V_c\) certifies that the cut is valid and applicable. If \(V_c\) is the origin-node domain and descendant construction only adds restrictions, the ancestor relation certifies this containment. If presolve, bound restoration, or domain modification can enlarge \(F_w\), descendant status must be supplemented by an explicit containment certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A descendant may activate a local cut when its feasible set is certified to lie within the cut's validity domain; this is a sufficient applicability certificate rather than a necessary characterization of all sets on which the inequality may be valid.
knowledge_statements.title: Descendant Applicability

children.title: Stale Local-Cut Failures
children.top_down_role: Correctness risks from retaining cuts after their scope expires.

knowledge_statements.title: Stale Local-Cut Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete loss of correctness when an expired local cut remains active.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the minimization problem with feasible set \(F=\{0,1\}\) and objective \(f(x)=-x\). In the branch node \(v\) imposing \(x=0\), the local inequality \(x\le 0\) is valid. After moving to the sibling node \(w\) imposing \(x=1\), retaining that inequality makes the relaxation infeasible, although \(F_w=\{1\}\) is feasible and contains the global optimizer with value \(-1\). Thus a stale local cut can cause erroneous infeasibility, an invalid node bound, and incorrect pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Keeping a node-specific cut active at an incompatible sibling can falsely make a feasible, even optimal, node appear infeasible.
assumptions_latex: Branching creates sibling domains \(x=0\) and \(x=1\).
The cut \(x\le 0\) is not deactivated when entering the second sibling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Activation of the stale cut at \(w\) violates relaxation containment and may delete the global optimizer.

notation.meaning: Feasible set of the sibling node.

children.title: Integrated Search Bound Correctness
children.top_down_role: Correctness of node bounds, pruning decisions, and global bounds under valid relaxation strengthening.

children.title: Relaxation Containment Invariant
children.top_down_role: Preservation of relevant feasible integer points in strengthened node relaxations.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation Containment Invariant
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Containment invariant for every strengthened node relaxation in a minimization search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every live node \(v\), let \(F_v\) be its mixed-integer feasible set and let \(R_v\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the relaxation used for bounding. The relaxation-containment invariant is \(F_v\subseteq R_v\). It holds initially when the base relaxation contains all points of \(F_v\), and it remains true after adding inequalities only if every added inequality is valid on \(F_v\). Bound tightening, presolve transformations, and cut activation must each preserve this inclusion; otherwise infeasibility and objective bounds obtained from \(R_v\) need not be valid for the node.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every strengthened node relaxation must retain all feasible mixed-integer points belonging to that node.
assumptions_latex: \(F_v\) is the node’s exact feasible set.
\(R_v\) is the set actually used to compute the node bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Correct node bounding requires \(F_v\subseteq R_v\) at every bounding operation.

notation.meaning: Mixed-integer feasible set at node v.

children.title: Node Dual-Bound Correctness
children.top_down_role: Sound interpretation of strengthened relaxation values within node domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Node Dual-Bound Correctness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower-bound correctness for a minimization node solved over a valid strengthened relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let node \(v\) have feasible set \(F_v\), relaxation \(R_v\), and objective \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), with \(F_v\subseteq R_v\). Define the relaxation value in the extended reals by \(L_v=\inf\{f(x):x\in R_v\}\) and the node optimum by \(z_v=\inf\{f(x):x\in F_v\}\), using \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\). Then \(L_v\le z_v\). Moreover, if \(R_v=\varnothing\), containment implies \(F_v=\varnothing\), so relaxation infeasibility is a valid certificate of node infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing over a containing relaxation gives a valid node lower bound; an empty containing relaxation certifies node infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(F_v\subseteq R_v\).
The problem is a minimization problem with the same objective on both sets.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_v\le z_v\), and \(R_v=\varnothing\) implies \(F_v=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Relaxation-based lower bound at node v.
Node feasible set and its relaxation.

children.title: Global Bound Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Sound composition of open-node information into a global dual bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Bound Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregation of valid open-node lower bounds for a minimization search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(O\) be a nonempty set of open branch-and-bound nodes whose feasible sets cover every feasible point not already fathomed, and let \(L_v\) be a valid lower bound for node \(v\), so \(L_v\le\inf\{f(x):x\in F_v\}\). Then the aggregate value \(L=\min_{v\in O}L_v\) is a valid lower bound on the best objective value among all remaining feasible points. If \(O\) is finite, this minimum is attained; for an infinite open set, replace the minimum by \(\inf_{v\in O}L_v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For minimization, the smallest valid lower bound among open nodes is a valid global lower bound on all remaining solutions.
assumptions_latex: The open-node feasible sets cover all unfathomed feasible points.
Every \(L_v\) is a valid lower bound for its node.
\(O\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L=\min_{v\in O}L_v\le\inf\{f(x):x\in\bigcup_{v\in O}F_v\}\) for finite \(O\).

notation.meaning: Valid lower bound for node v.

children.title: Bound-Based Pruning Correctness
children.top_down_role: Correct closure of subproblems using certified bounds and incumbent information.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Based Pruning Correctness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact certificate for pruning a minimization node using an incumbent and valid node bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=f(\bar x)\) be the objective value of a globally feasible incumbent \(\bar x\), and let \(L_v\) be a certified lower bound satisfying \(L_v\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in F_v\). If \(L_v\ge U\), then every feasible solution in node \(v\) has objective at least the incumbent value, so the node cannot contain a strictly improving solution and may be pruned. The verifiable certificate consists of incumbent feasibility, the validity record for \(L_v\), and the scalar comparison \(L_v\ge U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimization node may be pruned when its certified lower bound is no smaller than the value of a feasible incumbent.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar x\) is globally feasible and \(U=f(\bar x)\).
\(L_v\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in F_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_v\ge U\) implies that no \(x\in F_v\) satisfies \(f(x)<U\).

notation.meaning: Objective value of the feasible incumbent.
Certified lower bound for node v.

children.title: Integrated Search Termination Regimes
children.top_down_role: Finite-completion regimes and the boundaries introduced by incomplete separation and numerical computation.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Conforti, Cornuéjols, and Zambelli, Sections 5.2.5, 5.4.2, and 9.2

children.title: Finite-Tree Termination Regimes
children.top_down_role: Completion based on finite subdivision and sound node closure.

assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq X\) and \(f:F\to\mathbb R\) define a minimization problem.
Each branching step replaces a node region by finitely many child regions covering all feasible points in the parent region.

The complete generated tree is finite, every lower bound is valid, every closure decision preserves the incumbent or proves that the node cannot improve it, and every generated node is eventually processed or closed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{The search terminates after finitely many node operations and returns a global minimizer, or correctly concludes that }F=\varnothing.\)
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite exhaustive branch-and-bound with valid bounds and sound closure has the stated conditional correctness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-tree termination for minimization branch-and-bound under exhaustive branching and sound node closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a search space, let \(F\subseteq X\) be the exact feasible set, and let \(f:F\to\mathbb R\) be minimized. Suppose branching replaces each processed node region by finitely many child regions whose union contains every feasible point in the parent region. Suppose the complete generated tree is finite, every node lower bound is valid, every incumbent is feasible, every node closure decision is sound, and every generated node is eventually processed or closed. Then only finitely many node operations occur. When no active node remains, the incumbent, if one exists, is globally optimal; if no incumbent exists, then \(F=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exhaustive finite branching tree terminates and returns a global optimum, or correctly reports infeasibility, when bounds, incumbents, and all node closures are sound.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Tree Termination Regimes

children.title: Cut-Enhanced Termination Regimes
children.top_down_role: Termination analyses incorporating finite cutting-plane subsystems.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Enhanced Termination Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination when valid cutting is embedded within a finite branching search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the finite-tree regime above, augmented at each node by cutting-plane rounds. Suppose every added inequality is valid for the node's exact integer-feasible set, each node performs only finitely many cut rounds and generates finitely many cuts per round, and node closure uses bounds from the resulting valid relaxations. Then cutting does not remove any feasible integer solution or invalidate any lower bound. Consequently the integrated search still terminates finitely and has the same exact optimality or infeasibility conclusion as the underlying finite branching tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finitely many valid cuts per node preserve finite-tree termination and exact branch-and-bound correctness.
assumptions_latex: \(\text{The underlying branching tree is finite.}\)
\(\text{Every cut is valid for the corresponding node integer-feasible set.}\)
\(\text{Cut generation at every node terminates after finitely many operations.}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{The cut-enhanced search terminates finitely without changing the exact optimum or feasibility status.}\)

notation.meaning: Exact integer-feasible set at node v

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

review_flags: finite-tree integration assumptions require locator-level confirmation

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem is mathematically plausible and fits the leaf, but the cited primal cutting-plane section has not been shown to support finite per-node cutting, preservation of valid branch-and-bound bounds, and finite-tree termination together. Locator-level full-text confirmation or a dedicated branch-and-cut termination source is required.

children.title: Heuristic-Separation Termination Boundary
children.top_down_role: Completion limitations when separation is incomplete.

assumptions_latex: \(P=\{x\in[0,1]^2:x_1+x_2\le 3/2\}\subseteq\mathbb R^2\).
\(X=P\cap\mathbb Z^2\), and the separator is permitted to miss violated inequalities valid for \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{A no-cut-found response from an incomplete separator does not certify membership in }\operatorname{conv}(X)\text{ or justify node closure.}\)
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the explicit two-variable counterexample directly establishes the failure boundary
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of no-cut-found to certify closure under incomplete separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{x\in[0,1]^2:x_1+x_2\le 3/2\}\subseteq\mathbb R^2\) and \(X=P\cap\mathbb Z^2\). Every point of \(X\) satisfies \(x_1+x_2\le1\), so this inequality is valid for \(\operatorname{conv}(X)\). The point \(\bar x=(3/4,3/4)\in P\) violates that inequality. An incomplete separator may nevertheless return no cut at \(\bar x\). Hence no-cut-found does not certify membership in \(\operatorname{conv}(X)\), exhaustion of valid cuts, or sound node closure. A separate complete mechanism is required for a guarantee of sound completion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fractional point can violate an integer-hull inequality even when an incomplete separator reports no cut, so that report alone is not a closure certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Heuristic-Separation Termination Boundary

children.title: Numerical Termination Boundary
children.top_down_role: Termination and correctness limitations caused by tolerance-dependent computation.

assumptions_latex: \(\hat x\in F\), \(U=f(\hat x)\), and \(L\le f^\star\le U\) are mathematically certified.
\(\varepsilon>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U-L\le\varepsilon\Rightarrow f(\hat x)-f^\star\le\varepsilon\); exact optimality additionally requires \(\varepsilon=0\) or a certified objective-gap argument, and the implication itself requires certified bounds.

notation.meaning: Certified lower and incumbent upper bounds

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the approximate-gap implication follows directly from certified lower and upper bounds
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of exact correctness under positive gap tolerances and uncertified numerical bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the exact feasible set of a minimization problem, let \(f^\star=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\), and let \(\hat x\in F\) be a certified incumbent with \(U=f(\hat x)\). If \(L\le f^\star\le U\) is certified and \(U-L\le\varepsilon\) for \(\varepsilon>0\), then \(f(\hat x)-f^\star\le\varepsilon\). This does not establish exact optimality unless \(\varepsilon=0\) or a separate certified objective-gap argument excludes every better value. Certified numerical error control can establish the bound premises, but it does not by itself turn a positive-gap conclusion into exact optimality. If feasibility or either bound is accepted only through unchecked floating-point tolerances, even the approximate implication is unavailable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified positive gap gives approximate optimality; exact optimality also needs a zero gap or a certified discrete-gap argument, and uncertified numerical bounds give neither guarantee.
knowledge_statements.title: Numerical Termination Boundary

children.title: Floating-Point Validity Regime
children.top_down_role: Validity management under finite-precision arithmetic.

assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is the exact feasible set.
The verification arithmetic or enclosure procedure is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{x\in F}(\hat a^{\mathsf T}x-\hat b)\le0\) must be certified before \(\hat a^{\mathsf T}x\le\hat b\) is used as an exact valid cut.

notation.meaning: Exact optimum of the node relaxation

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact cut validity is universal satisfaction over the exact feasible set
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certified validity conditions for floating-point cuts and lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the exact feasible set, and let a floating-point procedure propose \(\hat a^{\mathsf T}x\le\hat b\) with \(\hat a\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\hat b\in\mathbb R\). The proposal may be used as an exact valid cut only after a sound exact-arithmetic or outward-rounded verification certifies \(\sup_{x\in F}(\hat a^{\mathsf T}x-\hat b)\le0\). Similarly, if \(z_R^\star\) is the exact optimum of a minimization relaxation, a reported lower bound \(L\) is admissible only after sound error control certifies \(L\le z_R^\star\). Sampled residuals and unchecked solver status do not establish either universal inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A floating-point cut or lower bound is mathematically admissible only after sound verification establishes the corresponding exact inequality.
knowledge_statements.title: Floating-Point Validity Regime

children.title: Feasibility Tolerance Semantics
children.top_down_role: Interpretation of feasibility margins used by solver components.

assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a finite row-index set, \(a_i\in\mathbb R^n\), \(b_i\in\mathbb R\), and \(x\in\mathbb R^n\).
\(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and \(\tau_{\rm abs},\tau_{\rm rel},\tau_{\rm int}\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\) is tolerance-feasible exactly when every row satisfies \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x-b_i\le t_i(x)\) and every \(j\in I\) satisfies \(|x_j-\operatorname{round}(x_j)|\le\tau_{\rm int}\).

notation.meaning: Finite index set of linear inequality rows

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the record explicitly stipulates a local scaled-residual convention
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A declared scaled-residual convention for linear feasibility and integrality tolerances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be a finite row-index set, let \(a_i\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(b_i\in\mathbb R\) for every \(i\in M\), and let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\). For declared tolerances \(\tau_{\rm abs},\tau_{\rm rel}\ge0\), define \(t_i(x)=\tau_{\rm abs}+\tau_{\rm rel}\max\{|b_i|,|a_i|^{\mathsf T}|x|\}\). The point \(x\) is numerically feasible for the linear system when \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x-b_i\le t_i(x)\) for every \(i\in M\). Given \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and \(\tau_{\rm int}\ge0\), it is numerically integral when \(|x_j-\operatorname{round}(x_j)|\le\tau_{\rm int}\) for every \(j\in I\). These are stipulated tolerance predicates and do not imply exact feasibility or integrality when a positive tolerance is active.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the declared convention, numerical feasibility uses scaled row residuals and numerical integrality uses distance to a nearest integer; these predicates are distinct from exact feasibility and integrality.
knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Tolerance Semantics

children.title: Violation Classification
children.top_down_role: Tolerance-sensitive classification of candidate cut violations.

assumptions_latex: \(a,x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(b\in\mathbb R\), and \(t(x)\ge0\).
The residual is evaluated exactly or enclosed sufficiently to certify the applicable class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r(x)\le0\), \(0<r(x)\le t(x)\), and \(r(x)>t(x)\) form three disjoint and exhaustive residual classes.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the three intervals explicitly define an exhaustive local classification
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local three-way classification of exact satisfaction, tolerance ambiguity, and numerical violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a,x\in\mathbb R^n\), let \(b\in\mathbb R\), and consider the row \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\). Define its exact residual by \(r(x)=a^{\mathsf T}x-b\), and let \(t(x)\ge0\) be its declared feasibility tolerance. Classify the row at \(x\) as exactly satisfied when \(r(x)\le0\), tolerance-ambiguous when \(0<r(x)\le t(x)\), and numerically violated when \(r(x)>t(x)\). Under the stipulated binary convention, the first two classes are reported feasible and the third is reported violated. A tolerance-ambiguous row violates the exact inequality despite being accepted numerically.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exact residual lies in exactly one of three locally defined classes: exact satisfaction, tolerance ambiguity, or numerical violation.
knowledge_statements.title: Violation Classification

children.title: Tolerance-Induced Validity Failures
children.top_down_role: Loss of correctness caused by inconsistent or unsafe tolerance use.

assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb R\), \(\tau>0\), and \(0<\delta\le\tau\).
Each row is numerically accepted when its positive violation is at most \(\tau\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x\in\mathbb R:x\ge\delta,\ x\le0\}=\varnothing\), but \(x=0\) is accepted by the row-tolerance test.

notation.meaning: Positive inconsistency no larger than the tolerance

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the explicit one-dimensional system directly verifies the failure
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A positive row tolerance can make an exactly infeasible system numerically acceptable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb R\). For any \(\tau>0\), choose \(\delta\) with \(0<\delta\le\tau\) and consider \(x\ge\delta\) together with \(x\le0\). The system is exactly infeasible. Under a row test that accepts any violation no larger than \(\tau\), the point \(x=0\) is nevertheless accepted: it satisfies \(x\le0\) exactly and violates \(x\ge\delta\) by \(\delta\le\tau\). Thus tolerance feasibility can accept a point even when the exact system has no feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every positive row tolerance, an exactly infeasible one-variable system has a point accepted by the tolerance tests.
knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance-Induced Validity Failures

children.title: Safe-Cut Generation
children.top_down_role: Generation and postprocessing designed to preserve correctness despite inexact computation.

assumptions_latex: \(F_v\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is the exact node-feasible set and \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\).
Every accepted validity or separation test is sound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{Every returned inequality }a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\text{ is valid for all }x\in F_v\text{ and satisfies }a^{\mathsf T}\bar x>b.\)

notation.meaning: Exact feasible set at node v

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: universal exact validation and exact positive violation imply the stated output invariant
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generate inexactly, convert to an exact candidate, certify validity and violation, and retain only safe cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an exact node-feasible set \(F_v\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), a relaxation point \(\bar x\in\mathbb R^n\), and a possibly inexact separator. Generate a candidate inequality and convert it to a single exact candidate \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\), with \(a\in\mathbb Q^n\) and \(b\in\mathbb Q\), by a declared rational reconstruction or directed-rounding rule. Use a sound certificate to verify \(a^{\mathsf T}x\le b\) for every \(x\in F_v\), and evaluate \(a^{\mathsf T}\bar x-b\) exactly. Return the cut only if universal validity is certified and \(a^{\mathsf T}\bar x-b>0\); otherwise discard it or generate another candidate according to a declared finite policy. Output either a certified cut or no safe cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A safe-cut routine converts a proposed cut to exact coefficients and returns it only after certifying universal validity and exact positive violation.
knowledge_statements.title: Safe-Cut Generation

children.title: Exact-Rational Integrated Search

children.title: Exact Rational Cutting
children.top_down_role: Cut generation and representation using exact rational arithmetic.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Rational Cutting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cutting-plane iteration with rational coefficients and exact validity checks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a rational node relaxation \(P_0\), an exact objective, and a separation routine producing rational candidate inequalities with checkable validity certificates. At iteration \(k\), solve the current relaxation \(P_k\) exactly to obtain \(x^k\). If \(x^k\) satisfies the required integer conditions, return it. Otherwise request a candidate \(a^Tx\le b\), verify its certificate exactly, and test \(a^Tx^k>b\) in rational arithmetic. If both tests succeed, set \(P_{k+1}=P_k\cap\{x:a^Tx\le b\}\); otherwise reject the candidate. Stop according to a declared finite cut policy and return the strengthened relaxation if no solution is produced.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact rational cutting solves, separates, validates, and adds cuts using rational arithmetic under an explicit stopping policy.
assumptions_latex: \(P_0\text{ and the objective have rational data.}\)
\(\text{Each accepted cut has an exactly checkable validity certificate.}\)
\(\text{A finite stopping policy is specified.}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_k\cap F=P_0\cap F\) for every iteration \(k\), where \(F\) is the exact integer-feasible set.

notation.meaning: Rational relaxation after k accepted cuts
Exact relaxation optimizer at iteration k

children.title: Exact Rational Bounding
children.top_down_role: Node and global bound management using exact rational arithmetic.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb Q^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb Q^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb Q^n\).
\(y\in\mathbb Q^m\), \(y\ge0\), and \(A^{\mathsf T}y\le c\) are verified exactly.
The node-feasible set is contained in the linear relaxation, and \(U\) is a certified incumbent value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(b^{\mathsf T}y\le L\); therefore \(b^{\mathsf T}y\ge U\) certifies valid node closure.

notation.meaning: Exact optimum of the rational linear relaxation

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact rational weak duality directly establishes the certificate
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A rational dual-feasibility certificate for an exact node lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb Q^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb Q^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb Q^n\), and define \(L=\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\ge b,\ x\ge0\}\). A vector \(y\in\mathbb Q^m\) is an exact lower-bound certificate when \(y\ge0\) and \(A^{\mathsf T}y\le c\), with both inequalities checked in rational arithmetic. For every feasible \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \(b^{\mathsf T}y\le c^{\mathsf T}x\), and hence \(b^{\mathsf T}y\le L\). If the exact feasible set of a minimization node is contained in this relaxation, then \(b^{\mathsf T}y\) is also a node lower bound. Given a certified incumbent value \(U\), the exact comparison \(b^{\mathsf T}y\ge U\) certifies valid node closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exactly dual-feasible rational vector certifies a lower bound and permits pruning when that bound reaches the certified incumbent value.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Rational Bounding

children.title: Exact Rational Validation
children.top_down_role: Exact checking of cuts, bounds, and pruning evidence.

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb Q^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb Q^m\), \(c,\hat x\in\mathbb Q^n\), and \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
\(L\in\mathbb Q\) is a certified lower bound for the node under consideration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\hat x\ge b\) and \(\hat x_j\in\mathbb Z\) for all \(j\in I\) certify the incumbent; separately, \(L\ge U=c^{\mathsf T}\hat x\) certifies bound closure of the node.

notation.meaning: Certified node lower bound and exact incumbent value

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: each certificate predicate is exactly decidable for rational data
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separate exact certificates for incumbent feasibility and bound-based node closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb Q^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb Q^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb Q^n\) define rational mixed-integer data, and let \(I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) be the integer index set. A candidate \(\hat x\in\mathbb Q^n\) is exactly validated as an incumbent by checking \(A\hat x\ge b\) and \(\hat x_j\in\mathbb Z\) for every \(j\in I\) in exact arithmetic; its certified value is \(U=c^{\mathsf T}\hat x\). Separately, if \(L\in\mathbb Q\) is a certified lower bound for a node, then the exact comparison \(L\ge U\) certifies bound closure of that node. Floating-point status flags and rounded comparisons do not constitute these exact certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact validation separately certifies incumbent feasibility and value, then certifies node closure by comparing an exact lower bound with that value.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Rational Validation

children.title: Arithmetic Cost Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Computational and representation costs of exact arithmetic.

knowledge_statements.title: Arithmetic Cost Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bit-complexity boundary for exact-rational node processing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let every input coefficient be rational with numerator and denominator bit length at most \(L_0\). If an exact-rational search performs \(N\) arithmetic operations and all intermediate rational operands have bit length at most \(L\), then its bit cost is \(O(NM(L))\) up to logarithmic normalization factors, where \(M(L)\) bounds multiplication of \(L\)-bit integers. Thus a unit-cost arithmetic count is a valid polynomial-time surrogate only when intermediate bit lengths remain polynomially bounded in the encoded input size; without such a bound, coefficient growth can dominate the search cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact-rational operation counts represent computational cost only when intermediate numerator and denominator lengths remain controlled; otherwise coefficient growth can dominate search.
assumptions_latex: \(L_0,L,N\in\mathbb{N}\).
Every intermediate rational is stored as a normalized numerator-denominator pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T_{\mathrm{bit}}=O(NM(L))\) up to logarithmic normalization factors.

notation.meaning: Bit cost of multiplying two L-bit integers.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation supports the claimed rational-arithmetic cost. The bound also requires a precise cost model for addition, gcd reduction, division, and normalization before the stated O(NM(L)) estimate can be assessed.

children.title: Integrated Search Certificate System

children.title: Integrated Search Proof Certificate
children.top_down_role: Composite certificate architecture linking search-tree subdivision, cut derivations, bounds, primal solutions, and pruning.

children.title: Branching Disjunction Records
children.top_down_role: Certificate records representing subdivision of node domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Branching Disjunction Records
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Locally checkable record that child domains cover a parent domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a search node \(v\) with integer-feasible domain \(F_v\), a branching-disjunction record consists of child predicates \(D_{v1},\ldots,D_{vk}\) and the claim \(F_v\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^k D_{vi}\). It is valid when the stated variable domains imply this inclusion and each child domain is exactly \(F_{vi}=F_v\cap D_{vi}\). For integer branching on \(x_j\) at integer \(t\), the canonical record is \(D_{v1}=\{x:x_j\le t\}\) and \(D_{v2}=\{x:x_j\ge t+1\}\). Verification checks integrality of \(x_j\), the disjunction, and the recorded child-domain updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A branching record certifies that explicitly defined child domains cover every integer-feasible point of their parent node.
assumptions_latex: \(F_v\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) includes the node-local constraints.
The variables cited by an integer branching rule are integral on \(F_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F_v=\bigcup_{i=1}^k F_{vi}\).

notation.meaning: Predicate defining child i of node v.

children.title: Cut Derivation Records
children.top_down_role: Checkable provenance for introduced inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Derivation Records
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checkable provenance establishing validity of every introduced inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(v\), a cut-derivation record for \(a^Tx\ge\beta\) specifies its parent inequalities, numerical multipliers, and every side condition of the declared valid inference rule. The record is accepted only if exact recomputation produces \(a\) and \(\beta\) and the rule establishes \(a^Tx\ge\beta\) for every \(x\in F_v\). A globally tagged cut must instead be valid for the root feasible set \(F\); a locally tagged cut may be inherited only by descendants whose domains imply all recorded local assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut record exposes an exact, rule-by-rule derivation and identifies whether its validity is global or restricted to a node domain.
assumptions_latex: \(F_v\subseteq F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
Every invoked inference rule and its side conditions are identified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a^Tx\ge\beta\) holds on its recorded validity domain.

children.title: Node Bound Records
children.top_down_role: Evidence supporting bounds assigned to subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Node Bound Records
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verifiable lower-bound evidence for a minimization subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization node \(v\), a node-bound record consists of a relaxation \(R_v\supseteq F_v\), a scalar \(L_v\), and a checkable relaxation certificate proving \(c^Tx\ge L_v\) for every \(x\in R_v\). Its validity implies \(z_v^*:=\inf\{c^Tx:x\in F_v\}\ge L_v\). The record must identify all node-local constraints and cuts used in \(R_v\); any referenced local inequality must be valid under the ancestry assumptions of \(v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node-bound record certifies a lower bound by exhibiting a valid relaxation and checkable evidence for its relaxation objective bound.
assumptions_latex: \(F_v\subseteq R_v\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\).
The node subproblem minimizes \(c^Tx\).

notation.meaning: Certified lower bound at node v.
Infimum over the node's integer-feasible set.

children.title: Incumbent Feasibility Records
children.top_down_role: Evidence supporting primal solutions used in objective comparisons.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Feasibility Records
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal evidence validating an incumbent and its objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the minimization problem \(\inf\{c^Tx:x\in F\}\), an incumbent-feasibility record contains an explicitly encoded point \(\bar x\), the asserted value \(U=c^T\bar x\), and evaluations of every original constraint and integrality requirement. The record is valid exactly when these checks establish \(\bar x\in F\) and exact objective evaluation yields \(U\). It then certifies the primal upper bound \(z^*\le U\); node-local cuts are neither necessary nor sufficient substitutes for checking the original feasible-set conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An incumbent record verifies the proposed solution against every original constraint and certifies its objective as a global primal upper bound.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is the original mixed-integer feasible set.
The problem minimizes \(c^Tx\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\in F\) and \(z^*\le U=c^T\bar x\).

children.title: Leaf Pruning Records
children.top_down_role: Checkable reasons for closing terminal search subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Leaf Pruning Records
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Checkable justification for closing a terminal node in minimization search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an incumbent upper bound \(U\), a leaf-pruning record for node \(v\) references checkable evidence for one of the following claims: \(F_v=\varnothing\); a certified lower bound \(L_v\ge U\); or an exact solution of the node subproblem with value at least \(U\). The record includes or references the relevant infeasibility, bound, or exact-solution certificate and all node-local assumptions. A valid record certifies \(\inf\{c^Tx:x\in F_v\}\ge U\), using the convention \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A leaf-pruning record closes a node using certified infeasibility, an incumbent-dominating lower bound, or an exact node optimum that cannot improve the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: The global problem is a minimization problem.
\(U\) is supported by a valid incumbent-feasibility record.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf\{c^Tx:x\in F_v\}\ge U\), with \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\).

children.title: Infeasibility Certificates
children.top_down_role: Evidence supporting the absence of feasible integer solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite integrated-search evidence that the root integer-feasible set is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An integrated-search infeasibility certificate is a finite rooted tree whose root domain is \(F\), whose internal branching records certify that their child domains cover their parent domains, and whose cuts are valid on their recorded domains. Every leaf \(\ell\) carries a checkable certificate that a relaxation containing \(F_\ell\) is empty. Validity of every record certifies \(F=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite verified search tree certifies root infeasibility when its branches cover every case and every leaf has a valid relaxation-emptiness certificate.
assumptions_latex: The certificate tree is finite.
Every local cut and branching disjunction verifies on its stated domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: Feasible set associated with leaf ell.

children.title: Optimality Certificates
children.top_down_role: Combined primal and dual evidence supporting an optimal solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimality Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Combined primal incumbent and exhaustive search-tree evidence for minimization optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(z^*=\inf\{c^Tx:x\in F\}\), an optimality certificate consists of a feasible incumbent \(\bar x\in F\) with \(U=c^T\bar x\) and a finite verified search tree covering \(F\). Every leaf is certified infeasible or has a certified lower bound at least \(U\). A valid certificate establishes \(z^*=U\) and global optimality of \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An optimality certificate combines a feasible incumbent with an exhaustive verified tree certifying that every leaf is infeasible or has lower bound at least the incumbent value.
assumptions_latex: The global problem minimizes \(c^Tx\).
All branching, cut, leaf, and incumbent records verify exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z^*=c^T\bar x=U\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Optimality from Closure of the Upper–Lower Bound Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A feasible incumbent together with coincident valid upper and lower bounds certifies exact optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\{\bar f_k\}\) and \(\{\underline f_k\}\) be sequences of upper and lower bounds, respectively, on the optimal value \(f^*\). If, for some \(k\), \(\bar f_k-\underline f_k=0\), and \(x^k\) is feasible for \((P)\) with \(f(x^k)=\bar f_k\), then \(x^k\) is an optimal solution of \((P)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If valid upper and lower bounds on the optimal value coincide and a feasible solution attains the upper bound, then that solution is optimal.
assumptions_latex: \bar f_k\text{ and }\underline f_k\text{ are valid upper and lower bounds on }f^*,\text{ respectively}
\exists k:\ \bar f_k-\underline f_k=0
x^k\text{ is feasible for }(P)
f(x^k)=\bar f_k
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^k\text{ is an optimal solution of }(P)

children.title: Objective-Bound Certificates

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Bound Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global lower-bound evidence without requiring a matching primal solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the minimization problem \(z^*=\inf\{c^Tx:x\in F\}\), an objective-bound certificate for \(L\) is a finite verified search tree covering \(F\) such that every leaf \(\ell\) is certified infeasible or has a certified node lower bound \(L_\ell\ge L\). A valid certificate establishes \(z^*\ge L\) without requiring a feasible incumbent attaining \(L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global lower-bound certificate is an exhaustive verified tree in which every leaf is infeasible or has a certified lower bound at least the claimed value.
assumptions_latex: The global problem minimizes \(c^Tx\).
The finite certificate tree covers the root feasible set.

notation.meaning: Certified lower bound for leaf ell.

children.title: Dual-Bound Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificate families supporting node and global dual bounds in cut-strengthened relaxations.

children.title: LP Dual-Solution Certificates
children.top_down_role: Dual evidence associated with solved node relaxations.

knowledge_statements.title: LP Dual-Solution Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-feasible multiplier certificate for a node LP lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_v\in\mathbb{Q}^{m\times n}\), \(b_v\in\mathbb{Q}^m\), and \(c\in\mathbb{Q}^n\), and consider \(p_v=\inf\{c^Tx:A_vx\ge b_v,\ x\ge0\}\). A vector \(y\in\mathbb{Q}^m\) is an LP dual-solution certificate when exact checks establish \(y\ge0\) and \(A_v^Ty\le c\). It certifies \(L_v=b_v^Ty\) as a lower bound on the node LP and on every integer-feasible subset of its feasible region. Equality with the objective value of a recorded primal-feasible point additionally certifies LP optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exactly verified dual-feasible multiplier certifies its dual objective as a lower bound for the node LP and every integer-feasible subset of that relaxation.

The node LP has the displayed minimization form.

children.title: Farkas Infeasibility Certificates

knowledge_statements.title: Farkas Infeasibility Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas multiplier proving that a linear node relaxation is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_v\in\mathbb{Q}^{m\times n}\) and \(b_v\in\mathbb{Q}^m\). For the node system \(A_vx\ge b_v\), \(x\ge0\), a Farkas infeasibility certificate is a vector \(y\in\mathbb{Q}^m\) satisfying \(y\ge0\), \(A_v^Ty\le0\), and \(b_v^Ty>0\). Exact verification of these conditions certifies that the linear relaxation, and every integer-feasible node domain contained in it, is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative multiplier with nonpositive combined coefficients and a positive combined right-hand side certifies infeasibility of the node linear system.
assumptions_latex: \(A_v\in\mathbb{Q}^{m\times n}\) and \(b_v\in\mathbb{Q}^m\).
The node relaxation is represented in the displayed inequality form.

children.title: Local-Domain Bound Certificates

knowledge_statements.title: Local-Domain Bound Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual bound explicitly conditioned on node-local domain constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let node \(v\) have relaxation \(R_v=\{x\ge0:Ax\ge b,\ G_vx\ge h_v\}\), where \(G_vx\ge h_v\) records its local domain restrictions. A local-domain bound certificate consists of multipliers \(y\ge0\) and \(s\ge0\) satisfying \(A^Ty+G_v^Ts\le c\). It certifies \(c^Tx\ge b^Ty+h_v^Ts=:L_v\) for every \(x\in R_v\). The bound may be used only at \(v\) or descendants whose domains imply the same local restrictions; it is not a root bound unless those restrictions are globally valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local bound combines global and node-specific constraints by dual multipliers and remains valid only where all recorded local assumptions hold.
assumptions_latex: All displayed coefficient data are rational.
The node relaxation minimizes \(c^Tx\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in R_v}c^Tx\ge L_v=b^Ty+h_v^Ts\).

children.title: Global-Bound Composition Certificates
children.top_down_role: Evidence composing node bounds and closed leaves into a global conclusion.

knowledge_statements.title: Global-Bound Composition Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite branch-and-bound tree certificate for a minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the integer-feasible set and let the leaf domains \(D_1,\ldots,D_q\) satisfy \(F\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^q D_i\). For every leaf, provide either a certificate that \(F\cap D_i=\varnothing\), or a certified bound \(f(x)\ge L_i\) for every \(x\in F\cap D_i\). Then \(L=\min\{L_i:F\cap D_i\text{ is not certified empty}\}\), with \(L=+\infty\) when all leaves are empty, is a valid global lower bound. If a feasible incumbent \(\bar x\in F\) has value \(U=f(\bar x)\) and \(L\ge U\), the composed certificate establishes global optimality of \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Leaf coverage plus a valid lower bound or infeasibility certificate at every leaf yields a global bound; matching a feasible incumbent certifies optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\bigcup_{i=1}^q D_i\)
Each leaf certificate is valid on its stated domain.
\(q<\infty\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f(x)\ge L\) for all \(x\in F\), and \(L\ge f(\bar x)\) certifies that \(\bar x\) is optimal.

notation.meaning: certified lower bound at leaf i
objective value of the feasible incumbent

children.title: Linear-Combination Derivation Trails

knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Combination Derivation Trails
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Syntactic audit trail for inequalities derived by nonnegative linear combination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the available inequalities are \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\ge b_i\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\). A linear-combination derivation trail for \(a^{\mathsf T}x\ge b\) records rational coefficients \(\lambda_i\ge0\), references each used inequality, and verifies \(a=\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i a_i\) and \(b\le\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i b_i\). The recorded identities certify that every point satisfying the referenced inequalities satisfies the derived inequality. Equality premises may be represented by two opposite inequalities or by unrestricted multipliers under an explicitly declared equality rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trail certifies a derived inequality by listing referenced premises and nonnegative rational coefficients whose exact weighted sum dominates the claimed right-hand side.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\ge b_i\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\)
\(\lambda_i\in\mathbb Q_{\ge0}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_i^{\mathsf T}x\ge b_i\ \forall i\Longrightarrow a^{\mathsf T}x\ge b\).

children.title: Dual-Multiplier Derivation Trails

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Multiplier Derivation Trails
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact dual certificate for implication by a rational linear system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the system \(Ax\ge b\), a dual-multiplier trail certifying \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}x\ge\beta\) consists of \(y\in\mathbb Q^m\) satisfying \(y\ge0\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y=\alpha\), and \(b^{\mathsf T}y\ge\beta\). A checker verifies these relations exactly against the cited rows of \((A,b)\). Consequently, every \(x\) satisfying \(Ax\ge b\) obeys \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}x=(A^{\mathsf T}y)^{\mathsf T}x=y^{\mathsf T}Ax\ge y^{\mathsf T}b\ge\beta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative dual vector certifies an inequality when its exact row aggregation gives the claimed coefficients and at least the claimed right-hand side.
assumptions_latex: \(Ax\ge b\)
\(y\in\mathbb Q^m_{\ge0}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A^{\mathsf T}y=\alpha\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y\ge\beta\) imply \(Ax\ge b\Longrightarrow\alpha^{\mathsf T}x\ge\beta\).

children.title: Derivation Translation Interface
children.top_down_role: Correspondence between linear-combination records and dual evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Derivation Translation Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact correspondence between row-combination trails and sparse dual multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Index the available inequalities as the rows of \(Ax\ge b\). A linear-combination trail containing coefficients \((\lambda_i)_{i=1}^m\) translates to the dual vector \(y=(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_m)\), with omitted rows assigned coefficient zero. Conversely, a rational dual vector \(y\ge0\) translates to a trail listing every row with \(y_i\ne0\). Under exact row identifiers and coefficient arithmetic, the two representations certify the same aggregate: \(A^{\mathsf T}y=\sum_i y_i a_i\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y=\sum_i y_i b_i\). Translation preserves validity precisely when signs, row orientation, and equality-row conventions are preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coefficient list and a sparse dual vector are equivalent certificate representations when row identities, signs, orientations, and exact rational values are preserved.
assumptions_latex: Rows of \(Ax\ge b\) have stable identifiers.
All translated coefficients are exact rationals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y_i=\lambda_i\) yields identical aggregated left- and right-hand sides in both representations.

children.title: Audit Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Missing or incompatible evidence that prevents independent checking.

knowledge_statements.title: Audit Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions under which a linear-dual derivation audit cannot establish validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Exact audit validity fails if a referenced row is missing or reoriented, a required multiplier is negative, or either identity \(A^{\mathsf T}y=\alpha\) or inequality \(b^{\mathsf T}y\ge\beta\) is checked only after tolerance-based coefficient deletion. Concretely, for any \(\varepsilon>0\), the feasible premise \(\varepsilon x\ge1\) does not imply \(0\ge1\). A checker that treats the coefficient \(\varepsilon\) as zero may nevertheless confuse the premise with the false constant inequality. Thus approximate row matching or arithmetic is insufficient for an exact validity certificate unless accompanied by a separately proved error enclosure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Missing rows, wrong orientations, negative multipliers, or tolerance-based coefficient deletion invalidate exact audits; small discarded coefficients can turn feasible premises into false constant claims.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon>0\)
The audit is intended to certify exact logical implication.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Tolerance-based equality alone does not certify \(Ax\ge b\Longrightarrow\alpha^{\mathsf T}x\ge\beta\).

notation.meaning: positive coefficient small enough to be discarded by a tolerant checker

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the displayed family directly witnesses failure of tolerance-based coefficient deletion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, but the tolerant-deletion example does not fully specify a checker acceptance path demonstrating an unsound certificate. A proof-audit source and a precise failure model are required.

children.title: Integer-Rounding Derivations

knowledge_statements.title: Integer-Rounding Derivations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chvátal–Gomory audit record for a pure-integer linear system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb Z^n\) satisfy \(Ax\le b\), where \(A\in\mathbb Q^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb Q^m\). An integer-rounding derivation records \(\lambda\in\mathbb Q^m_{\ge0}\) such that \(c^{\mathsf T}=\lambda^{\mathsf T}A\in\mathbb Z^n\), and claims \(c^{\mathsf T}x\le\lfloor\lambda^{\mathsf T}b\rfloor\). Exact verification of nonnegativity, aggregation, integrality of \(c\), and the floor value certifies the claim, because \(c^{\mathsf T}x\) is integral and is at most \(\lambda^{\mathsf T}b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Chvátal–Gomory trail records a nonnegative row aggregation with integral left coefficients and rounds its right-hand side down exactly.
assumptions_latex: \(x\in\mathbb Z^n\) and \(Ax\le b\)
\(\lambda\in\mathbb Q^m_{\ge0}\)
\(\lambda^{\mathsf T}A\in\mathbb Z^n\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((\lambda^{\mathsf T}A)x\le\lfloor\lambda^{\mathsf T}b\rfloor\).

children.title: Disjunctive Derivations

knowledge_statements.title: Disjunctive Derivations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branchwise validity certificate composed through a finite certified disjunction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq P_1\cup\cdots\cup P_k\) be certified, where each \(P_j\) is a branch domain. A disjunctive derivation of \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}x\ge\beta\) records, for every \(j\), a valid branch certificate establishing \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}x\ge\beta\) for all \(x\in F\cap P_j\). The audit verifies both the covering disjunction and every branch certificate. Since each \(x\in F\) belongs to at least one \(P_j\), the common inequality is valid on \(F\). Empty branches may instead carry independently checkable infeasibility certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut is certified disjunctively when a verified disjunction covers the feasible set and every branch proves the same cut or is certified empty.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq\bigcup_{j=1}^k P_j\)
Each branch certificate is valid on \(F\cap P_j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}x\ge\beta\) for every \(x\in F\).

children.title: Local-Scope Derivations

knowledge_statements.title: Local-Scope Derivations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity certificate parameterized by inherited branch assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a search node \(v\), let \(D_v\) be the domain defined by all branch assumptions inherited along the root-to-\(v\) path. A local derivation certificate for \(g(x)\ge0\) records those assumptions, their node identifiers, and a valid derivation of \(g(x)\ge0\) from the global model together with \(x\in D_v\). The certificate establishes validity only on \(F\cap D_v\). It may be inherited by a descendant \(w\) after verifying \(D_w\subseteq D_v\), but it cannot be exported to an unrelated node or the root without a separate global derivation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local derivation is valid only under its recorded ancestral branch assumptions and passes to descendants whose domains are contained in the certified scope.

The derivation is valid from the global model and \(x\in D_v\).
