children.title: Local-Cut Scope Leakage
children.top_down_role: Use of locally valid cuts outside their certified subtrees.

knowledge_statements.title: Local-Cut Scope Leakage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local validity is inherited by domains contained in the certified scope; applying the cut elsewhere requires a separate validity argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be the integer-feasible set of the original problem. A cut \(a^\top x\leq b\) certified at node \(u\) is locally valid when \(a^\top x\leq b\) for every \(x\in F\cap D_u\). It may be imposed at a node \(v\) without a new validity argument when \(D_v\subseteq D_u\). Scope leakage occurs when the cut is imposed at some \(v\) with \(D_v\nsubseteq D_u\) despite lacking a validity certificate for \(F\cap D_v\). If there exists \(\bar x\in F\cap D_v\) such that \(a^\top\bar x>b\), the cut invalidly excludes \(\bar x\) from node \(v\). If no other live node has a domain containing \(\bar x\), the search loses an original feasible solution and cannot support an exhaustive-search correctness claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut certified only within one node's domain is leaked when used outside that scope without a new validity argument. If it excludes an original feasible point that survives in no other live node, the search is no longer exhaustive.
assumptions_latex: A branch-and-cut node \(u\) represents a certified domain \(D_u\), and every descendant \(v\) satisfies \(D_v\subseteq D_u\).
A local cut \(a^\top x\leq b\) is certified only for integer-feasible points in \(D_u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Applying the cut outside \(D_u\) can invalidly exclude a point from a node; it removes that point from the entire live search when no other live node contains it.

notation.meaning: domain associated with search-tree node u

children.title: Presolve Transformation Failures
children.top_down_role: Loss of validity or checkability across model transformations.

children.title: Forward Mapping Failures
children.top_down_role: Invalid transfer of model objects into presolved representations.

assumptions_latex: A presolve transformation maps an original feasible set \(F\) to a reduced feasible set \(F'\) through a claimed map \(T\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Forward mapping fails exactly when some \(x\in F\) is mapped outside \(F'\) or is left without a defined reduced image.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: forward equivalence of presolve requires every original feasible point to have a feasible reduced image
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of feasibility preservation from the original formulation to the presolved formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A forward presolve map is feasibility preserving when \(T\) is defined on all of \(F\) and \(T(F)\subseteq F'\). Forward mapping failure occurs if there exists \(x\in F\) for which either \(T(x)\) is undefined or \(T(x)\notin F'\). For an objective pair \(c,c'\), objective-preserving forward reduction additionally requires a known constant \(\kappa\) satisfying \(c^\top x=c'^\top T(x)+\kappa\) for every \(x\in F\). Failure of this equality can corrupt objective comparisons even when feasibility is preserved.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Presolve fails forward when an original feasible point has no reduced image, maps to an infeasible reduced point, or receives an inconsistent objective value.
knowledge_statements.title: Forward Mapping Failures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is coherent for a fully solution-preserving reduction, but presolve may preserve only feasibility, optimal solutions, or objective values under different mappings. A dedicated source is needed to establish the intended presolve-equivalence variant and objective correspondence.

children.title: Inverse Recovery Failures
children.top_down_role: Invalid recovery of transformed objects in the original representation.

assumptions_latex: A reduced feasible set \(F'\) is intended to represent an original feasible set \(F\).
A claimed recovery map \(R\) reconstructs original variables from reduced solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Inverse recovery fails when some \(y\in F'\) has no reconstructible point \(R(y)\in F\), or the reconstructed objective relation is wrong.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: solution-preserving presolve requires reconstruction of every accepted reduced solution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of feasible-solution reconstruction from reduced variables back to the original formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Inverse recovery is valid when \(R\) is defined for every \(y\in F'\), satisfies \(R(y)\in F\), and, for objectives \(c,c'\), obeys \(c^\top R(y)=c'^\top y+\kappa\) for a recorded constant \(\kappa\). Recovery failure occurs if some \(y\in F'\) makes \(R(y)\) undefined, yields \(R(y)\notin F\), or violates the objective identity. Consequently, a reduced feasible or optimal solution need not produce a feasible or correspondingly optimal solution of the original problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inverse recovery fails when a reduced solution cannot be reconstructed as an original feasible solution with the recorded objective correspondence.
knowledge_statements.title: Inverse Recovery Failures

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The recovery conditions are plausible, but the claim that every reduced feasible point must admit recovery depends on the selected notion of presolve equivalence. A presolve source must support this quantification and the constant-shift objective identity.

children.title: Transformation-Provenance Gaps
children.top_down_role: Missing transformation records needed to establish validity.

assumptions_latex: Presolve applies transformations \(T_1,\ldots,T_k\) before search or certificate production.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A provenance gap exists when the data needed to verify or invert \(T_k\circ\cdots\circ T_1\) are absent or inconsistent.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: reproducible presolve requires an ordered transformation record with parameters and reconstruction data
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Missing records that prevent validation or reversal of a presolve transformation sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each presolve step \(T_i\), let \(P_i\) record its input identifiers, output identifiers, numerical parameters, justification, and recovery data. Transformation provenance is complete when the ordered collection \((T_i,P_i)_{i=1}^k\) determines the composite map \(T_k\circ\cdots\circ T_1\), permits every claimed implication to be checked, and supplies each inverse reconstruction required for retained solutions. A provenance gap occurs when any such record is missing, ambiguous, reordered, or inconsistent, so that equivalence of the original and reduced formulations cannot be independently established.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Presolve provenance is incomplete when missing or inconsistent transformation records prevent checking the reduction or reconstructing original solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Transformation-Provenance Gaps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the proposed mandatory provenance fields or the assertion that each missing, reordered, or ambiguous record prevents independent equivalence verification.

children.title: Certificate Checkability Loss
children.top_down_role: Loss of independently checkable evidence across model transformations.

assumptions_latex: A certificate \(z'\) is produced for a reduced formulation obtained by presolve.
Certificate validity for the original formulation is intended to follow by recorded transformations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Checkability is lost when no finite recorded derivation maps \(z'\) to an original-space certificate whose predicates can be evaluated from the original input.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a certificate is independently checkable only when its verification predicates and transformation back to the original instance are available
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of an independently evaluable certificate after presolve changes variables or constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be the original instance and let \(V(I,z)\) be a decidable predicate validating an original-space certificate \(z\). A reduced certificate \(z'\) remains checkable when recorded presolve data determine a finite reconstruction \(z=R_c(z')\) and all quantities needed to evaluate \(V(I,z)\). Certificate checkability is lost if \(R_c(z')\) is undefined or underdetermined, or if validation depends on discarded rows, substitutions, bounds, multipliers, or rounding decisions that were not recorded. In that case, acceptance of \(z'\) does not independently certify the claimed property of \(I\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduced certificate becomes uncheckable when missing presolve records prevent reconstructing and evaluating a certificate against the original instance.
knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Checkability Loss

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The abstract verification-predicate formulation is internally consistent and fits the leaf, but the required reconstruction data and listed failure modes need a dedicated presolve-certificate source.

children.title: Violation Classification Failures
children.top_down_role: Tolerance-sensitive misclassification during separation.

children.title: False Violation Detection
children.top_down_role: Numerical classification of a satisfied inequality as violated.

assumptions_latex: An inequality \(a^\top x\leq b\) is tested at a computed point \(\hat x\).
The implementation declares violation when the computed residual exceeds a threshold \(\tau\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: False violation detection occurs when \(\widehat r>\tau\) but the exact residual \(r\leq0\).
review_flags: numerical-error treatment not explicit in provisional locator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A numerical classifier reports violation although the exact inequality is satisfied.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the inequality \(a^\top x\leq b\), define the exact residual at \(\hat x\) by \(r=a^\top\hat x-b\) and the computed residual by \(\widehat r=\operatorname{fl}(a^\top\hat x-b)\). Under the rule declaring violation precisely when \(\widehat r>\tau\), a false violation is the event \(r\leq0\) and \(\widehat r>\tau\). If a certified error bound \(|\widehat r-r|\leq\eta\) is available, false detection is excluded whenever the rule requires \(\widehat r>\eta\); using \(\tau<\eta\) leaves a nonempty uncertainty region.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A false violation is reported when the computed residual exceeds the test threshold even though the exact inequality residual is nonpositive.
knowledge_statements.title: False Violation Detection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The false-detection event is mathematically precise, but the cited branch-and-cut section is not shown to support the floating-point residual model or the certified-error-bound consequence. A numerical-analysis locator is required.

children.title: Missed Violation Detection
children.top_down_role: Numerical failure to recognize a materially violated inequality.

assumptions_latex: An inequality \(a^\top x\leq b\) is tested at a computed point \(\hat x\).
The implementation declares violation only when the computed residual exceeds \(\tau\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Missed violation detection occurs when the exact residual \(r>0\) but the computed residual \(\widehat r\leq\tau\).
review_flags: numerical-error treatment not explicit in provisional locator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A numerical classifier accepts an inequality although its exact residual is positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the inequality \(a^\top x\leq b\), let \(r=a^\top\hat x-b\) be the exact residual and \(\widehat r=\operatorname{fl}(a^\top\hat x-b)\) its computed value. Under the rule declaring violation precisely when \(\widehat r>\tau\), a missed violation is the event \(r>0\) and \(\widehat r\leq\tau\). If \(|\widehat r-r|\leq\eta\), every point with \(r>\tau+\eta\) is detected, whereas violations satisfying \(0<r\leq\tau+\eta\) may remain unreported.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A violation is missed when the exact residual is positive but its computed value does not exceed the classifier's threshold.
knowledge_statements.title: Missed Violation Detection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The missed-detection event and the bound r>tau+eta are internally correct, but the supplied locator does not establish the floating-point error model. A supporting numerical-analysis source is required.

children.title: Tolerance Ambiguity
children.top_down_role: Borderline violation status created by finite-precision tolerances.

assumptions_latex: A computed residual \(\widehat r\) approximates an exact residual \(r\) with \(|\widehat r-r|\leq\eta\).
Feasibility is intended to mean \(r\leq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When \(|\widehat r-\tau|\leq\eta\), the exact sign relative to \(\tau\) cannot be inferred from \(\widehat r\) alone.

notation.meaning: exact residual, computed residual, and certified error radius

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: interval error bounds yield a three-way residual classification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The residual error interval intersects the chosen feasibility boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(|\widehat r-r|\leq\eta\), the exact residual lies in \([\widehat r-\eta,\widehat r+\eta]\). Relative to a threshold \(\tau\), classification is certified as nonviolation if \(\widehat r+\eta\leq\tau\), certified as violation if \(\widehat r-\eta>\tau\), and ambiguous otherwise. Thus the ambiguity condition is \(\widehat r-\eta\leq\tau<\widehat r+\eta\). A binary rule that assigns every ambiguous residual to either class necessarily permits false or missed classifications unless additional exact arithmetic or sharper error information is obtained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A residual classification is ambiguous when its certified error interval crosses the chosen threshold, so the computed value alone cannot determine the exact class.
knowledge_statements.title: Tolerance Ambiguity

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact ambiguity condition is rhat-eta <= tau < rhat+eta, not |rhat-tau| <= eta as stated in the conclusion: equality at rhat+eta=tau is certified nonviolation. A source is also required for the numerical classification model.

children.title: Separation Consequences
children.top_down_role: Correctness or progress effects of violation misclassification.

knowledge_statements.title: Separation Consequences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: How violation-classification errors affect a cutting-plane update.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be the current relaxation and let \(a^\top x\leq b\) be a candidate inequality valid for every feasible point in the node's certified scope. If the separator reports a violation, the update is \(P'=P\cap\{x:a^\top x\leq b\}\). A false violation report may therefore insert an inequality that does not separate the exact current point, causing an unnecessary update but not excluding a feasible point under the validity assumption. Exclusion of feasible points requires a separate error in the inequality's validity or scope. A missed violation report leaves \(P'=P\), so the available relaxation strengthening is omitted. Repeated missed reports can prevent progress based on that separator, although they do not themselves invalidate feasible points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A false violation report can add a valid inequality that does not actually separate the current point, while a missed report suppresses available relaxation strengthening. Loss of feasible points requires a separate validity or scope error.
assumptions_latex: A separator adds an inequality only after classifying the current point as violating it.
The inequality is valid for every feasible point in the node's certified scope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A false classification can cause a valid but nonseparating cut insertion, while a missed classification can leave the current relaxation unchanged; neither alone excludes feasible points when cut validity and scope are correct.

notation.meaning: current relaxation and its updated version

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

children.title: Bound-Pruning Correctness Failures
children.top_down_role: Propagation of numerical error into search-tree closure decisions.

children.title: Bound Misestimation
children.top_down_role: Numerically unsound node or objective bound values.

assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem, and node \(u\) has true relaxation bound \(L_u\).
The solver uses a computed bound \(\widehat L_u\) for pruning and global-bound updates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Underestimation weakens pruning, whereas overestimation can make pruning invalid by exceeding the best objective attainable in the node.

notation.meaning: true and computed lower bounds at node u
optimal integer objective attainable in node u

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direction-sensitive consequences of an erroneous node lower bound in minimization.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization node \(u\), a valid lower bound satisfies \(L_u\leq z_u^*\), where \(z_u^*\) is the best integer objective attainable in that node. Bound misestimation is the use of \(\widehat L_u\neq L_u\). If \(\widehat L_u<L_u\), pruning may be delayed but validity is retained provided \(\widehat L_u\leq z_u^*\). If \(\widehat L_u>z_u^*\), the computed value is not a valid lower bound and can justify elimination of a node containing an improving solution. The analogous inequalities reverse for maximization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For minimization, an underestimated lower bound wastes search, while an overestimate above the node optimum can wrongly eliminate improving solutions.
knowledge_statements.title: Bound Misestimation

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

children.title: Premature Node Pruning
children.top_down_role: Search-node closure caused by unreliable bound comparisons.

assumptions_latex: The problem is minimized with incumbent value \(U\).
Node \(u\) is pruned by bound when the solver's computed lower bound satisfies \(\widehat L_u\geq U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pruning is premature if \(z_u^*<U\leq\widehat L_u\), because node \(u\) contains a solution improving the incumbent.

notation.meaning: computed node lower bound and true node optimum

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incorrect bound pruning in a minimization branch-and-bound tree.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In minimization, bound pruning of node \(u\) is valid when a certified lower bound \(L_u\) satisfies \(L_u\geq U\), where \(U\) is the objective of the incumbent. If pruning instead uses \(\widehat L_u\), it is premature precisely when the node contains an improving feasible solution, equivalently when \(z_u^*<U\), while \(\widehat L_u\geq U\). The combined condition \(z_u^*<U\leq\widehat L_u\) shows that the discarded subtree can contain a better solution and therefore invalidates any optimality conclusion based on exhaustion of the remaining tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node is pruned prematurely when its computed bound meets the incumbent even though the subtree contains a strictly better feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Premature Node Pruning

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

children.title: Global-Gap Corruption
children.top_down_role: Distortion of global progress measures by incorrect bounds.

assumptions_latex: For minimization, \(L_u\) is a valid lower bound for every active node \(u\) in the set \(A\).
The incumbent value \(U\) is finite and comes from a feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing any \(L_u\) by an invalid overestimate can raise the reported global lower bound and understate or reverse the reported optimality gap.

notation.meaning: active-node set and valid global lower bound

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Corruption of the global dual bound and reported minimization gap by erroneous node bounds.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization search with active nodes \(A\), the valid global lower bound is \(L=\min_{u\in A}L_u\), and the absolute primal-dual gap is \(G=U-L\). If computed bounds are used, the solver reports \(\widehat L=\min_{u\in A}\widehat L_u\) and \(\widehat G=U-\widehat L\). Global-gap corruption occurs when \(\widehat L\) is not a valid lower bound on the unexplored search space. In particular, invalid overestimates can produce \(\widehat L>L\), hence \(\widehat G<G\), and may yield a false zero-gap or optimality declaration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invalidly high node bounds can inflate the global lower bound, shrink the reported gap, and produce a false optimality declaration.
knowledge_statements.title: Global-Gap Corruption

source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

children.title: Search Correctness Failure
children.top_down_role: Loss of valid search conclusions after unsound pruning.

knowledge_statements.title: Search Correctness Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incorrect bound-based pruning in a minimization branch-and-cut search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing \(c^\top x\) over \(F\), with incumbent value \(U\) and an active node region \(R\). Let \(z(R)=\inf\{c^\top x:x\in F\cap R\}\). A search correctness failure occurs if the algorithm reports a lower bound \(\widehat L(R)>U\) and consequently prunes \(R\), although \(z(R)<U\). If \(R\) contains every globally optimal solution still represented by the active search tree, this pruning destroys the tree-cover invariant: subsequent termination can return the incumbent with \(U>z^*\), where \(z^*=\inf\{c^\top x:x\in F\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node containing all remaining optimal solutions is wrongly pruned by an overestimated lower bound, allowing the search to return a strictly suboptimal incumbent.
assumptions_latex: \(F\neq\varnothing\) and \(z^*>-\infty\).
\(U\) is the objective value of a feasible incumbent.
Before pruning, active node regions cover every feasible point not validly excluded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat L(R)>U>z(R)\) permits invalid pruning and may yield \(U>z^*\) at termination.

notation.meaning: feasible region represented by the node being considered for pruning
lower bound reported by the solver for node region R

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports this precise pruning-failure formulation.
Exact source and terminology require editorial validation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits the exact leaf. The invalid-pruning mechanism is mathematically plausible, but no source reference or inspectable locator supports this formulation. In addition, the condition referring to globally optimal solutions presupposes attainment, whereas the assumptions only impose a finite infimum. Source-backed clarification of the intended tree-cover and attainment conditions is required before the statement can be reviewed reliably.

children.title: Search-Balance Failures
children.top_down_role: Poor allocation of effort among separation, branching, reoptimization, and primal search.

children.title: Root Overcutting
children.top_down_role: Excessive root separation that delays useful enumeration.

knowledge_statements.title: Root Overcutting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational boundary for excessive separation before the first root branching decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At the root node, let \(z_i\) be the relaxation bound after cut round \(i\), and let \(s_i>0\) be that round's separation and reoptimization time. For tolerances \(\varepsilon\ge 0\) and \(\tau>0\), root overcutting occurs by round \(k\) when no child node has been created, \(\sum_{i=1}^{k}s_i\ge\tau\), and every completed round has marginal bound efficiency \((z_i-z_{i-1})/s_i\le\varepsilon\). Thus the policy consumes the prescribed root-time budget while producing only low-efficiency dual-bound improvement and postponing enumeration.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Root separation exceeds its time budget without branching, while every cut round produces at most a prescribed amount of bound improvement per unit time.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem, so stronger valid cuts cannot decrease the root relaxation bound.
Cut-round times \(s_i\) include separation and relaxation reoptimization.
\(\varepsilon\) and \(\tau\) are fixed before assessing the root policy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{i=1}^{k}s_i\ge\tau\), \(\max_{1\le i\le k}(z_i-z_{i-1})/s_i\le\varepsilon\), and no root child exists.

notation.meaning: root relaxation bound after cut round i
computational time consumed by cut round i

review_flags: The supplied sources do not establish this quantitative overcutting threshold.
Operational criterion requires source support or calibration convention.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind matches the Root Overcutting leaf, and the plain and LaTeX statements agree. However, the all-round efficiency threshold, root-time budget, and absence-of-branching criterion are a proposed operational definition rather than a standard consequence of the listed literature. No candidate citation supports or calibrates this exact boundary.

children.title: In-Tree Underseparation
children.top_down_role: Weak node bounds caused by overly conservative tree separation.

knowledge_statements.title: In-Tree Underseparation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure to apply an available pruning cut at a nonroot search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v\) be a nonroot node with relaxation bound \(z_v<U\), where \(U\) is the incumbent value. For each available valid cut \(q\in\mathcal Q_v\), let \(z_v(q)\) denote the bound after adding \(q\) and reoptimizing. In-tree underseparation occurs when \(\max_{q\in\mathcal Q_v}z_v(q)\ge U\), but the separation policy adds no such cut and branches from \(v\). A cut already available to the separator could therefore have certified pruning, whereas conservative separation leaves the weaker bound \(z_v\) and creates avoidable descendants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonroot node is branched even though an available valid cut would raise its bound to the incumbent and certify pruning.
assumptions_latex: The problem is minimized and \(U\) is a feasible incumbent value.
Every \(q\in\mathcal Q_v\) is valid for all integer-feasible points in node \(v\).
The node relaxation is solved sufficiently accurately to compare its bound with \(U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_v<U\le\max_{q\in\mathcal Q_v}z_v(q)\), yet the policy branches without applying a pruning cut.

notation.meaning: valid cuts available to the node separator
node relaxation bound after adding cut q

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the available-pruning-cut criterion.
A source connecting node separation and avoidable branching is required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits the In-Tree Underseparation leaf. The criterion is coherent under an exact interpretation of cut availability, but no source supports the claim that this counterfactual pruning condition is the relevant boundary. The meaning of an available cut also requires a source-backed operational convention, including whether availability accounts for cut selection, numerical tolerances, and simultaneous cuts.

children.title: Incumbent Starvation
children.top_down_role: Strong dual-bound effort without adequate primal progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Starvation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon imbalance between dual-bound work and primal incumbent generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a computation horizon \(T>0\) and a primal-work fraction \(\rho\in[0,1)\). Let \(D_T\) and \(P_T\) be time spent by horizon \(T\) on bound strengthening and incumbent-producing procedures, respectively. Incumbent starvation occurs when \(D_T/T\ge 1-\rho\), \(P_T/T\le\rho\), the global lower bound satisfies \(L_T>L_0\), and the incumbent remains \(U_T=+\infty\) despite \(F\neq\varnothing\). The search has made measurable dual progress but has devoted too little of the prescribed budget to obtaining any primal certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: By a fixed horizon, most effort improves the dual bound while little supports primal search, and no incumbent exists although the problem is feasible.
assumptions_latex: The problem is minimized and has a nonempty feasible set \(F\).
Algorithmic time is partitioned consistently into dual and primal work.
No incumbent is represented by the convention \(U_T=+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_T/T\ge1-\rho\), \(P_T/T\le\rho\), \(L_T>L_0\), and \(U_T=+\infty\).

notation.meaning: time spent strengthening or proving dual bounds by horizon T
time spent on procedures intended to produce incumbents by horizon T
global lower and incumbent upper bounds at horizon T

review_flags: The supplied locators do not support this finite-horizon starvation criterion.
The primal-versus-dual work accounting convention requires a source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind is appropriate for Incumbent Starvation, and the mathematical and plain statements are consistent. The finite-horizon time fractions and strict dual-progress requirement constitute a bespoke quantitative definition. No source establishes the primal-versus-dual time partition or the threshold parameter rho, so the exact criterion cannot yet be relied upon.

children.title: Branching–Cutting Policy Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Branching and separation policies that work at cross-purposes.

knowledge_statements.title: Branching–Cutting Policy Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterfactual criterion for destructive interaction between branching and cutting decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a fixed node and computational budget, let \(P_0\) be a scalar progress score with neither action, and let \(P_B\), \(P_C\), and \(P_{BC}\) be the scores under branching alone, cutting alone, and the combined policy. For \(\eta>0\), a branching–cutting policy mismatch occurs when both isolated actions improve progress, \(P_B>P_0\) and \(P_C>P_0\), but \(P_{BC}\le\max\{P_B,P_C\}\) and the interaction loss \((P_B-P_0)+(P_C-P_0)-(P_{BC}-P_0)\) is at least \(\eta\). The combined policy then fails to realize either additive or strictly superior progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branching and cutting each help separately, but their combined policy performs no better than the stronger isolated action and loses substantial expected progress through interaction.
assumptions_latex: All four scores use the same node state, computational budget, and progress metric.
Larger values of the progress score are preferable.
\(\eta>0\) is fixed before comparing the policies.

notation.meaning: counterfactual progress scores for branching, cutting, and their combination

review_flags: No supplied locator establishes this counterfactual interaction definition.
The progress metric and materiality threshold require domain-specific sourcing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure_boundary kind fits the Branching–Cutting Policy Mismatch leaf. The algebra is internally consistent, but the scalar progress score, matched counterfactual experiments, and interaction-loss threshold define a nonstandard diagnostic boundary. No source supports this formulation or specifies a progress metric for which the comparisons are meaningful.
